```json
          {
            "text": "# --- START: NEW HYBRID BME/MCP FUNCTION ---",
            "lineNumber": 2260
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2261
          },
          {
            "text": "def HBMEcatPdf(ck,cs,ps,dmodel,Pmodel,nsmax,dmax,options = None):",
            "lineNumber": 2262,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2263
          },
          {
            "text": "    Performs Hybrid BME (HBME) categorical data prediction.",
            "lineNumber": 2264
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 2265
          },
          {
            "text": "    This function implements a two-step hybrid approach:",
            "lineNumber": 2266
          },
          {
            "text": "    1. **Regional prior (MCP step):** Run &#96;MCPcatPdf&#96; with up to &#96;nsmax_total&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2267
          },
          {
            "text": "       neighbours, restricted to &#96;dmax_mcp&#96;, to build a spatially varying",
            "lineNumber": 2268
          },
          {
            "text": "       prior that captures the regional trend.",
            "lineNumber": 2269
          },
          {
            "text": "    2. **Local update (BME step):** Run &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; with the &#96;nsmax&#96; *closest*",
            "lineNumber": 2270
          },
          {
            "text": "       neighbours and &#96;model_structure='full'&#96; to rigorously update the prior,",
            "lineNumber": 2271
          },
          {
            "text": "       correctly accounting for local spatial redundancy.",
            "lineNumber": 2272
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2273
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 2274
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 2275
          },
          {
            "text": "    ck : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2276
          },
          {
            "text": "        Estimation point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, d)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2277
          },
          {
            "text": "    cs : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2278
          },
          {
            "text": "        Data point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(n, d)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2279
          },
          {
            "text": "    ps : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2280
          },
          {
            "text": "        Soft data (PDFs) at data points, shape &#96;&#96;(n, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2281
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2282
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of distances for &#96;Pmodel&#96;, shape &#96;&#96;(nd,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2283
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2284
          },
          {
            "text": "        3D array of bivariate probability tables, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, nc, nd)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2285
          },
          {
            "text": "    nsmax : int",
            "lineNumber": 2286
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of *closest* neighbours for the final BME update step.",
            "lineNumber": 2287
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmax : float",
            "lineNumber": 2288
          },
          {
            "text": "        Maximum search distance for the BME update step (Step 2).",
            "lineNumber": 2289
          },
          {
            "text": "    options : dict, optional",
            "lineNumber": 2290
          },
          {
            "text": "        Dictionary of options:",
            "lineNumber": 2291
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2292
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'nsmax_total'&#96;&#96; (int): Maximum number of neighbours for the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2293
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior step (Step 1). Default &#96;&#96;20&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2294
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2295
          },
          {
            "text": "          .. warning::",
            "lineNumber": 2296
          },
          {
            "text": "             This must be kept **small** (typically 10–25).  At distances",
            "lineNumber": 2297
          },
          {
            "text": "             beyond the covariance correlation range the bivariate table",
            "lineNumber": 2298
          },
          {
            "text": "             factorises to the independence product P(c')·P(c), so each",
            "lineNumber": 2299
          },
          {
            "text": "             out-of-range neighbour contributes &#96;&#96;log P(c)&#96;&#96; to the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2300
          },
          {
            "text": "             log-posterior.  With n decorrelated neighbours the MCP result",
            "lineNumber": 2301
          },
          {
            "text": "             degenerates to the global marginal distribution **P(c), the",
            "lineNumber": 2302
          },
          {
            "text": "             same at every estimation point**, eliminating all spatial",
            "lineNumber": 2303
          },
          {
            "text": "             variation from the prior and making the final HBME map nearly",
            "lineNumber": 2304
          },
          {
            "text": "             flat.  A good starting value is &#96;&#96;nsmax_total ≈ 2–3 × nsmax&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2305
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2306
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (float): Maximum search radius for the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2307
          },
          {
            "text": "          step.  Defaults to &#96;&#96;dmax&#96;&#96;.  **Setting this to the covariance",
            "lineNumber": 2308
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlation range is strongly recommended** so that only spatially",
            "lineNumber": 2309
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlated neighbours contribute to the prior.  Ignored when",
            "lineNumber": 2310
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; is &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2311
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2312
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; is",
            "lineNumber": 2313
          },
          {
            "text": "          **determined automatically** from &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96; and &#96;&#96;Pmodel&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2314
          },
          {
            "text": "          using :func:&#96;_find_effective_range&#96; with the threshold given",
            "lineNumber": 2315
          },
          {
            "text": "          by &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96;.  This ensures the MCP ring radius",
            "lineNumber": 2316
          },
          {
            "text": "          equals the effective decorrelation distance in the bivariate",
            "lineNumber": 2317
          },
          {
            "text": "          model, preventing out-of-range data from contaminating the",
            "lineNumber": 2318
          },
          {
            "text": "          MCP prior.  Default &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2319
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2320
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96; (float): Decorrelation threshold",
            "lineNumber": 2321
          },
          {
            "text": "          for the automatic range detection.  The range is the distance",
            "lineNumber": 2322
          },
          {
            "text": "          at which the normalised total variation between &#96;&#96;Pmodel&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2323
          },
          {
            "text": "          the independence product &#96;&#96;p(c)*p(c')&#96;&#96; drops below this",
            "lineNumber": 2324
          },
          {
            "text": "          fraction.  Default &#96;&#96;0.05&#96;&#96; (5 %).",
            "lineNumber": 2325
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2326
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'use_annular_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96; (default), the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2327
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior is computed using only data in the **ring**",
            "lineNumber": 2328
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;dmax &lt; r &lt;= dmax_mcp&#96;&#96;, i.e. data that lie *outside* the local",
            "lineNumber": 2329
          },
          {
            "text": "          BME update zone.  This gives strict data independence between the",
            "lineNumber": 2330
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior step and the likelihood step (no data leakage).  If",
            "lineNumber": 2331
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96;, MCP uses all data within &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; (original",
            "lineNumber": 2332
          },
          {
            "text": "          behaviour, slightly faster but reuses data).",
            "lineNumber": 2333
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2334
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'global_marginal'&#96;&#96; (np.ndarray, shape &#96;&#96;(nc,)&#96;&#96;): Empirical",
            "lineNumber": 2335
          },
          {
            "text": "          category frequencies &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96;.  When provided, the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2336
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; is passed to BMEcatPdf together with &#96;&#96;global_marginal&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2337
          },
          {
            "text": "          so that the Bayes-factor correction &#96;&#96;q(c)/p(c)&#96;&#96; is applied",
            "lineNumber": 2338
          },
          {
            "text": "          automatically, preventing double-counting of the global",
            "lineNumber": 2339
          },
          {
            "text": "          marginal.  If not provided, &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; is estimated automatically",
            "lineNumber": 2340
          },
          {
            "text": "          from &#96;&#96;ps.mean(axis=0)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2341
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2342
          },
          {
            "text": "        - All other options (e.g., &#96;&#96;'tol'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'reg'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'estimator'&#96;&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 2343
          },
          {
            "text": "          are forwarded to the final &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; update step.",
            "lineNumber": 2344
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'model_structure'&#96;&#96; is *ignored* for the BME step and forced to",
            "lineNumber": 2345
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'full'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2346
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2347
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 2348
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 2349
          },
          {
            "text": "    pk : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2350
          },
          {
            "text": "        The estimated posterior marginal PDFs, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2351
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2352
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 2353
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 2354
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Choosing nsmax_total and dmax_mcp:**",
            "lineNumber": 2355
          },
          {
            "text": "    Let r be the covariance correlation range.  Set &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp ≈ r&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2356
          },
          {
            "text": "    choose &#96;&#96;nsmax_total&#96;&#96; as the expected number of data points within that",
            "lineNumber": 2357
          },
          {
            "text": "    radius (typically 10–25 for datasets of 50–200 points).  Using too many",
            "lineNumber": 2358
          },
          {
            "text": "    decorrelated neighbours (beyond r) causes the MCP prior to converge to",
            "lineNumber": 2359
          },
          {
            "text": "    the global marginal P(c) at every location, destroying spatial variation.",
            "lineNumber": 2360
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2361
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Bayes-factor correction:**",
            "lineNumber": 2362
          },
          {
            "text": "    The Maximum Entropy table solved by &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; carries an implicit",
            "lineNumber": 2363
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; weight (the global marginal).  Passing the MCP result &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2364
          },
          {
            "text": "    directly as a prior therefore weights the final posterior by",
            "lineNumber": 2365
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;q(c) · p(c)&#96;&#96; rather than &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; alone — a subtle double-counting",
            "lineNumber": 2366
          },
          {
            "text": "    of the baseline frequency.  The Bayes-factor correction divides the",
            "lineNumber": 2367
          },
          {
            "text": "    supplied prior by &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; before entering &#96;&#96;producttablepdf&#96;&#96;, so the",
            "lineNumber": 2368
          },
          {
            "text": "    net effect is exactly &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;.  When no prior is given this correction",
            "lineNumber": 2369
          },
          {
            "text": "    is never triggered and the original BME behaviour is preserved.",
            "lineNumber": 2370
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2371
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 2372
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- 1. Setup Options ---",
            "lineNumber": 2373
          },
          {
            "text": "    if options is None:",
            "lineNumber": 2374
          },

          }

      "codeBlock": {

        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def MPLestimator(active_constraints, ndim, nc, tol):",
            "lineNumber": 898,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 899
          },
          {
            "text": "    Fits a MaxEnt PDF using non-regularized Maximum Pseudo-Likelihood (MPL).",
            "lineNumber": 900
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 901
          },
          {
            "text": "    This estimator is a composite likelihood method. It finds the parameters",
            "lineNumber": 902
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;mu&#96; for each bivariate marginal *independently* and then combines them.",
            "lineNumber": 903
          },
          {
            "text": "    It is fast but ignores higher-order interactions and can be unstable",
            "lineNumber": 904
          },
          {
            "text": "    if target probabilities are 0 or 1.",
            "lineNumber": 905
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 906
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 907
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 908
          },
          {
            "text": "    active_constraints : list",
            "lineNumber": 909
          },
          {
            "text": "        A list of tuples, &#96;&#96;[((i, j), Pbiv_table), ...]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 910
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;(i, j)&#96;&#96;: A tuple of the two dimension indices.",
            "lineNumber": 911
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;Pbiv_table&#96;&#96;: The &#96;&#96;(nc, nc)&#96;&#96; target probability table.",
            "lineNumber": 912
          },
          {
            "text": "    ndim : int",
            "lineNumber": 913
          },
          {
            "text": "        The total number of dimensions (e.g., estimation point + neighbors).",
            "lineNumber": 914
          },
          {
            "text": "    nc : int",
            "lineNumber": 915
          },
          {
            "text": "        The number of categories.",
            "lineNumber": 916
          },
          {
            "text": "    tol : float",
            "lineNumber": 917
          },
          {
            "text": "        The convergence tolerance for the L-BFGS-B optimizer.",
            "lineNumber": 918
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 919
```

---

## 1. Neighbour selection (`neighbour_ranking`) in the notebook

`bme_opts_3d` is the right place. Ensure `separable_pmodel_3d` already includes `'p_marginal'` (your notebook does), then extend options, for example:

```python
bme_opts_3d = {
    'auto_dmax': True,
    'category_codes': LITHO_CODES,
    'separable_pmodel': separable_pmodel_3d,
    # 'tv' (default in code), 'mutual_info', or legacy 'distance'
    'neighbour_ranking': 'tv',
}
```

You can compare runs by changing `'neighbour_ranking'` to `'mutual_info'` or `'distance'`.

---

## 2. Spatial maps of “XGBoostLSS prior” vs “MCP” before BME

- **XGBoostLSS prior** is `prior_matrix` with shape `(675, 4)` aligned with `ck_bme` — straightforward to map in plan view (`ck_bme[:, 0]`, `ck_bme[:, 1]`).

- **MCP “prior”** in this workflow: `MCPcatPdf` uses a **uniform** prior unless you set something like `prior_pdf_at_ck` or `use_neighbor_average_as_prior`. So there is **no** spatial MCP prior comparable to XGB unless you define one.

Reasonable notebook interpretation (what people usually want):

1. **Map A:** dominant lithology from `prior_matrix` (or probability of one class, or entropy).
2. **Map B:** dominant class from **`result_mcp_3d`** (MCP **baseline prediction**, same grid) — not a prior in the strict sense, but the spatial field MCP gives **before** any XGB prior is used in BME.

If you only need maps **before** the slow `BMEcatPdf` call, run `MCPcatPdf` first, plot `prior_matrix` vs `result_mcp_3d`, then run `BMEcatPdf`.

Example pattern (adjust column names / projection to match your earlier plots):

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

dom_xgb = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)[np.argmax(prior_matrix, axis=1)]
dom_mcp = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)[np.argmax(result_mcp_3d, axis=1)]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, dom, title in zip(axes, [dom_xgb, dom_mcp],
                           ['XGBoostLSS prior (argmax)', 'MCP baseline (argmax, uniform prior)']):
    sc = ax.scatter(ck_bme[:, 0], ck_bme[:, 1], c=dom, cmap='tab10', s=8)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
plt.tight_layout()
```

Add a short markdown note that MCP’s **prior** is uniform; the second panel is the **MCP predictive field**, for spatial comparison with the XGB prior.

---

## 3. Why that cell takes a long time

The cell does **two full grid passes**: `MCPcatPdf` then `BMEcatPdf`, each over **675** targets with **~7913** wells (`cs_bme`).

**`BMEcatPdf` dominates**  
For each grid point it calls `maxentropytable` with default **`model_structure='full'`** — all pairs among estimation point + neighbours — then an iterative estimator (e.g. MPL). That is much heavier than MCP’s closed-form log-sum-exp over neighbours.

**Separable path extras**  
For each point you still do neighbour search over all wells (full `cdist`-style work per target on 3-D coords).

**Default TV neighbour ranking (important)**  
With `separable_pmodel` that includes `p_marginal`, `neighbours_separable` uses **`neighbour_ranking='tv'`** by default. It calls `probamodel2bitable_separable` **once per feasible well inside the per-axis box**, then keeps the top `nsmax`. If horizontal `auto_dmax` is large, **thousands** of wells can be feasible per grid node → cost scales like **675 × N_feasible × (2 runs if MCP+BME)**, on top of ME for BME.

**Mitigations (conceptual)**  
- Set `'neighbour_ranking': 'distance'` to restore cheap geometric ranking.  
- Tighten search: smaller `nsmax`, stricter `auto_dmax_threshold`, or capped neighbourhood.  
- Speed up ME: e.g. `model_structure='knn'` and `k_neighbors=...` in `options` (trade accuracy for speed).  
- Set `'show_progress': 1` to see which phase feels slow.

---

**Summary:** Extend `bme_opts_3d` with `'neighbour_ranking'`. Plot `prior_matrix` and either clarify MCP’s uniform prior or compare to `result_mcp_3d` as the MCP spatial baseline. Slowness is expected from **675 × full well search × default TV ranking over all feasible neighbours × two estimators**, with **BME + full pairwise ME** being the largest cost.

Now I have a complete picture of all four issues. Let me address them all clearly.

---

## Issue 1: `maxentropytable` error — distance above interpolation range

**Root cause:** The new TV/MI neighbour ranking can select neighbours that are geometrically *far apart from each other* (even though each is individually close to the estimation point). When `maxentropytable` then needs a **pairwise Pmodel** for the constraint between two *selected data points*, it computes the horizontal Euclidean distance between them — which can exceed `dmax_h` (≈17 025 m here, but some data-to-data pairs are 17 286, 20 488 … m apart). The old distance ranking always picked the geometrically closest candidates, so their mutual distances were naturally bounded. TV/MI cares only about information content relative to the estimation point, not about keeping data-point pairs within range.

**Why it never happened before:** The old geometric score `sqrt(sum((d_k/dmax_k)^2))` guaranteed that all selected neighbours lie within the per-axis dmax box, and the box's horizontal extent = `dmax_h`. The pairwise distance between any two points inside a ball of radius `dmax_h` is at most `2*dmax_h`, which is often still within the `dmodel` range. With TV/MI the selected points are no longer guaranteed to be close to each other in ordinary space.

**`get_prob_pair` in `maxentropytable`** calls `probamodel2bitable_separable`, which calls the 1-D interpolators for each component. The horizontal component's `dmodel_h` max is 17 024.8 m, but the data–data distance can be up to ~22 000 m → interpolation fails.

**Three ways to fix this** (you need to switch to Agent mode to implement):

**Option A (safest, recommended):** Clamp out-of-range distances to `dmax` in `get_prob_pair` before calling the interpolator. Already done in `probamodel2bitable` for the scalar case via `np.interp` (which clips implicitly), but `probamodel2bitable_separable` uses `interp1d` with `bounds_error=True`. Change this to `fill_value='extrapolate'` or `bounds_error=False, fill_value=(Pmodel[:,:,0], Pmodel[:,:,-1])` in `probatablefit.py`.

**Option B (fast workaround in notebook):** Stay on `'neighbour_ranking': 'distance'` — the old behaviour — until the interpolation range issue is resolved, since the primary gain of TV/MI is in *ranking*, not in the pairwise ME constraints.

**Option C (architectural):** After TV/MI ranking selects `nsmax` neighbours, add a post-filter that removes any pair of selected neighbours whose mutual distance exceeds `dmodel_h[-1]`. This shrinks the effective `nsub` for that point.

---

## Issue 2: `dmodel_h` / `Pmodel_h` as inputs when using `separable_pmodel`

**Short answer: yes, they are effectively ignored for the main computation.** When `options['separable_pmodel']` is set:

- `neighbours_separable` uses **`sep_opt['components'][k]['dmodel']`** and `dmax` — never the top-level `dmodel_h`.
- `maxentropytable` reads `sep_me = options.get('separable_pmodel')` and uses `dmodels_sep` / `Pmodels_sep` from there — never the positional `dmodel`/`Pmodel` arguments.
- `MCPcatPdf`/`BMEcatPdf` similarly branch on `sep_opt is not None`.

The positional `dmodel_h, Pmodel_h, nsmax_3d, 1.0` arguments are **placeholder values**; `ncat` is taken from `sep_opt['components'][0]['Pmodel'].shape[0]` and `dmax=1.0` is never used. The code is correct but the call signature is misleading. You could pass `None, None` for `dmodel`/`Pmodel` but the function signature requires positional arrays. Adding a comment like `# dmodel_h/Pmodel_h unused when separable_pmodel is set` would clarify intent.

---

## Issue 3: Too many warning messages in Prior LOOCV

Both warning sources come from the LOOCV cell (cell 41) at runtime — 52 folds × 2 warnings each = **104 warnings**:

1. **`UserWarning: XGBoostLSS native tuning failed`** — from `BMEcatPrior.py:640`. This is expected because `hyperparams=None` with `n_trials=0` means Optuna runs 0 trials and raises "No trials are completed yet."
2. **`FutureWarning` from xgboost** — a library deprecation from XGBoost 2.1+.

**To suppress them in the notebook**, wrap the `BMEcatPriorLOOCV(...)` call:

```python
import warnings
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.filterwarnings('ignore', message='XGBoostLSS native tuning failed')
    warnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=FutureWarning, module='xgboost')
    loocv = BMEcatPriorLOOCV(
        cs=cs_bme, ps=ps_bme, cs_features=X_well, station_ids=station_ids,
        method='xgboostlss', hyperparams=None, categories=LITHO_CODES, verbose=True,
    )
```

```python
# --- Spatial comparison: XGBoostLSS prior vs MCP baseline (uniform prior) ---
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap

LITHO_COLORS = ['#a6cee3', '#fb9a99', '#b2df8a', '#1f78b4']  # adjust to your palette
cmap = ListedColormap(LITHO_COLORS)
litho_arr = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)

dom_xgb  = np.argmax(prior_matrix, axis=1)      # (675,) index into LITHO_CODES
dom_mcp  = np.argmax(result_mcp_3d, axis=1)

# Pick a representative depth slice for plan-view maps
depth_unique = np.unique(ck_bme[:, 2])
target_z = depth_unique[len(depth_unique) // 2]  # middle depth slice
mask_z = np.abs(ck_bme[:, 2] - target_z) < 1.0

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5), sharex=True, sharey=True)
titles = [
    f'XGBoostLSS prior — argmax (z ≈ {target_z:.0f} m)',
    f'MCP baseline (uniform prior) — argmax (z ≈ {target_z:.0f} m)',
]
for ax, dom, title in zip(axes, [dom_xgb, dom_mcp], titles):
    sc = ax.scatter(
        ck_bme[mask_z, 0], ck_bme[mask_z, 1],
        c=dom[mask_z], cmap=cmap, vmin=0, vmax=len(LITHO_CODES)-1, s=30
    )
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel('X (m)')
    ax.set_ylabel('Y (m)')
    ax.set_aspect('equal')

patches = [mpatches.Patch(color=LITHO_COLORS[i], label=LITHO_LABELS[i])
           for i in range(len(LITHO_CODES))]
axes[1].legend(handles=patches, loc='lower right', fontsize=8)
plt.suptitle('Prior comparison — plan view at one depth slice', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Optionally: entropy comparison to see confidence levels
from scipy.stats import entropy as entropy_fn
ent_xgb = np.array([entropy_fn(row) for row in prior_matrix])
ent_mcp = np.array([entropy_fn(row) for row in result_mcp_3d])

fig2, axes2 = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 4), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, ent, title in zip(axes2, [ent_xgb, ent_mcp],
                           ['Entropy — XGBoostLSS prior', 'Entropy — MCP baseline']):
    sc = ax.scatter(ck_bme[mask_z, 0], ck_bme[mask_z, 1],
                    c=ent[mask_z], cmap='magma_r', s=30)
    plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, label='Shannon entropy (nats)')
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

**Conceptual note to add as a markdown cell:** `result_mcp_3d` (computed with a uniform prior) represents what the spatial transition model alone predicts, without any borehole lithology information — that is the closest analogue to a "MCP prior" in this workflow. The XGBoostLSS `prior_matrix` is the ancillary (feature-based) prior that gets combined with MCP via Bayes-factor correction inside `BMEcatPdf`.

For issue 2, it is weird that we implement the option for the input and do not use the proper place for the Pmodel and dmodel input. Please consult the idea for the covaraince model implementation in stamps and propose a better way for the function inputs to account for separable cases@stamps/stamps/general/coord2K.py and the help of "BMEposteriorMoments" function in which there is a logic for the sepearable model inputs (including covmodel, covparam, nhmax, nsmax, and dmax). Please investigate it and follow the similar convention "    """Compute the BME posterior mean, variance, and third central moment at all estimation locations.

    This is the primary estimation function of the stamps BME engine.  For
    each estimation location in *ck* it evaluates the Bayesian Maximum Entropy
    (BME) posterior distribution conditioned on all available hard and soft
    data, and returns three summary statistics.

    The function selects one of two internal computation paths:

    * **Analytical Gaussian path** (fast) — used whenever every soft datum is
      of type 10 (Gaussian PDF), or when ``options['soft_approx_gaussian']``
      is ``True``, or when more than 20 non-Gaussian soft data are present in
      the neighbourhood (automatic threshold).  Reduces to Simple Kriging or
      Ordinary Kriging depending on *order*.
    * **QMC Importance-Sampling path** (general) — used for non-Gaussian soft
      data (interval / histogram / linear PDFs).  Draws Quasi-Monte Carlo
      samples from the conditional Gaussian prior, weights them by the soft
      likelihood, and estimates the normalised posterior moments.  If the QMC
      normalisation constant is numerically unstable, a per-location Gaussian
      fallback is applied automatically.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ck : ndarray, shape (nk, nd)
        Estimation locations.  ``nd`` is the number of coordinate dimensions:
        ``nd=2`` for purely spatial problems (easting, northing) or ``nd=3``
        for space-time problems (easting, northing, time).  The last column is
        treated as the time axis when ``nd=3``.
    ch : ndarray, shape (nh, nd), optional
        Hard-data (exact observation) locations.  Same coordinate convention
        as *ck*.  Pass ``None`` when no hard data are available.
    cs : ndarray, shape (ns, nd), optional
        Soft-data locations.  Pass ``None`` when no soft data are available.
    zh : ndarray, shape (nh,) or (nh, 1), optional
        Hard-data observed values, one scalar per row of *ch*.  Reshaped
        internally to ``(nh, 1)`` if necessary.
    zs : list of tuples, length ns, optional
        Soft-data probabilistic information.  Each element ``zs[i]``
        describes the PDF at location ``cs[i]`` using the stamps format:

        * ``(1,  nl, limi, probdens)`` — histogram PDF (type 1)
        * ``(2,  nl, limi, probdens)`` — linear PDF (type 2)
        * ``(10, mean, variance)``     — Gaussian PDF (type 10)
        * ``None``                     — missing observation (skipped)

        where ``nl`` is the number of PDF classes (shape ``(1,)`` or
        scalar), ``limi`` are the class boundaries (shape ``(1, nl+1)`` for
        type 1/2), and ``probdens`` are the probability densities
        (shape ``(1, nl)``).
        Use :func:`stamps.bme.softconverter.probaUniform` or
        :func:`stamps.bme.softconverter.probaGaussian` to construct these
        tuples from raw interval or Gaussian parameters.
    covmodel : callable or str, optional
        Covariance model function (e.g. ``exponentialC``, ``sphericalC``).
        Required unless *covmat* is provided.  Accepts the signature
        ``covmodel(dist, sill, range_param)``.
    covparam : list or ndarray, optional
        Parameters for *covmodel* in stamps nested-model format.  Required
        unless *covmat* is provided.  See :func:`stamps.models.covmodel` for
        the expected structure.
    covmat : ndarray, shape (nk+nh+ns, nk+nh+ns), optional
        Pre-computed full covariance matrix covering all estimation and data
        locations in the stacked order ``[ck; ch; cs]``.  When provided,
        *covmodel* and *covparam* are ignored and no distances need to be
        computed.  Useful when the same matrix is reused across multiple calls
        (e.g. in a GUI loop).
    order : {np.nan, 0, ndarray of shape (nk+nh+ns, 1)}, default ``np.nan``
        Prior-mean specification controlling the large-scale trend:

        * ``np.nan``  — **zero-mean prior**.  Equivalent to Simple Kriging.
          Estimates revert to 0 wherever data are absent.  Appropriate only
          when the field has been pre-de-meaned.
        * ``0``       — **global-mean prior**.  A single constant equal to
          the weighted average of all data (equivalent to Ordinary Kriging).
          Estimates revert to the data mean in data-sparse areas.
        * ``ndarray`` — **spatially-varying prior mean**, one value per row
          of the stacked ``[ck; ch; cs]`` coordinate array.  Use the output
          of :func:`BMEpriorMean` (method ``'kernel'`` or ``'kriging'``) to
          build this array for a data-adaptive locally-varying trend.
    options : BMEoptions or None, optional
        Dictionary-like object controlling numerical options.  When ``None``
        (default), :class:`stamps.bme.BMEoptions` defaults are used.
        Relevant keys:

        * ``'soft_approx_gaussian'`` *(bool, default False)* — force the
          analytical Gaussian approximation for all soft data, bypassing QMC.
          Speeds up computation at the cost of accuracy when intervals are wide
          or asymmetric.
        * ``'outlier_handling'`` *(str, default ``'inflate'``)* — how to treat
          soft data whose interval is statistically incompatible with the
          conditional prior ``E[Zs|Zh]``:
          ``'inflate'`` expands the interval to restore compatibility;
          ``'exclude'`` removes the datum from the neighbourhood;
          ``'ignore'`` keeps all data unchanged.
        * ``'outlier_inflate_margin'`` *(float, default 0.10)* — fractional
          extra margin added beyond the minimum inflation required.
        * ``'min_overlap_prob'`` *(float, default 0.10)* — minimum overlap
          probability (``P(interval | prior)``) below which a soft datum is
          flagged for handling.
        * ``'pca_integration_threshold'`` *(float, default 0.999)* — fraction
          of conditional variance retained when PCA dimension-reduction is
          applied before QMC integration.  Reducing this (e.g. to 0.95)
          dramatically lowers QMC dimension at a small accuracy cost.
        * ``'nonneg_estimate'`` *(bool, default False)* — clamp negative
          posterior means to zero using truncated-Normal theory.  Appropriate
          for physically non-negative variables (concentrations, proportions).
    nhmax : int or None, optional
        Maximum number of hard-data neighbours included in each local
        neighbourhood.  ``None`` (default) includes all hard data within
        *dmax*.  Increasing this improves accuracy but raises the cost of
        the covariance system solve.
    nsmax : int or None, optional
        Maximum number of soft-data neighbours.  ``None`` includes all soft
        data within *dmax*.  Raising *nsmax* beyond ~16 can render QMC
        integration prohibitively expensive; consider enabling
        ``'pca_integration_threshold'`` or ``'soft_approx_gaussian'``.
    dmax : float or array-like, optional
        Maximum search radius.  For purely spatial problems supply a single
        positive float (metres or matching coordinate units).  For space-time
        problems supply a three-element array ``[s_max, t_max, s_t_ratio]``
        where ``s_t_ratio`` converts time units to space units.  ``None``
        (default) includes all data regardless of distance.
    general_knowledge : {'gaussian'}, default ``'gaussian'``
        Prior structural model.  Currently only ``'gaussian'`` (Gaussian
        random field) is supported.  Reserved for future extension to
        non-Gaussian structural models.
    pdfk, pdfh, pdfs : list or None, optional
        Legacy MATLAB-compatibility arguments carrying pre-computed prior PDFs
        at estimation, hard-data, and soft-data locations respectively.
        **Not needed for standard usage** — pass ``None``.
    hk_k, hk_h, hk_s : list or None, optional
        Legacy MATLAB-compatibility arguments for hard-knowledge (mean, variance)
        tuples at each coordinate set.  **Not needed for standard usage** —
        pass ``None``.
    gui_args : tuple or None, optional
        Hook for GUI progress dialogs.  Pass a tuple ``(QProgressDialog,)``
        when running inside a Qt application; pass ``None`` for headless use.
    ck_cov_output : bool, default ``False``
        If ``True``, also return the posterior covariance matrix among the
        estimation locations (useful for uncertainty propagation).
    n_workers : int, default 1
        Number of parallel threads for neighbourhood processing via
        :class:`concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor`.  Values ``> 1``
        are effective when many independent neighbourhood groups exist.
        Thread-safety relies on the GIL; set ``n_workers=1`` for deterministic
        reproducibility.

    Returns
    -------
    zk : ndarray, shape (nk, 3)
        BME posterior statistics at each estimation location:

        * ``zk[:, 0]`` — posterior mean  ``E[Zk | Zh, Zs]``
        * ``zk[:, 1]`` — posterior variance  ``Var[Zk | Zh, Zs]``
          (guaranteed non-negative; ``delta_mu`` QMC-noise contribution is
          subtracted before clamping)
        * ``zk[:, 2]`` — third central moment
          ``E[(Zk - E[Zk])^3 | Zh, Zs]``
          (zero for the Gaussian fast-path; non-zero for QMC path)

        Rows corresponding to estimation locations with no neighbours within
        *dmax* will contain ``np.nan`` in all three columns.

        If *ck_cov_output* is ``True``, returns a tuple
        ``(zk, ck_cov)`` where ``ck_cov`` is the ``(nk, nk)`` posterior
        covariance matrix computed via the Gaussian approximation.

    Notes
    -----
    **BME integration theory**

    The BME posterior PDF at estimation location :math:`\\mathbf{c}_k` is:

    .. math::

        f_K(z_k) \\propto f_G(z_k | \\mathbf{z}_h)
            \\cdot
            \\underbrace{\\int f_G(\\mathbf{z}_s | z_k, \\mathbf{z}_h)
                          \\cdot f_S(\\mathbf{z}_s)\\,d\\mathbf{z}_s}_{\\text{SI}}

    where :math:`f_G` is the Gaussian prior and :math:`f_S` is the product
    of soft-data likelihoods.  The normalisation constant is:

    .. math::

        \\text{NC} = \\int f_G(\\mathbf{z}_s | \\mathbf{z}_h)
                          \\cdot f_S(\\mathbf{z}_s)\\,d\\mathbf{z}_s

    The posterior moments are:

    .. math::

        E[Z_k | \\mathbf{z}_h, \\mathbf{z}_s]
            = \\mu_{k|h} + \\frac{\\text{SI}_1}{\\text{NC}}

Now I have everything I need. Here is a thorough analysis of both issues.

---

## Issue 1 — Root cause and proposed fix

### What is actually happening

`probamodel2bitable` uses `scipy.interpolate.interp1d` **with default `bounds_error=True`**. Every call with a distance beyond `dmodel[-1]` raises `ValueError`.

The TV/MI ranking in `neighbours_separable` selects up to `nsmax` data points based on their **information content relative to the estimation point**. Each selected point is guaranteed to be within the per-axis `dmax` box. But when `maxentropytable` then builds the ME constraint table, it calls `get_prob_pair(i, j)` for **every pair of selected data points**. The distance between two selected *data* points can be up to `2 × dmax_h` — and because the horizontal Pmodel was fitted only to `dmax_h` ≈ 17 025 m, any data–data pair exceeding that blows up.

With the old **distance-based ranking**, all selected points also happened to be close to the estimation point, so data–data pairs typically stayed within range. That was a coincidental constraint. TV/MI removes it.

### The physically correct fix — extrapolate to the independence table

When two points are **farther apart than the correlation range**, their joint probability should approach independence: `P(a, b; d→∞) → p(a)·p(b)`. The fix is to make `probamodel2bitable` silently return `outer(p, p)` for out-of-range distances, instead of crashing.

**In `probatablefit.py` — change `probamodel2bitable`:**

```python
def probamodel2bitable(d, dmodel, Pmodel):
    nc = Pmodel.shape[0]
    Pd = np.zeros((nc, nc))
    d_clamp = float(np.clip(d, dmodel[0], dmodel[-1]))   # <-- clamp
    for k in range(nc):
        for l in range(nc):
            f = interp1d(dmodel, Pmodel[k, l], kind='linear')
            Pd[k, l] = f(d_clamp)
    return Pd
```

A single-line `np.clip` before the loop is sufficient. This is valid because:
1. The Pmodel is already converging toward `outer(p, p)` at `dmodel[-1]` by definition of the correlation range.
2. Extrapolating *beyond* the fitted range is physically meaningless and numerically unstable.
3. For the separable product chain, clamping each component's distance independently is consistent — a very far-away data point contributes a near-independence table to the chain product, which is correct.

Alternatively, replace `interp1d` (which checks bounds) with `np.interp` (which extrapolates by clamping):

```python
def probamodel2bitable(d, dmodel, Pmodel):
    nc = Pmodel.shape[0]
    Pmodel_vec = Pmodel.reshape(nc**2, -1)
    # np.interp clamps d to [dmodel[0], dmodel[-1]] silently
    Pd = np.array([np.interp(d, dmodel, Pmodel_vec[k]) for k in range(nc**2)])
    return Pd.reshape(nc, nc)
```

Note: `BMEcatPdf.py`'s own `probamodel2bitable` (the local copy) already uses `np.interp` internally, so it never crashes. The crash comes from **`probatablefit.py`**'s version used by `probamodel2bitable_separable` → `get_prob_pair` inside `maxentropytable`.

---

## Issue 2 — Better API design following BMEposteriorMoments / coord2K convention

### The stamps convention (from `BMEposteriorMoments`)

The stamps Gaussian BME engine cleanly separates:

| Concern | Parameter |
|---|---|
| **Model structure** | `covmodel`, `covparam` (or `covmat` pre-computed) |
| **Search budget** | `nhmax`, `nsmax` (separate caps for hard/soft) |
| **Search radius** | `dmax` (scalar or 3-vector for space-time `[s_max, t_max, s_t_ratio]`) |
| **Algorithmic options** | `options` dict |

Separable space-time is expressed naturally through **the model name** (`'exponentialC/exponentialC'`) and parameters `(sill, ar_s, ar_t)` — no special `options` key needed. The caller does not need to pass a dummy `covmodel` when using the separable form; they use the correct one.

### Why the current `MCPcatPdf` / `BMEcatPdf` API is awkward

```python
MCPcatPdf(ck, cs, ps,
          dmodel, Pmodel,        # ← required positional args
          nsmax, dmax,
          options=None)          # separable_pmodel lives here
```

When you use `separable_pmodel`, you must still pass `dmodel` and `Pmodel` as **positional placeholders**. The model and the search parameters are also conflated: `dmax` is embedded inside `components[k]['dmax']` and `nsmax` is not separated from being a single scalar.

### Proposed new signature following stamps convention

```python
MCPcatPdf(
    ck, cs, ps,
    # --- model (choose one form) ---
    dmodel=None, Pmodel=None,           # 1-D isotropic model
    separable_pmodel=None,              # separable multi-axis model
    # --- search parameters ---
    nsmax=None, dmax=None,
    # --- algorithmic options ---
    options=None,
)
```

Key principles:
1. **`separable_pmodel` becomes a top-level named argument**, not buried in `options`. Just as `covmodel`/`covparam` vs. `covmat` in `BMEposteriorMoments` are first-class alternatives.
2. **`dmax` is a single scalar or per-axis array** (for the 1-D case), same as `dmax` in `BMEposteriorMoments`. For the separable case, per-axis `dmax` lives inside `components[k]['dmax']` — the caller still has a consistent single `dmax` argument for the 1-D path.
3. **`auto_dmax` moves to `options`** (it already is there — keep it).
4. **`nsmax` stays a single scalar** — in BME Gaussian it is split as `nhmax` / `nsmax`, but since categorical BME has only one data type, one limit is sufficient.
5. **The model structure drives the computation path**, not a runtime options flag — exactly how `isspacetime(models)` in `coord2K` picks the separable vs. non-separable distance formula.

Internal logic at entry:

```python
def MCPcatPdf(ck, cs, ps,
              dmodel=None, Pmodel=None,
              separable_pmodel=None,
              nsmax=None, dmax=None,
              options=None):
    if options is None:
        options = {}
    # Inject separable_pmodel into options for downstream compatibility
    # (maxentropytable, neighbours_separable all read from options)
    if separable_pmodel is not None:
        options = {**options, 'separable_pmodel': separable_pmodel}
    sep_opt = options.get('separable_pmodel')
    if sep_opt is not None:
        if dmodel is None or Pmodel is None:
            # infer nc from separable components
            ncat = int(sep_opt['components'][0]['Pmodel'].shape[0])
        ...
    elif dmodel is None or Pmodel is None:
        raise ValueError("Provide dmodel+Pmodel, or separable_pmodel.")
    ...
```

This keeps full backward-compatibility (old code passing `dmodel, Pmodel` positionally still works via `dmodel=dmodel, Pmodel=Pmodel` after the signature change; positional arg order is preserved if `dmodel` and `Pmodel` remain at positions 3 and 4).

## Issue 1 — Suitability of the reference code

### What the reference code does right

The architecture is conceptually correct and **the key insight is good**: pre-screen by `dmax` first (reducing the candidate set), then score only surviving candidates via TV. This is exactly the structure already in `neighbours_separable` (lines 369–415). The reference code just makes the vectorised form explicit.

Mapping the reference onto your current code:

| Reference step | Current `neighbours_separable` |
|---|---|
| `calculate_horizontal_dist / calculate_vertical_dist` | `cdist(c0[:,cols], c[:,cols])` per axis → `D[:, j]` |
| dmax pre-screen (implied) | `valid &= D[:, j] < dmaxs[j]` → `idx_all` |
| `interpolate_p_model(h_h, …)` → shape `(n, nc, nc)` | `probamodel2bitable(dvec[j], dmodels[j], Pmodels[j])` per point in loop |
| `compute_separable_product(P_h, P_v, p)` → `(n, nc, nc)` | `probamodel2bitable_separable(dvec, …)` per point |
| `tv_scores = 0.5 * np.abs(P_3d - P_indep).sum(axis=(1,2))` | `0.5 * np.abs(P3d - P_indep).sum()` per point in loop |

The only structural difference is vectorisation: the reference computes **all candidates at once** using batch `(n, nc, nc)` arrays; the current code uses a per-candidate Python `for m` loop. For large candidate pools this matters for speed, but the logic is identical.

### Three deficiencies in the reference code

**1. `P_indep` is undefined / unscoped.** The line:
```python
tv_scores = 0.5 * np.sum(np.abs(P_3d - P_indep), axis=(1, 2))
```
uses `P_indep` as a free variable. It must be `np.outer(p_marginal, p_marginal)`, broadcast to `(1, nc, nc)` for vectorised subtraction. The current implementation correctly computes this inside the loop but it is constant and should be moved outside.

**2. dmax pre-screening is absent from the shown code.** The function operates on all `data_coords`. Without a dmax filter, TV is computed for every data point in the dataset — the full 7913-well set in Pingtung — which is O(n × nc²) matrix operations. The filter must come first.

**3. Out-of-range distances in `interpolate_p_model`.** For the *TV scoring* step this is not actually the source of your error. Here is why: `auto_dmax` sets `dmax_h` from `dmodel_h[-1]` via `_find_effective_range`. All estimation-to-data distances that survive the dmax filter are ≤ `dmax_h` ≤ `dmodel_h[-1]`. So `interpolate_p_model` will never receive an out-of-range value during neighbour scoring.

### Where the actual error originates

The crash `"A value (17286 …) in x_new is above (17024 …)"` comes from `get_prob_pair(i, j)` inside **`maxentropytable`** — specifically line 1349 in your code — which computes the bivariate table for **pairs of selected data points** (not estimation-to-data). Two data wells that are individually within `dmax_h` of the estimation point can be up to `2 × dmax_h` apart from each other. `probamodel2bitable_separable` → `probamodel2bitable` in `probatablefit.py` uses `interp1d` with `bounds_error=True` (the default), so it crashes at line 40–41.

The reference code's pre-screening step does **not** protect against this because the problem occurs in `maxentropytable`, not in `neighbours_separable`. **The fix must be in `probatablefit.probamodel2bitable`**:

```python
# Change line 40-41 in probatablefit.py from:
f = interp1d(dmodel, Pmodel[k,l], kind='linear')
Pd[k,l] = f(d)

# To (drop interp1d entirely; np.interp silently clamps to [dmodel[0], dmodel[-1]]):
Pd[k,l] = np.interp(d, dmodel, Pmodel[k,l])
```

This is physically correct: beyond the correlation range the table approaches `outer(p, p)` (independence), and `dmodel[-1]` is already at or near that plateau by construction of `auto_dmax`.

## Issue 2 — Keeping `dmodel` / `Pmodel` but making them format-aware

### Your proposal is exactly the stamps convention

You are right. The stamps covariance engine already does precisely this in `coord2K`:

- `models`: `['exponentialC']` → pure spatial; `['exponentialC/exponentialC']` → separable S/T
- `params`: `(sill, range)` or `(sill, ar_s, ar_t)` depending on the model
- `dmax`: scalar → spatial; `[s_max, t_max, ratio]` → space-time

The format of the *parameters adapts* to the model, detected from the type/structure of the inputs. No separate `separable_pmodel` option key is needed.

### Proposed design following that convention exactly

**`dmodel`** — scalar 1-D array **or** list of 1-D arrays:
- 1-D: `dmodel = np.array([0, 100, …, 17000])` → shape `(nd,)`
- Separable: `dmodel = [dmodel_h, dmodel_v]` → list of two arrays

**`Pmodel`** — single 3-D array **or** list of 3-D arrays:
- 1-D: `Pmodel` → shape `(nc, nc, nd)`
- Separable: `Pmodel = [Pmodel_h, Pmodel_v]` → list of two `(nc, nc, nd_k)` arrays

**`dmax`** — scalar **or** array/list:
- 1-D: `dmax = 17000.0`
- Separable: `dmax = [dmax_h, dmax_v]` or `dmax = None` (→ auto_dmax computes per component)

**`nsmax`** — always a single `int`, no change.

**`p_marginal`** — only relevant for separable; goes in `options` (analogous to `order` in `BMEposteriorMoments` which is a model parameter but passed as a named arg). Alternatively it becomes a named keyword beside `dmax`. The stamps analogy here is `covmat=` — an optional override that replaces `covmodel`/`covparam`. A clean place is `options['p_marginal']` since it is a property of the fitted Pmodel, not of the search.

**`mode`** (`'product'`/`'additive'`) → `options['separable_mode']`, analogous to algorithmic options in `BMEoptions`.

The function signature stays identical externally:

```python
def MCPcatPdf(ck, cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, options=None):
    ...
```

Internal detection (analogous to `isspacetime(models)`):

```python
def _is_separable_pmodel(dmodel, Pmodel):
    """Return True when dmodel/Pmodel describe a separable multi-axis model."""
    return isinstance(dmodel, (list, tuple)) and isinstance(Pmodel, (list, tuple))
```

Then the routing replaces the current `options.get('separable_pmodel')` pattern:

```python
sep = _is_separable_pmodel(dmodel, Pmodel)
if sep:
    # dmodel is [dmodel_h, dmodel_v, …], Pmodel is [Pmodel_h, Pmodel_v, …]
    # dmax is [dmax_h, dmax_v, …] or None
    # Reconstruct components list from (dmodel_k, Pmodel_k, dmax_k) per axis
    # via coord_cols inferred from options (or a required key)
    p_marginal = options.get('p_marginal')
    mode = options.get('separable_mode', 'product')
    components = _build_components(dmodel, Pmodel, dmax, options)
    # hand off to neighbours_separable, maxentropytable as before
else:
    # 1-D: existing path unchanged
```

The notebook call becomes:

```python
# 1-D vertical (existing, unchanged)
result_mcp = MCPcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme,
    dmodel_v, Pmodel_v,
    nsmax, dmax_v,
    options={'category_codes': LITHO_CODES},
)

# Separable 3-D (natural; no placeholders, no buried options key)
result_mcp_3d = MCPcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme,
    [dmodel_h, dmodel_v],          # dmodel as list → separable detected
    [Pmodel_h, Pmodel_v],          # Pmodel as list → separable detected
    nsmax_3d,
    [dmax_h, dmax_v],              # per-axis dmax; or None → auto_dmax
    options={
        'category_codes': LITHO_CODES,
        'p_marginal': p_bg_station,         # marginal for product/additive
        'separable_mode': 'product',        # or 'additive'
        'coord_cols': [[0, 1], [2]],        # which columns are H, V
        'neighbour_ranking': 'tv',
    },
)
```

### How `coord_cols` fits in

In the current `separable_pmodel` dict, `coord_cols` specifies which coordinate columns correspond to each axis (e.g. `[0,1]` for XY Euclidean, `[2]` for depth Z). Under the new scheme this is the only information that cannot be inferred purely from the array shapes, so it must stay somewhere. `options['coord_cols']` is the natural place — it is metadata about the coordinate layout, analogous to the `s_t_ratio` that stamps passes inside `dmax` for the Gaussian S/T case.

### Summary of both changes needed

| Location | Fix |
|---|---|
| `probatablefit.probamodel2bitable` | Replace `interp1d(…)(d)` → `np.interp(d, dmodel, Pmodel[k,l])` to silently clamp data-to-data distances |
| `BMEcatPdf.py` — type-detection helper | Add `_is_separable_pmodel(dmodel, Pmodel)` → returns `True` when both are lists |
| `BMEcatPdf.py` — routing at entry | Replace `options.get('separable_pmodel')` with the type-detection call |
| Notebook / callers | Replace `separable_pmodel` dict in options with list-form `dmodel`/`Pmodel`/`dmax` |

Both changes can be made in Agent mode.

## Issue 1 — A check in `neighbours_separable` to prevent out-of-range pairwise distances

### Is it correct to fix this in the neighbour function?

Yes, and this is actually the **better fix location** compared to patching `probamodel2bitable`. The neighbour function is where the search radius is set; that is where the root cause lives.

### The mathematical basis for the check

If every selected candidate `i` satisfies `d_k(i, c0) < dmax_k` along axis `k`, then the pairwise distance between any two candidates is bounded by the **triangle inequality**:

```
d_k(i, j) ≤ d_k(i, c0) + d_k(c0, j) < 2 × dmax_k
```

For `maxentropytable` to always receive in-range distances, we need:

```
2 × dmax_k ≤ dmodel_k[-1]    →    dmax_k ≤ dmodel_k[-1] / 2
```

This gives a clean, one-time, provably correct reduction. No iteration needed.

### Where to place the check

Insert it **immediately after** reading `dmaxs[j]` from `comp['dmax']` and **before** the `valid` mask is built (lines 360–371). The flow becomes:

```
1. Read dmax_k from component
2. CHECK: if dmax_k > dmodel_k[-1] / 2, reduce to dmodel_k[-1] / 2
3. Apply valid mask with (possibly reduced) dmax_k
4. Score by TV/MI
5. Return top nsmax
```

Pseudo-code for the check block:
```python
for j, comp in enumerate(components):
    cols = np.asarray(comp['coord_cols'], dtype=int)
    dmaxs[j] = float(comp['dmax'])
    
    # --- Pairwise-range compliance check ---
    # Any two candidates within dmax_j of c0 can be at most 2*dmax_j apart.
    # Cap dmax_j so that data-to-data pairwise distances cannot exceed dmodel[-1],
    # preventing out-of-range interpolation errors in maxentropytable.
    dmodel_max_j = float(comp['dmodel'][-1])
    safe_dmax_j  = dmodel_max_j / 2.0
    if dmaxs[j] > safe_dmax_j:
        dmaxs[j] = safe_dmax_j
    # --- end check ---
```

### Why `dmodel[-1] / 2` is the right threshold

Look at what `auto_dmax` returns (via `_find_effective_range`): it finds the distance where TV drops to 5% of its d=0 value. For the Pingtung horizontal model this is essentially `dmodel_h[-1]` ≈ 17 025 m (the correlation length is close to the grid extent). So `dmax_h ≈ 17 025`, and two wells within that ball can be 17 286 m apart — just 1.5% over the table's max. Capping `dmax_h` at `17025 / 2 ≈ 8512 m` guarantees the violation cannot happen.

### Does this hurt the neighbourhood quality?

Only marginally. The pairwise probability `P(a,b; d > dmodel[-1]/2)` is already very close to the independence product `p_a × p_b`, so those far neighbours carry almost no spatial information anyway. Excluding them is scientifically sound — and the TV/MI ranking ensures the most *informative* of the closer wells are picked.

For the vertical axis (`dmodel_v[-1]` is much shorter), `dmax_v` from `auto_dmax` is already well within `dmodel_v[-1]`, so the cap has no effect there. The check only bites for the horizontal axis when `auto_dmax` returns a value close to the full table range.

### Comparison with patching `probamodel2bitable`

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Cap `dmax` in `neighbours_separable` | Fixes root cause; no silent behaviour change in core math; leaves a clear record (dmax was reduced) | Reduces neighbourhood radius |
| Clamp `d` in `probamodel2bitable` | Allows full radius; backward-compatible | Silently accepts physically invalid distances; extrapolation beyond fitted range is unsupported |

The user's intuition is right: fixing the neighbourhood function is the cleaner location.

## Issue 2 — Auto-detection of separable Pmodel; `mode` as a first-class parameter

### Current `MCPcatPdf` / `BMEcatPdf` signature

```python
def MCPcatPdf(ck, cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, options=None):
```

`separable_pmodel` lives in `options`. `mode` lives inside `options['separable_pmodel']['mode']`.

### Proposed signature keeping `dmodel`/`Pmodel` but making them format-aware

```python
def MCPcatPdf(ck, cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, mode='product', options=None):
```

**`dmodel` and `Pmodel`** carry the model in either form:

| Case | `dmodel` type | `Pmodel` type |
|---|---|---|
| 1-D (isotropic) | `ndarray` shape `(nd,)` | `ndarray` shape `(nc, nc, nd)` |
| Separable | `list` of arrays `[dmodel_h, dmodel_v]` | `list` of arrays `[Pmodel_h, Pmodel_v]` |

**`dmax`** adapts accordingly:
- 1-D: scalar float
- Separable: `None` (→ auto_dmax per component) or `list` `[dmax_h, dmax_v]`

**`mode`** — explicit named keyword, not buried in `options`:
- `'product'` (default) — Markov-chain composition `P_h D⁻¹ P_v`
- `'additive'` — additive combination

**`options`** retains only algorithmic knobs (ranking, estimator, tolerance, etc.) and the minimal model metadata that cannot be inferred from shape alone:
- `'p_marginal'` — needed for separable product/additive composition
- `'coord_cols'` — which columns of `cs`/`ck` belong to each axis (e.g. `[[0,1],[2]]`)
- `'category_codes'`, `'auto_dmax'`, `'neighbour_ranking'`, etc.

### Auto-detection (analogous to `isspacetime(models)`)

```python
def _detect_pmodel_form(dmodel, Pmodel):
    """Return 'separable' or '1d' from the type of dmodel/Pmodel."""
    if isinstance(dmodel, (list, tuple)) and isinstance(Pmodel, (list, tuple)):
        if len(dmodel) != len(Pmodel):
            raise ValueError("dmodel and Pmodel lists must have the same length")
        return 'separable'
    return '1d'
```

This mirrors `isspacetime(models)` exactly — detection driven purely by input structure, no extra flag.

### Internal routing

```python
form = _detect_pmodel_form(dmodel, Pmodel)

if form == 'separable':
    coord_cols = options.get('coord_cols')     # required for separable
    p_marginal  = options.get('p_marginal')    # required for product/additive
    dmax_list = dmax if isinstance(dmax, (list, tuple)) else [None] * len(dmodel)
    
    # Reconstruct the components list that all existing internals use
    components = [
        {
            'dmodel':     np.asarray(dmodel[k]),
            'Pmodel':     np.asarray(Pmodel[k]),
            'coord_cols': coord_cols[k],
            'dmax':       dmax_list[k] if dmax_list[k] is not None else np.inf,
        }
        for k in range(len(dmodel))
    ]
    sep_opt = {'components': components, 'p_marginal': p_marginal, 'mode': mode}
    # Inject into options so all downstream internals (maxentropytable,
    # neighbours_separable) continue to work unchanged
    options = {**options, 'separable_pmodel': sep_opt}
else:
    # 1-D path: dmodel/Pmodel are ndarrays; mode is unused
    ...
```

The `options['separable_pmodel']` key is still set internally so **all existing downstream code** (inside `maxentropytable`, `neighbours_separable`) requires **zero changes**. The auto-detection and new signature are purely a front-end translation layer.

### What the notebook call looks like

```python
# 1-D vertical — unchanged from current API
result_mcp = MCPcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme,
    dmodel_v, Pmodel_v,
    nsmax, dmax_v,
    options={'category_codes': LITHO_CODES},
)

# Separable 3-D — dmodel/Pmodel as lists; no placeholder args; mode explicit
result_mcp_3d = MCPcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme,
    [dmodel_h, dmodel_v],          # list → separable auto-detected
    [Pmodel_h, Pmodel_v],          # list → separable auto-detected
    nsmax_3d,
    [None, None],                  # or [dmax_h, dmax_v]; None → auto_dmax per component
    mode='product',                # explicit; default anyway
    options={
        'category_codes': LITHO_CODES,
        'coord_cols':  [[0, 1], [2]],    # H = columns XY, V = column Z
        'p_marginal':  p_bg_station,
        'neighbour_ranking': 'tv',
    },
)
```

### Summary of both proposed changes

| Concern | Proposed location | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Out-of-range pairwise distance | **Cap `dmax_k ≤ dmodel_k[-1] / 2` in `neighbours_separable`** before screening | Fixes root cause; provably correct via triangle inequality; no silent extrapolation |
| `mode` parameter | Named keyword in `MCPcatPdf` / `BMEcatPdf` | Matches stamps convention; first-class model config, not an option flag |
| Separable vs 1-D detection | `_detect_pmodel_form(dmodel, Pmodel)` at function entry | Same pattern as `isspacetime(models)` in `coord2K` |
| `p_marginal`, `coord_cols` | Stay in `options` | They are model metadata, not structural; analogous to how stamps puts `aniso_angle` in optional kwargs rather than the main `covparam` |
| All internal machinery | Unchanged | `sep_opt` injected back into options internally; `neighbours_separable`, `maxentropytable` need no edits |

```
### 5e. Separable 3-D Pmodel (product default; additive optional)

Instead of a single Euclidean 3-D distance on **stretched** coordinates (which can
wash out vertical structure), we combine the **horizontal** Pmodel (Section 5c, XY)
and the **vertical** Pmodel (Section 5a, Z) with a **separable** rule.

**Product mode (default)** — Markov-chain composition (Carle &amp; Fogg 1997):

\[
P_{3D}(h_{XY}, h_Z) \;=\; P_H(h_{XY})\, D^{-1}\, P_Z(h_Z),
\quad D = \mathrm{diag}(p),
\]

where \(p\) is the global marginal (here &#96;p_bg_station&#96;).  Row sums stay \(p_a\); no
clipping is required.  **Additive mode*
```

Now I have a complete picture. Here is the analysis of all three options.

---

## `mode` → into `options`

Agreed with you. `mode='product'` belongs in `options` alongside `auto_dmax`, `neighbour_ranking`, etc. It is a configuration choice, not a model structural indicator. The auto-detection of separable vs. 1-D is done from the type of `dmodel`/`Pmodel` (list vs ndarray), and `mode` simply governs how the detected separable model is composed.

```python
mode = options.get('mode', 'product')   # 'product' or 'additive'
```

---

## `category_codes` — is it redundant?

**No, but it can be auto-inferred in most cases.**

### What it does (lines 67–75 of `_coerce_ps_soft`)

It maps the raw `ps` labels (e.g. `[1, 2, 3, 4]` for Pingtung) to column indices `[0, 1, 2, 3]` of the `(n, nc)` soft-indicator matrix. Without it, the function assumes `ps` already contains 0-indexed integers `0 … nc-1`. Since Pingtung uses LithoCode values `[1, 2, 3, 4]` (from `LITHO_CODES`), `category_codes` is essential here.

### Can it be auto-detected?

Partially. The function already knows `nc` from `Pmodel.shape[0]`. When `ps` is 1-D:

- **Easy case**: `ps` values are already in `{0, 1, …, nc-1}` → no mapping needed, `category_codes` is redundant.
- **Auto-detectable**: `ps` values are not in `{0, …, nc-1}`, but `len(np.unique(ps)) == nc` → infer `category_codes = np.sort(np.unique(ps))`. This works correctly when the codes are in **sorted ascending order** matching the Pmodel row order (exactly the Pingtung convention: codes 1,2,3,4 → rows 0,1,2,3).
- **Cannot remove**: when codes are in a **non-sorted** custom order (e.g. `LITHO_CODES = [4, 2, 1, 3]`), auto-inferring `np.sort(np.unique(ps))` would give the wrong mapping. This is why `category_codes` must remain as an explicit option for the general case.

**Proposed behaviour**: make it optional. When absent and `ps` values fall outside `[0, nc)`, auto-detect via `np.sort(np.unique(ps))` with a clarifying message (not a warning/error). Users with non-sorted codes must still supply it explicitly.

---

## `coord_cols` — is it redundant?

**Redundant in the common case; only needed for unusual coordinate layouts.**

### What it does

Tells the function which columns of the `(n, d)` coordinate array map to each separable axis component. In Pingtung: `cs_bme` is `(n, 3)` with columns `[X, Y, Z]`, so `coord_cols = [[0, 1], [2]]` means "use columns 0,1 for horizontal distance, column 2 for vertical distance."

### Can it be auto-detected?

Yes, with a convention identical to the stamps S/T rule in `coord2K` (spatial = first columns, time/depth = last column):

| `cs` shape | separable components `K` | Auto default |
|---|---|---|
| `(n, 3)` and `K = 2` | XY + Z | `[[0, 1], [2]]` |
| `(n, 2)` and `K = 2` | X + Z | `[[0], [1]]` |
| `(n, 4)` and `K = 3` | XY + Z + T | `[[0, 1], [2], [3]]` |

This covers 99% of real use cases. For non-standard layouts (e.g., `cs` has `[Y, X, T, Z]` and the user wants the 3rd column to be horizontal), they would supply `coord_cols` explicitly.

**Proposed behaviour**: make `coord_cols` optional. When absent, the function auto-assigns columns using the convention above, inferring from `cs.shape[1]` and the number of `dmodel` list elements. If the auto-assignment would be ambiguous (e.g., `cs.shape[1] > K+1`), issue a clear message telling the user to specify `coord_cols`.

---

## `p_marginal` — is it redundant?

**Yes, it is fully redundant and can always be computed from `Pmodel`.**

### What it does

It is the category marginal `p(c)` vector, shape `(nc,)`. Used in:
1. Product composition: `D_inv = diag(1/p)`, so `P_3d = P_h @ D_inv @ P_v` (line 99)
2. Additive composition: `P_indep = outer(p, p)` (line 108)
3. TV/MI scoring in `neighbours_separable`: `P_indep = outer(p, p)` (line 406)

### Where it already comes from implicitly

Look at `_find_effective_range` at lines 1993–1996 — **the code already auto-derives `p_marginal` from `Pmodel`**:

```python
P_far = Pmodel[:, :, -1]
p_marginal = P_far.sum(axis=1)   # row marginals at the largest distance
```

For a correctly-fitted Pmodel, `P(a, b; d → ∞) = p(a) · p(b)`, so the row sums at the largest tabulated distance give exactly `p(c)`. The whole purpose of fitting the Pmodel out to a large enough distance is to reach this asymptote.

### Why it was a separate parameter

Two reasons that are no longer compelling:
1. *Accuracy concern*: the far-field table may not have fully converged to the independence product, so `p` estimated from it could be slightly off → now addressed by `auto_dmax` which ensures we only use the model up to its effective range.
2. *User control*: the user might want to supply empirical `p` from a different dataset → a legitimate edge case, but `p_marginal` in `options` remains available for that scenario.

**Proposed behaviour**: make `p_marginal` optional in `options`. When absent, auto-compute per component from `Pmodel_k[:, :, -1].sum(axis=1)` (using each component's far-field table). Since the separable components may have slightly different row marginals due to fitting, take the **average across components** or use the component with the most distant `dmodel[-1]` (closest to true independence).

---

## Summary: what can be removed vs. what must stay

| Option | Verdict | Proposed default when absent |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | Keep in `options` | `'product'` |
| `category_codes` | **Can be optional** | Auto-infer from `np.sort(np.unique(ps))` when `ps` is 1-D and values ∉ `[0, nc)` |
| `coord_cols` | **Can be optional** | Auto-assign by stamps S/T convention: first `(K-1)×... ` columns for spatial axes, last column(s) for depth/time |
| `p_marginal` | **Fully redundant** | Auto-compute from `Pmodel_k[:,:,-1].sum(axis=1)` averaged across components |

With these defaults, the minimal separable call in the notebook becomes:

```python
result_mcp_3d = MCPcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme,
    [dmodel_h, dmodel_v],    # list → separable auto-detected
    [Pmodel_h, Pmodel_v],    # list → separable auto-detected
    nsmax_3d,
    None,                    # dmax → auto_dmax per component
    options={
        'auto_dmax': True,
        'category_codes': LITHO_CODES,   # still needed: codes [1,2,3,4] not [0,1,2,3]
        # coord_cols: auto [[0,1],[2]] from cs.shape=(n,3), K=2
        # p_marginal: auto from Pmodel_h/v far-field
        # mode: 'product' by default
    },
)
```

In the Pingtung notebook, `category_codes` is the only option that cannot be eliminated, because the LithoCode values `[1,2,3,4]` are not 0-indexed. If the data were stored as 0-indexed classes, even that could be dropped.

import numpy as np
from stamps.bme.BMEcatPdf import MCPcatPdf, BMEcatPdf

nc, nd_h, nd_v = 3, 8, 6
np.random.seed(0)
dmodel_h = np.linspace(0, 4000, nd_h)
dmodel_v = np.linspace(0, 100, nd_v)
Pmodel_h = np.ones((nc, nc, nd_h)) / nc
Pmodel_v = np.ones((nc, nc, nd_v)) / nc
for k in range(nd_h):
    np.fill_diagonal(Pmodel_h[:,:,k], 0.4 - 0.3*k/(nd_h-1))
    Pmodel_h[:,:,k] /= Pmodel_h[:,:,k].sum()
for k in range(nd_v):
    np.fill_diagonal(Pmodel_v[:,:,k], 0.4 - 0.3*k/(nd_v-1))
    Pmodel_v[:,:,k] /= Pmodel_v[:,:,k].sum()

# 3D coords: X, Y, Z

All four issues are implemented. Here is a complete summary of every change made:

---

## Changes made

### Issue 1 — Fix out-of-range interpolation errors

**`stamps/stamps/stats/dependence/probatablefit.py`**
- Replaced `scipy.interpolate.interp1d` (raises `ValueError` when distance exceeds table range) with `np.interp` which silently clamps to `[dmodel[0], dmodel[-1]]`. This is physically correct: the Pmodel at its maximum tabulated distance is already at or near the independence product `p(c)·p(c')`.

**`stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py` — `neighbours_separable`**
- Added a pairwise-range compliance check immediately after reading each `dmax_k`: if `dmax_k > dmodel_k[-1] / 2`, it is capped at `dmodel_k[-1] / 2`. This guarantees that any two selected neighbours (both within `dmax_k` of the estimation point) are at most `2×dmax_k ≤ dmodel_k[-1]` apart — so `maxentropytable` never receives an out-of-range pairwise distance.

---

### Issue 2 — Clean separable API + auto-inference

**`stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py`** — three new helpers + refactored entry points:

- **`_p_marginal_from_pmodel(Pmodel)`** — auto-computes `p(c)` from the far-field row sums of any component Pmodel.
- **`_auto_coord_cols(nd, K)`** — assigns coordinate columns by stamps S/T convention: `[[0,1],[2]]` for 3-D XY+Z, etc.
- **`_resolve_pmodel(dmodel, Pmodel, dmax, cs, options)`** — detects separable mode when `dmodel` and `Pmodel` are Python lists, then builds the internal `separable_pmodel` dict. Reads `mode` from `options` (default `'product'`); auto-computes `p_marginal` and `coord_cols` when absent.
- **`_coerce_ps_soft`** — now auto-infers `category_codes` from `np.sort(np.unique(ps))` when `ps` is 1-D with values outside `[0, nc)`.
- **`MCPcatPdf` and `BMEcatPdf`** — both now call `_resolve_pmodel` at entry so list-form inputs work without any `options` key.

```
import time

def station_loocv(method_fn, cs_1d, ck_1d, ps, dmodel, Pmodel,
                  station_ids, categories, nsmax, dmax, options,
                  use_xgb_prior=False, cs_features=None):
    """Station-level LOOCV for any BMEcatPdf-compatible estimator."""
    unique_st = np.unique(station_ids)
    all_post, all_true = [], []
    for st in unique_st:
        tr = station_ids != st
        te = station_ids == st
        ck_te = cs_1d[te]; cs_tr = cs_1d[tr]; ps_tr = ps[tr]; ps_te = ps[te]
        ext = None
        if use_xgb_prior and cs_features is not None:
            ext, _ = BMEcatPrior(
                ck=cs_bme[te], cs=cs_bme[tr], ps=ps_tr,
                ck_features=cs_features[te],
                cs_features=cs_features[tr],
                method='xgboostlss',
                cv_config={'n_trials': 0},
                categories=categories, verbose=False,
                return_details=True,
            )
        post = method_fn(
            ck_te, cs_tr, ps_tr, dmodel, Pmodel,
            nsmax=nsmax, dmax=dmax, categories=categories,
            options=options, external_priors=ext,
        )
        all_post.append(post)
        all_true.append(ps_te)
    post_all = np.vstack(all_post)
    true_all = np.concatenate(all_true)
    cats = np.asarray(categories)
    acc = float(np.mean(cats[np.argmax(post_all, axis=1)] == true_all))
    ti  = np.searchsorted(categories, true_all)
    mll = float(np.mean(np.log(np.clip(
        post_all[np.arange(len(true_all)), ti], 1e-15, None))))
    return acc, mll

print('Running station-level LOOCV (this may take a few minutes)...')

t0 = time.perf_counter()
acc_mcp, mll_mcp = station_loocv(
    MCPcatPdf, cs_1d, ck_1d, ps_bme, dmodel, Pmodel,
    station_ids, LITHO_CODES, nsmax_bme, dmax_bme, bme_opts)
t_mcp = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'MCP done ({t_mcp:.1f} s): acc={acc_mcp:.3f}  mll={mll_mcp:.3f}')

t0 = time.perf_counter()
acc_xgb, mll_xgb = station_loocv(
    BMEcatPdf, cs_1d, ck_1d, ps_bme, dmodel, Pmodel,
    station_ids, LITHO_CODES, nsmax_bme, dmax_bme, bme_opts,
    use_xgb_prior=True, cs_features=X_well)
t_xgb = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'BME+XGBoost done ({t_xgb:.1f} s): acc={acc_xgb:.3f}  mll={mll_xgb:.3f}')
```

The `station_loocv` function passes `categories=categories, external_priors=ext` as keyword arguments directly to `MCPcatPdf`/`BMEcatPdf`, which don't accept those. The fix is to move them into `options` before calling, which is where `category_codes` and `prior_pdf_at_ck` live in the refactored functions.

The problem was that `station_loocv` was passing `categories=categories` and `external_priors=ext` as keyword arguments directly to `MCPcatPdf`/`BMEcatPdf`, which never accepted those parameter names. The fix:

1. **`categories`** → injected as `options['category_codes']` in `base_opts` at the start of the function, so it flows through `options` the way the estimator functions expect it.
2. **`external_priors`** → renamed to `options['prior_pdf_at_ck']` in `fold_opts` when an XGBoost prior is available — again using the correct option key.
3. The call to `method_fn` now uses the standard positional signature `(ck, cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, options=fold_opts)` matching both `MCPcatPdf` and `BMEcatPdf` exactly.
4. LOOCV warnings from XGBoost are also suppressed inside the fold loop using the same `warnings.catch_warnings()` pattern applied to the main LOOCV cell.

```
=== cell 44 [markdown] ===
## 10. BMEcatPdf with XGBoostLSS prior

We inject the prior via &#96;external_priors&#96;.  The Bayes-factor correction is applied automatically inside &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96;:

$$
q_{\text{BF}}(c_k) \propto \frac{p_{\text{prior}}(c_k)}{p_{\text{global}}(c_k)}
\cdot \prod_{s} P(c_s \mid c_k)
$$
```

```
## 10. BMEcatPdf with XGBoostLSS prior

We inject the prior via &#96;external_priors&#96;.  The Bayes-factor correction is applied automatically inside &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96;:

$$
q_{\text{BF}}(c_k) \propto \frac{p_{\text{prior}}(c_k)}{p_{\text{global}}(c_k)}
\cdot \prod_{s} P(c_s \mid c_k)
$$

where $p_{\text{global}}(c_k)$ is automatically derived from the training data marginal proportions.
```

Here is a summary of all changes made and the explanation of the "all-gravel" behavior:

---

**Changes made:**

**Cell 47 (estimation):** Added a third run — `result_bme_uniform_3d` = `BMEcatPdf` without any `prior_pdf_at_ck`. This gives a true "spatial model only" BMEcatPdf baseline. Now there are three results:
- `result_mcp_3d` — MCPcatPdf fast approximation
- `result_bme_uniform_3d` — BMEcatPdf, uniform prior (spatial only)
- `result_bme_3d` — BMEcatPdf, XGBoostLSS prior

**Cell 50 (comparison plot):** Changed from "MCP vs BME+XGB" to **"BME uniform vs BME+XGB"** — both are BMEcatPdf, differing only in prior. Added a printed diagnostic table showing class proportions for the XGB input prior, BME uniform, and BME+XGB at the z = -75 m slice.

**Cells 48/49 (prior maps):** Updated to compare the XGB prior (input) against `result_bme_uniform_3d` (the spatial-only BMEcatPdf), not MCPcatPdf.

---

**Why does BMEcatPdf ignore the XGBoostLSS prior?**

This is expected, not a bug. The ME table inside `BMEcatPdf` computes the joint probability over all neighbors simultaneously. With `nsmax=6` neighbors, if several hard-data points all carry gravel (label = 4), the product of their conditional probabilities:

\[P(c_k \mid c_1=\text{gravel}) \times P(c_k \mid c_2=\text{gravel}) \times \cdots\]

can be orders of magnitude larger for gravel than for any other class, completely overwhelming the prior. The XGB prior only visibly influences the posterior where:
- few neighbors exist (sparse data zone), or
- neighbors carry mixed or soft probabilities

The diagnostic table printed after the plot will confirm this: if "BME uniform" ≈ "BME+XGB" at a depth slice dominated by gravel-label wells, the data is simply too strong for the prior to shift the estimate.
