```json
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# --- START: New ME_dual functions ---",
            "lineNumber": 1059
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1060
          },
          {
            "text": "def _calculate_true_me_pdf(mu, nbiv, nc, ndim, idx):",
            "lineNumber": 1061,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1062
          },
          {
            "text": "    Helper function to calculate the full ME PDF from Lagrange multipliers.",
            "lineNumber": 1063
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1064
          },
          {
            "text": "    This function builds the full, log-linear multivariate PDF table",
            "lineNumber": 1065
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;P(X_0, ..., X_n)&#96; from the set of bivariate multipliers &#96;mu&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1066
          },
          {
            "text": "    It uses the log-sum-exp trick for numerical stability.",
            "lineNumber": 1067
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1068
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 1069
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 1070
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1071
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of all Lagrange multipliers, shape &#96;&#96;(nbiv * nc * nc,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1072
          },
          {
            "text": "    nbiv : int",
            "lineNumber": 1073
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of bivariate constraints.",
            "lineNumber": 1074
          },
          {
            "text": "    nc : int",
            "lineNumber": 1075
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of categories.",
            "lineNumber": 1076
          },
          {
            "text": "    ndim : int",
            "lineNumber": 1077
          },
          {
            "text": "        Total number of dimensions in the full PDF.",
            "lineNumber": 1078
          },
          {
            "text": "    idx : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1079
          },
          {
            "text": "        Array mapping &#96;mu&#96; indices to dimension pairs, shape &#96;&#96;(nbiv, 2)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1080
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1081
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 1082
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 1083
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pfit : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1084
          },
          {
            "text": "        The calculated full multivariate PDF, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, ..., nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1085
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1086
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- START BROADCASTING FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 1087
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_mat = mu.reshape(nbiv, nc, nc) # mu is 1D, reshape to (nbiv, nc, nc)",
            "lineNumber": 1088
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_dict = {tuple(idx[k]): mu_mat[k] for k in range(nbiv)}",
            "lineNumber": 1089
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1090
          },
          {
            "text": "    # P_logits is the sum of all log-linear terms (mu)",
            "lineNumber": 1091
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_logits = np.zeros([nc] * ndim)",
            "lineNumber": 1092
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1093
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Loop over all possible (i, j) pairs, just like GIS/IIS",
            "lineNumber": 1094
          },
          {
            "text": "    for i in range(ndim):",
            "lineNumber": 1095
          },
          {
            "text": "        for j in range(i + 1, ndim):",
            "lineNumber": 1096
          },
          {
            "text": "            # Check if this pair (i, j) has an active constraint",
            "lineNumber": 1097
          },
          {
            "text": "            if (i, j) in mu_dict:",
            "lineNumber": 1098
          },
          {
            "text": "                mu_k = mu_dict[(i, j)]",
            "lineNumber": 1099
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1100
          },
          {
            "text": "                # Create a (1, 1, ..., nc, ..., nc, ..., 1) shape",
            "lineNumber": 1101
          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape = [1] * ndim",
            "lineNumber": 1102
          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape[i] = nc",
            "lineNumber": 1103
          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape[j] = nc",
            "lineNumber": 1104
          },
          {
            "text": "                ",
            "lineNumber": 1105
          },
          {
            "text": "                # Reshape mu[k] and add to P_logits",
            "lineNumber": 1106
          },
          {
            "text": "                mu_broadcast = mu_k.reshape(broadcast_shape)",
            "lineNumber": 1107
          },
          {
            "text": "                P_logits += mu_broadcast",
            "lineNumber": 1108
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- END BROADCASTING FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 1109
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1110
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Pfit is the normalized probability table",
            "lineNumber": 1111
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Use log-sum-exp trick to avoid overflow",
            "lineNumber": 1112
          },
          {
            "text": "    max_logit = np.max(P_logits)",
            "lineNumber": 1113
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_exp = np.exp(P_logits - max_logit)",
            "lineNumber": 1114
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pfit = P_exp / np.sum(P_exp)",
            "lineNumber": 1115
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1116
          },
          {
            "text": "    return Pfit",
            "lineNumber": 1117,
            "isSignature": true
          },

            "lineNumber": 1118

          },
          {
            "text": "def maxentropytable(c, dmodel, Pmodel, options=None):",

          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1330
          },
          {
            "text": "    Estimates the Maximum Entropy multivariate probability table.",

          },

            "text": "    ",

          },
          {
            "text": "    This is the core ME solver. It takes a set of estimation and data",

          },

            "lineNumber": 1334

            "lineNumber": 1336
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1337
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",

          },

            "text": "    ----------",

          },

            "text": "        Typically, &#96;c[0]&#96; is the estimation point.",
            "lineNumber": 1342
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1343
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of distances for &#96;Pmodel&#96;, shape &#96;&#96;(nd,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1344
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1345
          },
          {
            "text": "        3D array of bivariate probability tables, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, nc, nd)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1346
          },
          {
            "text": "    options : dict, optional",
            "lineNumber": 1347
          },
          {
            "text": "        Dictionary of options:",
            "lineNumber": 1348
          },
          {
            "text": "        - 'tol' (float): Stopping criterion for estimators. Default 1e-5.",
            "lineNumber": 1349
          },
          {
            "text": "        - 'estimator' (str): 'MPL', 'MLE_reg', 'GIS', 'IIS', 'ME_dual'.",
            "lineNumber": 1350
          },
          {
            "text": "          Default 'MPL'.",
            "lineNumber": 1351
          },
          {
            "text": "        - 'reg' (float): Regularization for 'MLE_reg' and 'ME_dual'.",
            "lineNumber": 1352
          },
          {
            "text": "          Default 1e-7.",
            "lineNumber": 1353
          },
          {
            "text": "        - 'model_structure' (str): 'full' (all pairs, O(n^2)) or 'knn'",
            "lineNumber": 1354
          },

          },
          {

          },

          {

          },

          },

          },

          {
            "text": "# --- START: New ME_dual functions ---",

          {
```

```json
          },
          {
            "text": "def _calculate_true_me_pdf(mu, nbiv, nc, ndim, idx):",
            "lineNumber": 1061,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1062
          },
          {
            "text": "    Helper function to calculate the full ME PDF from Lagrange multipliers.",
            "lineNumber": 1063
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1064
          },
          {
            "text": "    This function builds the full, log-linear multivariate PDF table",
            "lineNumber": 1065
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;P(X_0, ..., X_n)&#96; from the set of bivariate multipliers &#96;mu&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1066
          },
          {
            "text": "    It uses the log-sum-exp trick for numerical stability.",
            "lineNumber": 1067
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1068
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 1069
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 1070
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1071
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of all Lagrange multipliers, shape &#96;&#96;(nbiv * nc * nc,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1072
          },
          {
            "text": "    nbiv : int",
            "lineNumber": 1073
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of bivariate constraints.",
            "lineNumber": 1074
          },
          {
            "text": "    nc : int",
            "lineNumber": 1075
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of categories.",
            "lineNumber": 1076
          },
          {
            "text": "    ndim : int",
            "lineNumber": 1077
          },
          {
            "text": "        Total number of dimensions in the full PDF.",
            "lineNumber": 1078
          },
          {
            "text": "    idx : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1079
          },
          {
            "text": "        Array mapping &#96;mu&#96; indices to dimension pairs, shape &#96;&#96;(nbiv, 2)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1080
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1081
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 1082
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 1083
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pfit : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1084
          },
          {
            "text": "        The calculated full multivariate PDF, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, ..., nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1085
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1086
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- START BROADCASTING FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 1087
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_mat = mu.reshape(nbiv, nc, nc) # mu is 1D, reshape to (nbiv, nc, nc)",
            "lineNumber": 1088
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_dict = {tuple(idx[k]): mu_mat[k] for k in range(nbiv)}",
            "lineNumber": 1089
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1090
          },
          {
            "text": "    # P_logits is the sum of all log-linear terms (mu)",
            "lineNumber": 1091
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_logits = np.zeros([nc] * ndim)",
            "lineNumber": 1092
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1093
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Loop over all possible (i, j) pairs, just like GIS/IIS",
            "lineNumber": 1094
          },
          {
            "text": "    for i in range(ndim):",
            "lineNumber": 1095
          },
          {
            "text": "        for j in range(i + 1, ndim):",
            "lineNumber": 1096
          },
          {
            "text": "            # Check if this pair (i, j) has an active constraint",
            "lineNumber": 1097
          },
          {
            "text": "            if (i, j) in mu_dict:",
            "lineNumber": 1098
          },
          {
            "text": "                mu_k = mu_dict[(i, j)]",
            "lineNumber": 1099
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1100
          },
          {
            "text": "                # Create a (1, 1, ..., nc, ..., nc, ..., 1) shape",
            "lineNumber": 1101
          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape = [1] * ndim",
            "lineNumber": 1102
          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape[i] = nc",
            "lineNumber": 1103
          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape[j] = nc",
            "lineNumber": 1104
          },
          {
            "text": "                ",
            "lineNumber": 1105
          },
          {
            "text": "                # Reshape mu[k] and add to P_logits",
            "lineNumber": 1106
          },
          {
            "text": "                mu_broadcast = mu_k.reshape(broadcast_shape)",
            "lineNumber": 1107
          },
          {
            "text": "                P_logits += mu_broadcast",
            "lineNumber": 1108
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- END BROADCASTING FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 1109
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1110
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Pfit is the normalized probability table",
            "lineNumber": 1111
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Use log-sum-exp trick to avoid overflow",
            "lineNumber": 1112
          },
          {
            "text": "    max_logit = np.max(P_logits)",
            "lineNumber": 1113
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_exp = np.exp(P_logits - max_logit)",

            "text": "    Pfit = P_exp / np.sum(P_exp)",

          },

            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1116
          },
          {
            "text": "    return Pfit",

            "isSignature": true

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "        ",

          },
          {
            "text": "    elif estimator == 'IIS':",

          },
          {
            "text": "        # Build the sparse Pbiv table for GIS/IIS",

          },
          {
            "text": "        Pbiv = [[[] for _ in range(ndim)] for _ in range(ndim)]",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "            Pbiv[i][j] = Pbiv_table",

          },
          {
            "text": "        Pfit, niter = iterativerescaling_IIS(Pbiv, tol)",

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "    elif estimator == 'ME_dual': ",

          },
```

Here is a detailed investigation of why BMEcatPdf pushes estimates toward gravel while MCPcatPdf gives more reasonable results.

## Root Cause: The Maximum Entropy Table Amplifies the Dominant Class

The fundamental difference between the two methods lies in **how they combine spatial information from multiple neighbours**.

### MCPcatPdf: Independent Products (Multiplicative, Log-Space)

MCPcatPdf makes a **conditional independence assumption**. Its posterior is:

$$\log P(c \mid \text{data}) = \log q_\text{eff}(c) - n \cdot \log p_\text{dc}(c) + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \log \Big(\sum_i P_\text{biv}(X_k{=}i,\, X_0{=}c) \cdot \text{data}_k(i)\Big)$$

Each neighbour contributes **independently** via a single bivariate table lookup. Cross-neighbour correlations are ignored. The result is a simple log-sum over `n` independent terms.

### BMEcatPdf: Full Maximum Entropy Joint Table

BMEcatPdf builds a **full `nc^(n+1)` joint probability table** via `maxentropytable`, then multiplies by the marginal data vectors via `producttablepdf`. The key lines are:

```1848:1868:stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py
Pkh_,niter = maxentropytable(np.vstack((ck0,cslocal)),
                             dmodel,
                             Pmodel,
                             options=options)
// ...
Pkh = producttablepdf(Pkh_,np.vstack((prior_to_use,pslocal))) 
```

The ME table `Pkh_` has shape `(4, 4, 4, ..., 4)` — one axis per point (estimation + neighbours). Then `producttablepdf` multiplies each axis by its marginal (prior for axis 0, hard-data one-hot for axes 1..n).

**Here is the critical structural issue:**

## The ME Table's Implicit Marginal Amplification

The ME table solved by `maxentropytable` is built from bivariate constraints derived from `Pmodel`. For the Pingtung dataset:

1. **Gravel dominates the global marginal** (`p_bg ≈ 0.4–0.5` for gravel vs 0.1–0.2 for others).

2. The ME table's structure encodes this marginal in **every axis**. Each axis marginal of the fitted ME table converges to approximately `p_global(c)`. So the "prior" baked into the ME table already favours gravel on every dimension.

3. When `producttablepdf` multiplies the ME table by `(prior_to_use, pslocal)`, the `prior_to_use` for the estimation point (axis 0) is:

```1814:1821:stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py
needs_bf = (_q_ext is not None) or (_use_local_marginal and _p_local_k is not None)
if needs_bf:
    _bf = _q_eff / _global_marginal
    _bf = np.clip(_bf, 1e-15, None)
    prior_to_use = _bf / _bf.sum()
else:
    prior_to_use = _q_eff   # uniform — no BF needed
```

For Case B (`local_marginal` only, no XGBoost), `_q_eff = _p_local_k`, so:

$$\texttt{prior\_to\_use} = \frac{p_\text{local}}{p_\text{global}} \cdot (\text{normalised})$$

This BF correction is designed to **cancel** the `p_global` baked into the ME table's axis-0 marginal. In theory, the net effect on axis 0 should be `p_local`.

**However, the problem is on axes 1 through n (the neighbour axes).**

## The n-Fold Marginal Amplification Problem

For **hard data** neighbours (one-hot encoding), `pslocal[k, :] = [0, 0, 0, 1]` (e.g., gravel). When `producttablepdf` multiplies:

```1571:1574:stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py
for i in range(ndim):
  expand_shape = [1] * ndim
  expand_shape[i] = nc
  Pprod *= pdf[i,:].reshape(expand_shape)
```

For each hard-data neighbour `k` that is gravel, this slices axis `k` to keep only the `c=gravel` slice. Then marginalization over axes 1..n (line 1873) sums the remaining `nc^n` sub-cube down to the axis-0 marginal.

The crucial insight: **in the ME table, the correlation structure between all pairs of neighbours encodes redundant information about the global marginal**. When you have `n` neighbours that are all gravel (which is the most common class), the ME table's `nc^(n+1)` joint assigns very high joint probability to the "all gravel" configuration. After conditioning on all-gravel data and marginalising, the estimation point gets overwhelmingly pushed toward gravel.

Compare this to MCP where each neighbour contributes a **single** `log sum_term` — there is no joint correlation between the neighbours to amplify the effect.

## Why MCPcatPdf Avoids This

In MCPcatPdf, each gravel neighbour contributes:

$$\log\!\Big(\underbrace{P_\text{biv}(\text{gravel}, c)}_{\text{one table lookup per class } c}\Big)$$

These are independent additive terms in log-space. A gravel neighbour at distance `d` contributes the same amount regardless of whether the other neighbours are also gravel. **There is no cross-neighbour amplification.**

In BMEcatPdf, the ME joint table captures pairwise correlations **between neighbours** (all `n(n+1)/2` pairs). When all `n` neighbours are the same class, the conditional-independence-violating correlation terms constructively reinforce, creating a much stronger push toward that class than any individual bivariate relationship would suggest.

## Quantitative Illustration

With `nsmax=6` and `nc=4`, the ME table has shape `(4,4,4,4,4,4,4)` = 4^7 = 16,384 entries. The MPL estimator fits Lagrange multipliers for all `7*6/2 = 21` pairwise constraints. When 5 out of 6 neighbours are gravel (common in this dataset), the ME table's joint probability on the `(c, gravel, gravel, gravel, gravel, gravel, gravel)` configurations is very high for `c=gravel` due to the multiplicative pairwise reinforcement:

$$P_\text{ME}(c_0, c_1, \ldots, c_6) \propto \exp\!\Bigg(\sum_{0\le i<j\le 6} \mu_{ij}(c_i, c_j)\Bigg)$$

The `μ_{ij}` terms all "agree" that gravel is likely, and these sum constructively across all 21 pairs.

## Why `p_local` and the BF Correction Are Insufficient

The BF correction (`prior_to_use = q_eff / p_global`) only modifies **axis 0** (the estimation point). It does not touch axes 1..n. The global marginal is still baked into every neighbour axis of the ME table. When all neighbours happen to be gravel, this embedded marginal on each neighbour axis reinforces the gravel dominance.

The `p_local` kernel smoothing helps in MCPcatPdf because the prior term `log q_eff(c) - n log p_dc(c)` directly scales the baseline. But in BMEcatPdf, the ME table is a **nonlinear** object — modifying only the prior (axis 0 marginal) cannot fully counteract the correlation-induced amplification across all other axes.

## Summary

| Aspect | MCPcatPdf | BMEcatPdf |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| **Neighbour interaction** | Independent (log-additive) | Fully correlated (ME joint) |
| **n gravel neighbours** | n × log(P_biv(gravel,c)) | Reinforced by n(n-1)/2 inter-neighbour correlations |
| **Dominant-class amplification** | Linear in n | Super-linear (pairwise terms compound) |
| **BF correction scope** | Modifies the entire prior term | Only modifies axis 0 of the nc^(n+1) table |

**The core problem is that BMEcatPdf's ME joint table inherently amplifies the dominant class through pairwise correlation terms between neighbours, and this amplification cannot be offset by a prior correction that only acts on the estimation point's axis.** When the data are sparse and gravel-dominated, this structural amplification overwhelms the local-marginal or composite prior adjustments.

### Possible Mitigations

1. **Reduce `nsmax`**: Fewer neighbours means fewer pairwise reinforcement terms (from 21 pairs at nsmax=6 to 6 pairs at nsmax=3). This directly reduces the dominant-class amplification.

2. **Use `model_structure='knn'`** in options: Instead of building all `n(n+1)/2` pairwise constraints, only use k-nearest-neighbour pairs. This reduces the cross-neighbour correlation coupling.

3. **Increase `reg`** (regularisation in the ME solver): Higher regularisation shrinks the Lagrange multipliers `μ_ij` toward zero, weakening the pairwise correlations and making BMEcatPdf behave more like MCPcatPdf.

4. **Use MCPcatPdf as the primary estimator**: Given the data sparsity and class imbalance, the independence assumption in MCPcatPdf appears to be more appropriate than the full BME joint model.

import json

NB_PATH = '/Users/hdragon689/Documents/MyDoc_iCloud/packages/stamps/stamps_v3/examples/pingtung_lithology/pingtung_lithology_workflow.ipynb'

diag_source = """\
# ── Diagnostic: 3 Z=-15 locations where MCPcatPdf and BMEcatPdf disagree ──────
from stamps.bme.BMEcatPdf import (
    _coerce_ps_soft, _resolve_pmodel,
    _find_effective_range, neighbours_separable,
)
from stamps.stats.dependence.probatablefit import probamodel2bitable_separable

# --- Reconstruct the separable config used inside BMEcatPdf/MCPcatPdf ----------
cs_f = np.asarray(cs_bme, dtype=float)
sep_diag, _, _, _ = _resolve_pmodel(
    [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel], None, cs_f, bme_opts_3d)

_thresh = bme_opts_3d.get('auto_dmax_threshold', 0.05)
for _co in sep_diag['components']:
    _co['dmax'] = _find_effective_range(_co['dmodel'], _co['Pmodel'], threshold=_thresh)

ps_soft = _coerce_ps_soft(ps_bme, nc, bme_opts_3d)
_p_marg = np.asarray(sep_diag.get('p_marginal'), dtype=float)
_p_marg = _p_marg / _p_marg.sum()

print('Separable dmax (applied inside neighbours_separable):')
for _co in sep_diag['components']:
    print(f"  cols={_co['coord_cols']}  dmax={_co['dmax']:.1f}")

# --- Find Z=-15 locations where MCP MAP ≠ BME-local MAP -----------------------
z_diag  = -15.0
mask_z15 = np.abs(ck_bme[:, 2] - z_diag) < 1.0
idx_z15  = np.where(mask_z15)[0]

disagree = idx_z15[map_mcp[idx_z15] != map_bme_loc[idx_z15]]
print(f'\\nGrid nodes at Z={z_diag:.0f} m: {len(idx_z15)}')
print(f'Nodes where MCP != BME-local:   {len(disagree)}')

if len(disagree) < 3:
    print('Fewer than 3 disagreeing nodes; showing all.')
    chosen = disagree
else:
    chosen = disagree[np.round(np.linspace(0, len(disagree)-1, 3)).astype(int)]

# --- For each chosen location: retrieve neighbours and print table -------------
lbl_map = dict(zip(LITHO_CODES, LITHO_LABELS))

for loc_idx in chosen:
    ck0 = ck_bme[[loc_idx], :]
    x0, y0, z0 = ck0[0, 0], ck0[0, 1], ck0[0, 2]

    csub, Zsub, dsub, nsub, sltidx, d_comp, p_local = neighbours_separable(
        ck0, cs_f, ps_soft, nsmax_3d,
        sep_diag['components'],
        options=bme_opts_3d,
        p_marginal=_p_marg,
        mode=sep_diag.get('mode', 'product'),
    )

    mcp_class = lbl_map[int(map_mcp[loc_idx])]
    bme_l_class = lbl_map[int(map_bme_loc[loc_idx])]
    bme_x_class = lbl_map[int(map_bme_xgb[loc_idx])]

    print(f'\\n{"="*72}')
    print(f'Location idx={loc_idx}  X={x0:.0f}  Y={y0:.0f}  Z={z0:.1f} m')
    print(f'  MCP+local MAP: {mcp_class:<12}  '
          f'BME+local MAP: {bme_l_class:<12}  '
          f'BME+composite MAP: {bme_x_class}')
    print(f'  Neighbours found: {nsub}')

    if p_local is not None:
        p_str = '  '.join(f'{l}={v:.3f}' for l, v in zip(LITHO_LABELS, p_local))
        print(f'  p_local: [{p_str}]')
    else:
        print('  p_local: None (no candidates in range)')

    if nsub == 0:
        print('  (no neighbours found)')
        continue

    # Compute TV score per neighbour
    _dms = [_co['dmodel'] for _co in sep_diag['components']]
    _Pms = [_co['Pmodel'] for _co in sep_diag['components']]
    _P_indep = np.outer(_p_marg, _p_marg)

    rows = []
    for k in range(nsub):
        _dvec = d_comp[k, :]
        _P3d  = probamodel2bitable_separable(_dvec, _dms, _Pms, _p_marg,
                                              mode=sep_diag.get('mode','product'))
        _tv   = 0.5 * np.abs(_P3d - _P_indep).sum()
        _class = lbl_map.get(LITHO_CODES[int(np.argmax(Zsub[k]))], '?')
        rows.append((_class, _dvec[0], _dvec[1], csub[k,2], _tv))

    print(f'\\n  {"#":>2}  {"Class":<10}  {"d_horiz(km)":>11}  {"d_vert(m)":>9}  {"TV":>6}  Z_data(m)')
    print(f'  {"-"*62}')
    for k, (cls, dh, dv, zk, tv) in enumerate(rows):
        print(f'  {k:2d}  {cls:<10}  {dh/1e3:>11.3f}  {abs(dv):>9.1f}  {tv:>6.3f}  {zk:.1f}')
    print(f'{"="*72}')

## Prerequisites — run these cells first

Then run **cell 21** (the diagnostic).

## Practical steps in Jupyter

1. **Open the notebook** `examples/pingtung_lithology/pingtung_lithology_workflow.ipynb` in JupyterLab or VS Code.

2. **Run all cells up to and including cell 20** — the easiest way is:
   - Use **Run → Run All Above Selected Cell** with cell 20 selected, or
   - `Shift+Enter` through cells 1 → 20 sequentially, or
   - `Kernel → Restart & Run All` if you want a clean state (note: this will also run cells 21 onwards if you don't stop it).

3. **Run cell 21** with `Shift+Enter`. You will see output like:

```
Separable dmax applied inside neighbours_separable:
  cols=[0 1]  dmax=10500.0
  cols=[2]    dmax=42.3

Grid nodes at Z=-15 m : 320
Nodes where MCP != BME-local  : 47

========================================================================

  MCP+local  : Fine sand
  BME+local  : Gravel
  BME+compos.: Gravel
  Neighbours : 5

   #  Class        d_horiz(km)   d_vert(m)      TV  Z_data(m)
  ------------------------------------------------------------
   0  Gravel             3.512       2.1   0.431  -17.1
   1  Gravel             4.801       5.0   0.387  -10.0
   ...
========================================================================
```

## What to look for in the output

**1. `p_local` vs the neighbour classes**
Check whether `p_local` reflects the actual neighbourhood. If most neighbours are gravel yet `p_local[Gravel]` is high, the kernel smoothing is working correctly. If `p_local[Gravel]` is lower than the neighbour fraction, it means distant non-gravel data are pulling the kernel average.

**2. `d_horiz` and `d_vert` of the neighbours**
These tell you whether the neighbours are within the effective range. If all neighbours are near the `dmax` boundary (e.g. 9–10 km horizontally), they carry very little structural information (low TV score) and the estimation falls back mainly toward the prior.

**3. TV score column**
Higher TV = neighbour is more correlated with the estimation point = more influential. If all TV scores are low (< 0.1), no neighbour is very informative and the result is driven almost entirely by the prior.

**4. Comparing MCP vs BME behaviour**
- MCP uses each neighbour **independently** (log-additive) — a single gravel neighbour with TV=0.43 tilts the result toward gravel proportionally.
- BME builds a **joint table** over all neighbours simultaneously — if multiple neighbours are gravel, their pairwise correlations amplify the gravel signal super-linearly. This is what the diagnosis is revealing.

## If cell 21 raises a NameError

That means a prerequisite cell was not run. The most commonly skipped ones are:
- `map_mcp`, `map_bme_loc`, `map_bme_xgb` — require cell 20
- `dmodel_h`, `Pmodel_h` — require cell 11
- `bme_opts_3d`, `nsmax_3d` — require cell 15

Just run the missing cell and re-run cell 21.

Now I have the full picture. Let me explain the issue clearly.

---

## What the current code does and why it's problematic

**Current approach (cell 11)** — vertical aggregation before horizontal analysis:

```python
for k, uid in enumerate(unique_keys):
    mask = station_ids == uid
    station_xy[k] = wells.loc[mask, ['X', 'Y']].values[0]
    for ci, c in enumerate(LITHO_CODES):
        station_ind[k, ci] = np.mean(wells.loc[mask, 'LithoCode'] == c)  # ← average over ALL Z
```

This collapses each borehole's entire depth profile into **a single soft-indicator vector** (the depth-averaged class proportions), then pairs those station-level vectors horizontally. Every inter-station pair at every distance bin gets the same mixed indicator regardless of depth. The resulting Pmodel is a horizontal transition structure for the **vertically averaged** geology, not for any specific stratigraphic layer.

This is problematic because:
1. It mixes lithology from shallow alluvial fans (gravel-dominated) with deep marine deposits (clay-dominated) into a single vector.
2. A pair of stations where one is entirely gravel and another is entirely clay gets averaged to `[0.5, 0.5]` at both ends — producing a near-flat off-diagonal table that underestimates horizontal correlation.
3. The Pmodel fed into the separable 3-D BME effectively has no depth discrimination in its horizontal component.

---

## What the revised approach should do

For each **Z-level** (depth slice), collect only the data rows whose Z falls within a tolerance band of that level, then compute horizontal pairs **from those rows only** — so each pair represents two boreholes sampled at the **same depth**. The transition table then reflects horizontal lithological continuity at that specific depth. Finally, pool the pairs across all Z-levels to build one overall horizontal Pmodel.

The key change is using `wells['Z']` to group rows into Z-levels, then calling `probatablecalc` on the XY coordinates of rows from the **same Z-level** (using `group_ids` to enforce same-level pairs, or simply by looping and accumulating).

---

## Concrete implementation plan

### Option A — Z-level slicing with pooled `probatablecalc`

For each unique Z-level `z_k`, select rows within ±Δz/2 of `z_k`, take their `(X, Y)` and one-hot indicators, and call `probatablecalc`. Then **sum** the raw pair counts `O` and weighted `P × O` across levels before dividing.

```python
# Step 1: find unique Z-levels (1 m spacing from the data)
z_unique = np.sort(wells['Z'].unique())   # e.g. 0, -2, -4, ..., -300 m

# Step 2: build XY coords + one-hot for all rows
xy_all   = wells[['X', 'Y']].values
code_all = wells['LithoCode'].values.astype(int)
cats_arr = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)
ind_all  = (code_all[:, None] == cats_arr[None, :]).astype(float)

# Step 3: adaptive bins on all XY (same d_max_h)
coord_limit_h = adaptive_bins(xy_all, n_bins=n_bins_h, d_max=d_max_h,
                               method='equal_pairs')

# Step 4: pool across Z-levels
PO_sum = np.zeros((nc, nc, n_bins_h + 1))  # weighted P×O accumulator
O_sum  = np.zeros(n_bins_h + 1)

for z_k in z_unique:
    mask_z = wells['Z'].values == z_k       # exact match (integer levels)
    if mask_z.sum() < 2:
        continue                            # need at least 2 boreholes at this level
    D_k, P_k, O_k = probatablecalc(
        xy_all[mask_z], ind_all[mask_z], coord_limit_h)
    valid = O_k > 0
    PO_sum[:, :, valid] += P_k[:, :, valid] * O_k[valid]
    O_sum[valid] += O_k[valid]

# Step 5: recover pooled average P
D_emp_h = coord_limit_h  # or compute mean distances separately
P_emp_h = np.where(O_sum > 0, PO_sum / O_sum, np.nan)
O_emp_h = O_sum
```

This is the most natural approach and reuses `probatablecalc` exactly as for the vertical model.

### Option B — Use `group_ids` within a single `probatablecalc` call

If you define `group_ids` as the Z-level bin for each row, `probatablecalc` will restrict pairs to same-Z-level ones, pooling across levels automatically in one call:

```python
xy_all     = wells[['X', 'Y']].values
group_ids  = wells['Z'].values.astype(str)   # each depth value is its own group

D_emp_h, P_emp_h, O_emp_h = probatablecalc(
    xy_all, ind_all, coord_limit_h, group_ids=group_ids)
```

This is the **simplest change** — just two extra lines and passing `group_ids`. The `group_ids` mechanism already exists in `probatablecalc` (line 542 in the docstring above) and does exactly this: only pairs sharing the same group ID contribute.

**Option B is the recommended approach** — it requires only adding `group_ids=wells['Z'].values.astype(str)` to the existing `probatablecalc` call in cell 11, and removing the station-averaging loop since you now pass all rows directly rather than station-aggregated vectors.

### Implication for anisotropy (cell 12)

The `polar_ptable_map` call in cell 12 also uses `station_xy` and `station_ind`. With the per-Z revision, you would pass `xy_all` (all rows' XY) and `ind_all` (all rows' one-hot) to `polar_ptable_map` with the same `group_ids` passed as a filter, or loop per Z-level. However, `polar_ptable_map` does not currently accept `group_ids` — so for the anisotropy analysis, looping per Z-level and pooling directional tables would be needed.

### Variables affected downstream

| Variable | Currently from | After revision |
|----------|---------------|----------------|
| `station_xy` | 52-row station average | Still needed for pair diagnostic display only |
| `station_ind` | depth-averaged | No longer used for Pmodel |
| `p_bg` | `station_ind.mean()` | Should be `ind_all.mean(axis=0)` (all rows) |
| `D_emp_h`, `P_emp_h`, `O_emp_h` | station-level | Z-level-restricted pairs |
| `dmodel_h`, `Pmodel_h` | fitted from above | refitted from new tables |

---

The change is clean. Here is a summary of exactly what changed and why nothing downstream breaks:

**What changed in cell 11:**

| | Before | After |
|--|--------|-------|
| Input to `probatablecalc` | `station_xy` (52 rows, depth-averaged) | `xy_all` (7913 rows, all depth samples) |
| Indicators | `station_ind` (depth-averaged fractions) | `ind_all = ps_onehot` (one-hot per sample) |
| Pairs allowed | All inter-station pairs | Same-Z-level pairs only via `group_ids=z_group_ids` |

**What was kept unchanged:**
- `station_xy` / `station_ind` — still computed, still used by cell 12 (anisotropy with `polar_ptable_map`)
- `p_bg` — still from `station_ind.mean()`, still used as the marginal for the separable model
- `pair_distance_diagnostic` on `station_xy` — still used for `d_max_h`
- `adaptive_bins` on `station_xy` — inter-station distances are the right range for bin edges
- `dmodel_h`, `Pmodel_h` — still produced by `build_pmodel`, all downstream cells unchanged

**What this produces:**
The new `probatablecalc` call pairs, for example, a gravel sample at `(X₁, Y₁, Z=-20)` with a clay sample at `(X₂, Y₂, Z=-20)` from a different borehole. These are genuine within-layer horizontal transitions. With 7913 samples across many Z-levels, the total pair count will be substantially larger than the 52-station version, giving much better-populated bins especially at short ranges.

```
### CELL 0 (markdown) ###
# Pingtung Lithology Estimation — BMEcatPdf Workflow

This notebook demonstrates a complete **categorical BME** workflow for 3-D
lithology estimation in the Pingtung alluvial plain (Taiwan).  The four
lithology classes are:

| Code | Class | Colour |
|------|-------|--------|
| 1 | Clay | Brown |
| 2 | Fine sand | Sandy |
| 3 | Sand | Gold |
| 4 | Gravel | Steel blue |

**Workflow**: data overview — vertical and horizontal Pmodel fitting —
anisotropy analysis — separable 3-D Pmodel — XGBoostLSS prior —
BMEcatPdf estimation — LOOCV evaluation.

### CELL 1 (code) ###
import sys, os, time, warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap
from scipy.spatial.distance import pdist, cdist

HERE = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname('.'))
REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, '..', '..'))
if REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)

from stamps.bme.BMEcatPdf import BMEcatPdf, MCPcatPdf
from stamps.stest.BMEcatPrior import BMEcatPrior, BMEcatPriorLOOCV
from stamps.stats.dependence.probatablecalc import (
    normalize_indicators, probatablecalc, adaptive_bins,
    pair_distance_diagnostic, probatablecalc_directional,
)
from stamps.stats.dependence.probatablefit import build_pmodel
from stamps.stats.dependence.anisotropy import (
    _ptable_range, polar_ptable_map,
    estimate_anisotropy_from_ptables, isotropy_test_categorical,
)

LITHO_CODES  = [1, 2, 3, 4]
LITHO_LABELS = ['Clay', 'Fine sand', 'Sand', 'Gravel']
LITHO_COLORS = ['#8B4513', '#F4A460', '#FFD700', '#4682B4']
LITHO_CMAP   = ListedColormap(LITHO_COLORS)
nc = len(LITHO_CODES)

DATA_DIR = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'data')
print('Imports OK  |  Data directory:', DATA_DIR)

### CELL 2 (markdown) ###
## 1. Data loading and statistics

Three CSV files: **wells** (borehole hard data for BME), **training** (XGBoost
corpus), and **estimation grid** (3-D prediction locations at 5 depth levels).

### CELL 3 (code) ###
wells    = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'pingtung_wells.csv'))
train_df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'pingtung_training.csv'))
grid_df  = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'pingtung_estimation_grid.csv'))

station_ids = (wells['X'].astype(str) + '_' + wells['Y'].astype(str)).values
n_wells = len(np.unique(station_ids))

print(f'Wells:           {wells.shape[0]:,} depth samples from {n_wells} boreholes')
print(f'Training corpus: {train_df.shape[0]:,} rows (for XGBoostLSS)')
print(f'Estimation grid: {grid_df.shape[0]:,} nodes')
print(f'Depth range:     {wells["Z"].min():.0f} to {wells["Z"].max():.0f} m')
print(f'Grid Z levels:   {sorted(grid_df["Z"].round(0).unique())}')
print()
print('Class distribution:')
for code_val, label in zip(LITHO_CODES, LITHO_LABELS):
    n = (wells['LithoCode'] == code_val).sum()
    print(f'  {label:12s}  {n:5d}  ({100*n/len(wells):.1f}%)')

### CELL 4 (code) ###
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

ax = axes[0]
for c, lbl, col in zip(LITHO_CODES, LITHO_LABELS, LITHO_COLORS):
    m = wells['LithoCode'] == c
    ax.scatter(wells.loc[m, 'X'], wells.loc[m, 'Z'],
               c=col, label=lbl, s=4, alpha=0.6)
ax.set_xlabel('Easting (m)'); ax.set_ylabel('Depth Z (m)')
ax.set_title('Cross-section: lithology vs easting')
ax.legend(fontsize=8, markerscale=3)

ax2 = axes[1]
well_lengths = wells.groupby(station_ids)['Z'].apply(lambda z: z.max() - z.min())
well_xy = wells.groupby(station_ids)[['X', 'Y']].first()
ax2.scatter(well_xy['X'], well_xy['Y'],
            s=10 + well_lengths.values / 2, c='steelblue',
            edgecolors='k', linewidths=0.3, alpha=0.7)
ax2.set_xlabel('Easting (m)'); ax2.set_ylabel('Northing (m)')
ax2.set_title(f'Borehole locations (n={n_wells}, size ~ depth range)')
ax2.set_aspect('equal')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

### CELL 5 (markdown) ###
## 2. Data overview — depth slices

Plan-view maps of borehole lithology at three representative depths.

### CELL 6 (code) ###
z_targets = [-15, -75, -150]
dz = 5.0

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 5))
for ax, zt in zip(axes, z_targets):
    near = np.abs(wells['Z'].values - zt) &lt;= dz
    for c, lbl, col in zip(LITHO_CODES, LITHO_LABELS, LITHO_COLORS):
        m = near &amp; (wells['LithoCode'].values == c)
        ax.scatter(wells.loc[m, 'X'], wells.loc[m, 'Y'],
                   c=col, s=30, label=lbl, edgecolors='k', linewidths=0.3)
    ax.set_title(f'Z = {zt} m  (n = {near.sum()})', fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xlabel('Easting (m)'); ax.set_ylabel('Northing (m)')
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
axes[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper left')
plt.suptitle('Borehole lithology at three depth levels', fontsize=12, y=1.01)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

### CELL 7 (markdown) ###
## 3. Vertical transition-probability model

Fit a 1-D Pmodel on within-borehole vertical pairs using &#96;adaptive_bins&#96;
(equal-pair binning) and &#96;build_pmodel&#96; (kernel smoothing + regularisation).

### CELL 8 (code) ###
cs_1d = wells[['Z']].values
cats_arr = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)
y_well = wells['LithoCode'].values.astype(int)
ps_onehot = (y_well[:, None] == cats_arr[None, :]).astype(float)
borehole_ids = station_ids

n_bins_v, d_max_v = 40, 80.0
coord_limit_v = adaptive_bins(cs_1d, n_bins=n_bins_v, d_max=d_max_v,
                              method='equal_pairs')
D_emp, P_emp, O_emp = probatablecalc(
    cs_1d, ps_onehot, coord_limit_v, group_ids=borehole_ids)

dmodel, Pmodel, pmodel_info = build_pmodel(
    D_emp, P_emp, O_emp,
    n_fit=80, n_bins=n_bins_v, d_max_emp=d_max_v,
    regularize=True, verbose=True)

print(f'Vertical Pmodel: dmodel {dmodel[0]:.1f} - {dmodel[-1]:.1f} m, shape {Pmodel.shape}')

### CELL 9 (code) ###
valid_v = ~np.isnan(D_emp[1:])
D_v  = D_emp[1:][valid_v]
P_v  = P_emp[:, :, 1:][:, :, valid_v]
O_v  = O_emp[1:][valid_v]
sz_v = 15 + 40 * (np.log1p(O_v) / np.log1p(O_v.max()))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(nc, nc, figsize=(14, 12), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for i in range(nc):
    for j in range(nc):
        ax = axes[i, j]
        col = LITHO_COLORS[j] if i != j else LITHO_COLORS[i]
        emp = P_v[i, j, :]
        ok = ~np.isnan(emp)
        ax.scatter(D_v[ok], emp[ok], s=sz_v[ok], color=col,
                   edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.2, alpha=0.65, zorder=3)
        ax.plot(dmodel, Pmodel[i, j, :], color=col,
                lw=1.5, ls='-' if i == j else '--', zorder=4)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 0.5); ax.grid(True, alpha=0.25)
        if i == 0: ax.set_title(LITHO_LABELS[j], fontsize=10, color=col)
        if j == 0: ax.set_ylabel(LITHO_LABELS[i], fontsize=9, color=LITHO_COLORS[i])
        if i == nc - 1: ax.set_xlabel('Vertical sep. (m)', fontsize=8)
fig.suptitle('Vertical Pmodel - 4x4 transition-probability matrix\n'
             '(circles = empirical, lines = fitted)', fontsize=11)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

### CELL 10 (markdown) ###
## 4. Horizontal Pmodel and anisotropy analysis

Station-level soft indicators (mean class proportions per borehole) are used
for horizontal lag estimation.  Directional analysis reveals horizontal
anisotropy via &#96;polar_ptable_map&#96; and &#96;estimate_anisotropy_from_ptables&#96;.

### CELL 11 (code) ###
unique_keys = np.unique(station_ids)
n_stations = len(unique_keys)

for k, uid in enumerate(unique_keys):

    station_xy[k] = wells.loc[mask, ['X', 'Y']].values[0]
    for ci, c in enumerate(LITHO_CODES):

p_bg = station_ind.mean(axis=0)

_, suggested_dmax_h, _ = pair_distance_diagnostic(

d_max_h = suggested_dmax_h
n_bins_h = 12
print(f'Suggested horizontal d_max: {d_max_h/1e3:.1f} km')

# --- Horizontal Pmodel: per-Z-level pairs (Option B) -------------------------
# Pass all individual depth samples to probatablecalc with group_ids set to

# empirical tables, so the Pmodel reflects within-layer horizontal transitions
# rather than the depth-averaged geology.
xy_all      = wells[['X', 'Y']].values          # (n_rows, 2) — duplicate XY per borehole
ind_all     = ps_onehot                          # (n_rows, nc) one-hot from cell 8
z_group_ids = wells['Z'].values.astype(str)      # group label = depth value

coord_limit_h = adaptive_bins(station_xy, n_bins=n_bins_h, d_max=d_max_h,

D_emp_h, P_emp_h, O_emp_h = probatablecalc(
    xy_all, ind_all, coord_limit_h, group_ids=z_group_ids)

print(f'\nHorizontal Pmodel (per-Z pairs):')

coord_limit_aniso = adaptive_bins(station_xy, n_bins=n_bins_h,

ang_step = np.pi / 6
angLag = np.arange(-np.pi/2, np.pi/2, ang_step)
angTol = np.full_like(angLag, ang_step / 2)

rLag = np.linspace(0.2 * d_max_h, d_max_h, 6)

for ax in axes:
    ax.set_ylabel('P(same class)'); ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[0].set_title('Vertical self-transition')

### CELL 14 (markdown) ###
## 5. Separable 3-D Pmodel (product mode)

The vertical and horizontal Pmodels are composed via a Markov-chain product:
$P_{3D}(a,b \mid \Delta h, \Delta z) = P_H \, D^{-1} \, P_V$
where $D = \mathrm{diag}(p)$.  Passing &#96;dmodel&#96; and &#96;Pmodel&#96; as **lists** to
&#96;MCPcatPdf&#96; / &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; activates separable mode automatically.

### CELL 15 (code) ###

    _ptable_range(dmodel, Pmodel[i, i, :], p_bg[i]**2) for i in range(nc)])
w_v = p_bg[~np.isnan(a_max_v_per_class)]
a_max_v = float(np.dot(a_max_v_per_class[~np.isnan(a_max_v_per_class)],
                        w_v / w_v.sum()))

cs_bme = wells[['X', 'Y', 'Z']].values
ck_bme = grid_df[['X', 'Y', 'Z']].values
ps_bme = y_well

nsmax_3d = 8

    'auto_dmax':         True,

}

## 6. XGBoostLSS prior estimation

Train a Dirichlet-output XGBoostLSS model to predict class probabilities at
the estimation grid.  The prior is later combined with the local marginal as
a composite prior in BMEcatPdf.

### CELL 17 (code) ###
def build_features(df):
    d = df.copy()
    d = d.assign(Z=-d['Z'])
    basin_dummies = pd.get_dummies(d['Basin'], prefix='Basin')
    d = pd.concat([d.drop(columns=['Basin']), basin_dummies], axis=1)
    exclude = {'X', 'Y', 'LithoCode'}
    feat_cols = [c for c in d.columns if c not in exclude]
    return d[feat_cols].values.astype(float), feat_cols

X_train, feat_names = build_features(train_df)
X_well, _ = build_features(wells)

basin_cols = [c for c in feat_names if c.startswith('Basin_')]

grid_dummies = pd.get_dummies(grid_tmp['Basin'], prefix='Basin')
grid_tmp = pd.concat([grid_tmp.drop(columns=['Basin']), grid_dummies], axis=1)
for bc in basin_cols:
    if bc not in grid_tmp.columns:
        grid_tmp[bc] = 0
grid_feat_cols = ['Z','Height','Formation Factor','inResModel',
    'Testing_Distance','Corner_Distance_1','Corner_Distance_2',
    'Corner_Distance_3'] + basin_cols
grid_tmp = grid_tmp.assign(Z=-grid_tmp['Z'])
X_grid = grid_tmp[[c for c in grid_feat_cols
                    if c in grid_tmp.columns]].values.astype(float)

print(f'Feature matrices: train {X_train.shape}, well {X_well.shape}, grid {X_grid.shape}')

### CELL 19 (markdown) ###
## 7. Estimation — MCPcatPdf and BMEcatPdf

Three estimators using the separable 3-D Pmodel:

1. **MCPcatPdf + local marginal** — fast conditional-independence approximation
   with kernel-smoothed nonstationary baseline $p_\text{local}(c)$.
2. **BMEcatPdf + local marginal** (Case B) — full BME with $p_\text{local}$
   as the prior; sparse-data limit $\to p_\text{local}$.
3. **BMEcatPdf + composite prior** (Case A) — XGBoostLSS combined with the
   local marginal: $q_\text{eff}(c) \propto p_\text{local}(c) \times q_\text{XGB}(c) / p_\text{global}(c)$.

The BF denominator is **always** $p_\text{global}$ (the structural Pmodel marginal).

### CELL 20 (code) ###
t0 = time.perf_counter()
result_mcp = MCPcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme, [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel],
    nsmax_3d, None, options=bme_opts_3d)
t_mcp = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'MCPcatPdf + local:      {result_mcp.shape}  ({t_mcp:.1f} s)')

t0 = time.perf_counter()
result_bme_local = BMEcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme, [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel],
    nsmax_3d, None, options=bme_opts_3d)
t_bme_local = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'BMEcatPdf + local:      {result_bme_local.shape}  ({t_bme_local:.1f} s)')

t0 = time.perf_counter()
result_bme_xgb = BMEcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme, [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel],
    nsmax_3d, None, options={**bme_opts_3d, 'prior_pdf_at_ck': prior_matrix})
t_bme_xgb = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'BMEcatPdf + composite:  {result_bme_xgb.shape}  ({t_bme_xgb:.1f} s)')

_codes = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)
map_mcp      = _codes[np.argmax(result_mcp, axis=1)]
map_bme_loc  = _codes[np.argmax(result_bme_local, axis=1)]
map_bme_xgb  = _codes[np.argmax(result_bme_xgb, axis=1)]

from stamps.bme.BMEcatPdf import (
    _coerce_ps_soft, _resolve_pmodel,
    _find_effective_range, neighbours_separable,
)
from stamps.stats.dependence.probatablefit import probamodel2bitable_separable

# --- Reconstruct the separable config used inside BMEcatPdf/MCPcatPdf ----------
cs_f = np.asarray(cs_bme, dtype=float)
sep_diag, _, _, _ = _resolve_pmodel(
    [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel], None, cs_f, bme_opts_3d)

_thresh = bme_opts_3d.get('auto_dmax_threshold', 0.05)
for _co in sep_diag['components']:
    _co['dmax'] = _find_effective_range(_co['dmodel'], _co['Pmodel'], threshold=_thresh)

ps_soft = _coerce_ps_soft(ps_bme, nc, bme_opts_3d)
_p_marg = np.asarray(sep_diag.get('p_marginal'), dtype=float)
_p_marg = _p_marg / _p_marg.sum()

print('Separable dmax applied inside neighbours_separable:')
for _co in sep_diag['components']:
    print(f"  cols={_co['coord_cols']}  dmax={_co['dmax']:.1f}")

# --- Find Z=-15 locations where MCP MAP != BME-local MAP ----------------------
z_diag   = -15.0
mask_z15 = np.abs(ck_bme[:, 2] - z_diag) &lt; 1.0
idx_z15  = np.where(mask_z15)[0]

disagree = idx_z15[map_mcp[idx_z15] != map_bme_loc[idx_z15]]
print(f'\nGrid nodes at Z={z_diag:.0f} m : {len(idx_z15)}')
print(f'Nodes where MCP != BME-local  : {len(disagree)}')

if len(disagree) == 0:
    print('No disagreeing nodes found at Z=-15 m.')
else:
    n_pick = min(3, len(disagree))
    chosen = disagree[np.round(np.linspace(0, len(disagree)-1, n_pick)).astype(int)]

    lbl_map  = dict(zip(LITHO_CODES, LITHO_LABELS))
    _dms = [_co['dmodel'] for _co in sep_diag['components']]
    _Pms = [_co['Pmodel'] for _co in sep_diag['components']]
    _P_indep = np.outer(_p_marg, _p_marg)

    for loc_idx in chosen:
        ck0 = ck_bme[[loc_idx], :]
        x0, y0, z0 = ck0[0, 0], ck0[0, 1], ck0[0, 2]

        csub, Zsub, dsub, nsub, sltidx, d_comp, p_local = neighbours_separable(
            ck0, cs_f, ps_soft, nsmax_3d,
            sep_diag['components'],
            options=bme_opts_3d,
            p_marginal=_p_marg,
            mode=sep_diag.get('mode', 'product'),
        )

        mcp_cls   = lbl_map[int(map_mcp[loc_idx])]
        bme_l_cls = lbl_map[int(map_bme_loc[loc_idx])]
        bme_x_cls = lbl_map[int(map_bme_xgb[loc_idx])]

        print(f'\n{"="*72}')
        print(f'Location idx={loc_idx}  X={x0:.0f}  Y={y0:.0f}  Z={z0:.1f} m')
        print(f'  MCP+local  : {mcp_cls}')
        print(f'  BME+local  : {bme_l_cls}')
        print(f'  BME+compos.: {bme_x_cls}')
        print(f'  Neighbours : {nsub}')

        if p_local is not None:
            _ps = '  '.join(f'{l}={v:.3f}' for l, v in zip(LITHO_LABELS, p_local))
            print(f'  p_local    : [{_ps}]')
        else:
            print('  p_local    : None (no candidates in kernel range)')

        if nsub == 0:
            print('  (no neighbours found)')
            print('=' * 72)
            continue

        # TV score per selected neighbour
        rows = []
        for k in range(nsub):
            _dvec = d_comp[k, :]
            _P3d  = probamodel2bitable_separable(
                _dvec, _dms, _Pms, _p_marg,
                mode=sep_diag.get('mode', 'product'))
            _tv  = 0.5 * np.abs(_P3d - _P_indep).sum()
            _cls = lbl_map.get(LITHO_CODES[int(np.argmax(Zsub[k]))], '?')
            rows.append((_cls, _dvec[0], _dvec[1], csub[k, 2], _tv))

        print(f'\n  {"#":&gt;2}  {"Class":&lt;10}  {"d_horiz(km)":&gt;11}  '
              f'{"d_vert(m)":&gt;9}  {"TV":&gt;6}  Z_data(m)')
        print(f'  {"-"*60}')
        for k, (_cls, dh, dv, zk, tv) in enumerate(rows):
            print(f'  {k:2d}  {_cls:&lt;10}  {dh/1e3:&gt;11.3f}  '
                  f'{abs(dv):&gt;9.1f}  {tv:&gt;6.3f}  {zk:.1f}')
        print('=' * 72)

### CELL 25 (markdown) ###
## 9. Station-level leave-one-out cross-validation

Each borehole is held out in turn; the remaining data train the estimator.
With &#96;use_xgb_prior=True&#96; the XGBoostLSS prior is re-fit on each fold.

### CELL 26 (code) ###
def station_loocv(method_fn, coords, ps, dmodel, Pmodel,
                  station_ids, categories, nsmax, dmax, options,
                  use_xgb_prior=False, cs_features=None):
    unique_st = np.unique(station_ids)
    all_post, all_true = [], []
    base_opts = {**options, 'category_codes': categories}
    for st in unique_st:
        tr = station_ids != st
        te = station_ids == st
        fold_opts = dict(base_opts)
        if use_xgb_prior and cs_features is not None:
            with warnings.catch_warnings():
                warnings.filterwarnings('ignore',
                    message='XGBoostLSS native tuning failed')
                warnings.filterwarnings('ignore',
                    category=FutureWarning, module='xgboost')
                ext, _ = BMEcatPrior(
                    ck=coords[te], cs=coords[tr], ps=ps[tr],
                    ck_features=cs_features[te],
                    cs_features=cs_features[tr],
                    method='xgboostlss', cv_config={'n_trials': 0},
                    categories=categories, verbose=False,
                    return_details=True)
            fold_opts['prior_pdf_at_ck'] = ext
        post = method_fn(coords[te], coords[tr], ps[tr],
                         dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax,
                         options=fold_opts)
        all_post.append(post)
        all_true.append(ps[te])
    post_all = np.vstack(all_post)
    true_all = np.concatenate(all_true)
    cats = np.asarray(categories)
    acc = float(np.mean(cats[np.argmax(post_all, axis=1)] == true_all))
    ti = np.searchsorted(categories, true_all)
    mll = float(np.mean(np.log(np.clip(
        post_all[np.arange(len(true_all)), ti], 1e-15, None))))
    return acc, mll

### CELL 27 (code) ###

### CELL 29 (markdown) ###
## 10. Summary

This notebook demonstrated the complete BMEcatPdf workflow for 3-D categorical
spatial estimation:

- **Data**: 52 boreholes (7,913 depth samples) with 4 lithology classes in the
  Pingtung alluvial plain.
- **Pmodel**: Vertical (within-borehole, 0-80 m) and horizontal (station-level,
  0-21 km) transition-probability models fitted via kernel smoothing with
  regularisation.  Directional analysis confirmed mild horizontal anisotropy.
- **Separable 3-D**: Product-mode composition $P_H \, D^{-1} \, P_V$ with
  &#96;auto_dmax&#96; and TV-based neighbour ranking.
- **XGBoostLSS prior**: Dirichlet-output gradient boosting using depth, basin,
  and distance covariates.
- **Composite prior**: $q_\text{eff}(c) \propto p_\text{local}(c) \times q_\text{XGB}(c) / p_\text{global}(c)$
  combines the kernel-smoothed local baseline with the XGBoost odds ratio.
  BF denominator is always $p_\text{global}$.
- **LOOCV**: Station-level leave-one-out cross-validation provides accuracy
  and mean log-likelihood for MCP, BME (local), and BME (composite) estimators.
```

```
print(f'Anisotropy ratio:     {r_hat:.3f}  (1 = isotropic)')
print(f'Principal range:      {a_max_h/1e3:.2f} km')

### CELL 13 (code) ###
valid_h = ~np.isnan(D_emp_h[1:])
D_h = D_emp_h[1:][valid_h]
P_h = P_emp_h[:, :, 1:][:, :, valid_h]
O_h = O_emp_h[1:][valid_h]
sz_h = 20 + 60 * (np.log1p(O_h) / np.log1p(O_h.max()))
sz_v2 = 20 + 60 * (np.log1p(O_v) / np.log1p(O_v.max()))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))
for i, (lbl, col) in enumerate(zip(LITHO_LABELS, LITHO_COLORS)):
    axes[0].scatter(D_v, P_v[i, i, :], s=sz_v2, color=col, alpha=0.65, zorder=3)
    axes[0].plot(dmodel, Pmodel[i, i, :], color=col, lw=2, label=lbl)
    axes[1].scatter(D_h / 1e3, P_h[i, i, :], s=sz_h, color=col, alpha=0.65, zorder=3)
    axes[1].plot(dmodel_h / 1e3, Pmodel_h[i, i, :], color=col, lw=2, label=lbl)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Vertical separation (m)')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Horizontal separation (km)')
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_ylabel('P(same class)'); ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[0].set_title('Vertical self-transition')
axes[1].set_title('Horizontal self-transition')
plt.suptitle('Vertical vs Horizontal Pmodel comparison', fontsize=12)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

### CELL 14 (markdown) ###
## 5. Separable 3-D Pmodel (product mode)

The vertical and horizontal Pmodels are composed via a Markov-chain product:
$P_{3D}(a,b \mid \Delta h, \Delta z) = P_H \, D^{-1} \, P_V$
where $D = \mathrm{diag}(p)$.  Passing &#96;dmodel&#96; and &#96;Pmodel&#96; as **lists** to
&#96;MCPcatPdf&#96; / &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; activates separable mode automatically.

### CELL 15 (code) ###
a_max_v_per_class = np.array([
    _ptable_range(dmodel, Pmodel[i, i, :], p_bg[i]**2) for i in range(nc)])
w_v = p_bg[~np.isnan(a_max_v_per_class)]
a_max_v = float(np.dot(a_max_v_per_class[~np.isnan(a_max_v_per_class)],
                        w_v / w_v.sum()))

cs_bme = wells[['X', 'Y', 'Z']].values
ck_bme = grid_df[['X', 'Y', 'Z']].values
ps_bme = y_well

nsmax_3d = 8
bme_opts_3d = {
    'auto_dmax':         True,
    'category_codes':    LITHO_CODES,
    'neighbour_ranking': 'tv',
    'local_marginal':    True,
}

print('Separable 3-D Pmodel (product mode)')
print(f'  Horizontal: {dmodel_h[0]/1e3:.2f} - {dmodel_h[-1]/1e3:.2f} km, '
      f'range {a_max_h/1e3:.2f} km')
print(f'  Vertical:   {dmodel[0]:.1f} - {dmodel[-1]:.1f} m, '
      f'range {a_max_v:.1f} m')
print(f'  nsmax={nsmax_3d}, ranking=tv, local_marginal=True')
print(f'  cs_bme: {cs_bme.shape}, ck_bme: {ck_bme.shape}')

### CELL 16 (markdown) ###
## 6. XGBoostLSS prior estimation

Train a Dirichlet-output XGBoostLSS model to predict class probabilities at
the estimation grid.  The prior is later combined with the local marginal as
a composite prior in BMEcatPdf.

### CELL 17 (code) ###
def build_features(df):
    d = df.copy()
    d = d.assign(Z=-d['Z'])
    basin_dummies = pd.get_dummies(d['Basin'], prefix='Basin')
    d = pd.concat([d.drop(columns=['Basin']), basin_dummies], axis=1)
    exclude = {'X', 'Y', 'LithoCode'}
    feat_cols = [c for c in d.columns if c not in exclude]
    return d[feat_cols].values.astype(float), feat_cols

X_train, feat_names = build_features(train_df)
X_well, _ = build_features(wells)

basin_cols = [c for c in feat_names if c.startswith('Basin_')]
grid_tmp = grid_df.copy()
grid_dummies = pd.get_dummies(grid_tmp['Basin'], prefix='Basin')
grid_tmp = pd.concat([grid_tmp.drop(columns=['Basin']), grid_dummies], axis=1)
for bc in basin_cols:
    if bc not in grid_tmp.columns:
        grid_tmp[bc] = 0
grid_feat_cols = ['Z','Height','Formation Factor','inResModel',
    'Testing_Distance','Corner_Distance_1','Corner_Distance_2',
    'Corner_Distance_3'] + basin_cols
grid_tmp = grid_tmp.assign(Z=-grid_tmp['Z'])
X_grid = grid_tmp[[c for c in grid_feat_cols
                    if c in grid_tmp.columns]].values.astype(float)

print(f'Feature matrices: train {X_train.shape}, well {X_well.shape}, grid {X_grid.shape}')

prior_matrix, prior_details = BMEcatPrior(
    ck=ck_bme, cs=cs_bme, ps=ps_bme,
    ck_features=X_grid, cs_features=X_well,
    station_ids=station_ids, method='xgboostlss',
    cv_config={'n_trials': 0}, categories=LITHO_CODES,
    label_map={1:'Clay', 2:'Fine sand', 3:'Sand', 4:'Gravel'},
    feature_labels=feat_names, verbose=True, return_details=True)

print(f'prior_matrix: {prior_matrix.shape}')
for lbl, v in zip(LITHO_LABELS, prior_matrix.mean(axis=0)):
    print(f'  Mean P({lbl}): {v:.3f}')

### CELL 18 (code) ###
fi = prior_details.get('feature_importances', {})
if fi:
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
    pd.Series(fi).sort_values(ascending=True).plot.barh(ax=ax, color='steelblue')
    ax.set_xlabel('Importance (gain)')
    ax.set_title('XGBoostLSS feature importances')
    plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

z_prior = -75.0
mask_pr = np.abs(grid_df['Z'] - z_prior) &lt; 1.0
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, nc, figsize=(16, 4))
for j, (lbl, col) in enumerate(zip(LITHO_LABELS, LITHO_COLORS)):
    ax = axes[j]
    sc = ax.scatter(grid_df.loc[mask_pr, 'X'], grid_df.loc[mask_pr, 'Y'],
                    c=prior_matrix[mask_pr, j], cmap='RdYlGn', vmin=0, vmax=1, s=20)
    ax.scatter(wells['X'], wells['Y'], c='k', s=25, marker='x', linewidths=0.8)
    plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, fraction=0.04)
    ax.set_title(f'P({lbl})', fontsize=10)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=7); ax.set_aspect('equal')
plt.suptitle(f'XGBoostLSS prior probabilities at Z = {z_prior:.0f} m',
             fontsize=12, y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

### CELL 19 (markdown) ###
## 7. Estimation — MCPcatPdf and BMEcatPdf

Three estimators using the separable 3-D Pmodel:

1. **MCPcatPdf + local marginal** — fast conditional-independence approximation
   with kernel-smoothed nonstationary baseline $p_\text{local}(c)$.
2. **BMEcatPdf + local marginal** (Case B) — full BME with $p_\text{local}$
   as the prior; sparse-data limit $\to p_\text{local}$.
3. **BMEcatPdf + composite prior** (Case A) — XGBoostLSS combined with the
   local marginal: $q_\text{eff}(c) \propto p_\text{local}(c) \times q_\text{XGB}(c) / p_\text{global}(c)$.

The BF denominator is **always** $p_\text{global}$ (the structural Pmodel marginal).

### CELL 20 (code) ###
t0 = time.perf_counter()
result_mcp = MCPcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme, [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel],
    nsmax_3d, None, options=bme_opts_3d)
t_mcp = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'MCPcatPdf + local:      {result_mcp.shape}  ({t_mcp:.1f} s)')

t0 = time.perf_counter()
result_bme_local = BMEcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme, [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel],
    nsmax_3d, None, options=bme_opts_3d)
t_bme_local = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'BMEcatPdf + local:      {result_bme_local.shape}  ({t_bme_local:.1f} s)')

t0 = time.perf_counter()
result_bme_xgb = BMEcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme, [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel],
    nsmax_3d, None, options={**bme_opts_3d, 'prior_pdf_at_ck': prior_matrix})
t_bme_xgb = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'BMEcatPdf + composite:  {result_bme_xgb.shape}  ({t_bme_xgb:.1f} s)')

_codes = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)
map_mcp      = _codes[np.argmax(result_mcp, axis=1)]
map_bme_loc  = _codes[np.argmax(result_bme_local, axis=1)]
map_bme_xgb  = _codes[np.argmax(result_bme_xgb, axis=1)]

```

The script `examples/pingtung_lithology/pingtung_estimation.py` is ready. Here's what it does:

**How to run:**
```bash
cd examples/pingtung_lithology
python pingtung_estimation.py
```

**Figures saved to `output/`:**

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `fig01_data_overview.png` | Cross-section + borehole location map |
| `fig02_depth_slices.png` | Plan-view lithology at Z = -15, -75, -150 m |
| `fig03_vertical_pmodel_matrix.png` | Full 4×4 vertical Pmodel matrix |
| `fig04_pmodel_comparison.png` | Self-transition: vertical vs horizontal |
| `fig05_aniso_rose.png` | Polar anisotropy rose diagram |
| `fig06_xgb_feature_importance.png` | XGBoostLSS feature importances |
| `fig07_xgb_prior_z75.png` | XGBoostLSS prior at Z = -75 m |
| `fig08_estimation_maps.png` | MAP lithology at all depth levels (3 methods) |
| `fig09_posterior_z75.png` | Per-class posteriors at Z = -75 m |
| `fig10_loocv_results.png` | Station LOOCV accuracy & log-likelihood bar chart |

**Data files saved to `output/`:**

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `geology_3d_mcp.json` | MCPcatPdf + local — viewer format |
| `geology_3d_bme_local.json` | BMEcatPdf + local — viewer format |
| `geology_3d_bme_composite.json` | BMEcatPdf + composite (XGB) — viewer format |
| `estimation_probabilities.csv` | Full posterior arrays + MAP codes for all 3 methods |

**Key differences from the notebook:**
- `XGB_N_TRIALS = 30` at the top — Optuna hyperparameter search is active (change to `0` to skip)
- `matplotlib.use('Agg')` ensures figures render without a display
- All `plt.show()` replaced by `savefig(name)` which saves to `output/`

**To view in `bme_geological_data_viewer`:** load any of the three `.json` files and select **TWD97** as the projection.

```json
          },

          },

            "text": "        The estimated posterior marginal PDFs, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, nc)&#96;&#96;.",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2638
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 2639
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 2640
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Choosing nsmax_total and dmax_mcp:**",
            "lineNumber": 2641
          },
          {
            "text": "    Let r be the covariance correlation range.  Set &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp ≈ r&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2642
          },
          {
            "text": "    choose &#96;&#96;nsmax_total&#96;&#96; as the expected number of data points within that",
            "lineNumber": 2643
          },
          {
            "text": "    radius (typically 10–25 for datasets of 50–200 points).  Using too many",
            "lineNumber": 2644
          },
          {
            "text": "    decorrelated neighbours (beyond r) causes the MCP prior to converge to",
            "lineNumber": 2645
          },
          {
            "text": "    the global marginal P(c) at every location, destroying spatial variation.",
            "lineNumber": 2646
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2647
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Bayes-factor correction:**",
            "lineNumber": 2648
          },
          {
            "text": "    The Maximum Entropy table solved by &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; carries an implicit",
            "lineNumber": 2649
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; weight (the global marginal).  Passing the MCP result &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2650
          },
          {
            "text": "    directly as a prior therefore weights the final posterior by",
            "lineNumber": 2651
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;q(c) · p(c)&#96;&#96; rather than &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; alone — a subtle double-counting",
            "lineNumber": 2652
          },
          {
            "text": "    of the baseline frequency.  The Bayes-factor correction divides the",
            "lineNumber": 2653
          },
          {
            "text": "    supplied prior by &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; before entering &#96;&#96;producttablepdf&#96;&#96;, so the",
            "lineNumber": 2654
          },
          {
            "text": "    net effect is exactly &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;.  When no prior is given this correction",
            "lineNumber": 2655
          },
          {
            "text": "    is never triggered and the original BME behaviour is preserved.",
            "lineNumber": 2656
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./stamps/stamps/bme/BMEprobaEstimations.py",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 4217,
            "column": 5
          },
```
