          }
        },
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# Backward-compatible name kept for any code written against the old API.",
            "lineNumber": 4221
          },
          {
            "text": "compute_bme_prior = BMEpriorMean",
            "lineNumber": 4222
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4223
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4224
          },
          {
            "text": "def BMEPosteriorMoments(",
            "lineNumber": 4225,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    ck, ch=None, cs=None, zh=None, zs=None,",
            "lineNumber": 4226,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    covmodel=None, covparam=None, covmat=None,",
            "lineNumber": 4227,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    order=np.nan, options=None,",
            "lineNumber": 4228,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    nhmax=None, nsmax=None, dmax=None,",
            "lineNumber": 4229,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    general_knowledge='gaussian',",
            "lineNumber": 4230,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    #  specific_knowledge='unknown',  ",
            "lineNumber": 4231,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    pdfk=None,pdfh=None,pdfs=None,hk_k=None,hk_h=None,hk_s=None,",
            "lineNumber": 4232,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    gui_args=None, ck_cov_output=False, n_workers=1):",
            "lineNumber": 4233,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Compute the BME posterior mean, variance, and third central moment at all estimation locations.",
            "lineNumber": 4234
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4235
          },
          {
            "text": "    This is the primary estimation function of the stamps BME engine.  For",
            "lineNumber": 4236
          },
          {
            "text": "    each estimation location in *ck* it evaluates the Bayesian Maximum Entropy",
            "lineNumber": 4237
          },
          {
            "text": "    (BME) posterior distribution conditioned on all available hard and soft",
            "lineNumber": 4238
          },
          {
            "text": "    data, and returns three summary statistics.",
            "lineNumber": 4239
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4240
          },
          {
            "text": "    The function selects one of two internal computation paths:",
            "lineNumber": 4241
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4242
          },
          {
            "text": "    * **Analytical Gaussian path** (fast) — used whenever every soft datum is",
            "lineNumber": 4243
          },
          {
            "text": "      of type 10 (Gaussian PDF), or when &#96;&#96;options['soft_approx_gaussian']&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 4244
          },
          {
            "text": "      is &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, or when more than 20 non-Gaussian soft data are present in",
            "lineNumber": 4245
          },
          {
            "text": "      the neighbourhood (automatic threshold).  Reduces to Simple Kriging or",
            "lineNumber": 4246
          },
          {
            "text": "      Ordinary Kriging depending on *order*.",
            "lineNumber": 4247
          },
          {
            "text": "    * **QMC Importance-Sampling path** (general) — used for non-Gaussian soft",
            "lineNumber": 4248
          },
          {
            "text": "      data (interval / histogram / linear PDFs).  Draws Quasi-Monte Carlo",
            "lineNumber": 4249
          },
          {
            "text": "      samples from the conditional Gaussian prior, weights them by the soft",
            "lineNumber": 4250
          },
          {
            "text": "      likelihood, and estimates the normalised posterior moments.  If the QMC",
            "lineNumber": 4251
          },
          {
            "text": "      normalisation constant is numerically unstable, a per-location Gaussian",
            "lineNumber": 4252
          },
          {
            "text": "      fallback is applied automatically.",
            "lineNumber": 4253
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4254
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 4255
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 4256
          },
          {
            "text": "    ck : ndarray, shape (nk, nd)",
            "lineNumber": 4257
          },
          {
            "text": "        Estimation locations.  &#96;&#96;nd&#96;&#96; is the number of coordinate dimensions:",
            "lineNumber": 4258
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;nd=2&#96;&#96; for purely spatial problems (easting, northing) or &#96;&#96;nd=3&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 4259
          },
          {
            "text": "        for space-time problems (easting, northing, time).  The last column is",
            "lineNumber": 4260
          },
          {
            "text": "        treated as the time axis when &#96;&#96;nd=3&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 4261
          },
          {
            "text": "    ch : ndarray, shape (nh, nd), optional",
            "lineNumber": 4262
          },
          {
            "text": "        Hard-data (exact observation) locations.  Same coordinate convention",
            "lineNumber": 4263
          },
          {
            "text": "        as *ck*.  Pass &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96; when no hard data are available.",
            "lineNumber": 4264
          },
          {
            "text": "    cs : ndarray, shape (ns, nd), optional",
            "lineNumber": 4265
          },
          {
            "text": "        Soft-data locations.  Pass &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96; when no soft data are available.",
            "lineNumber": 4266
          },
          {
            "text": "    zh : ndarray, shape (nh,) or (nh, 1), optional",
            "lineNumber": 4267
          },
          {
            "text": "        Hard-data observed values, one scalar per row of *ch*.  Reshaped",
            "lineNumber": 4268
          },
          {
            "text": "        internally to &#96;&#96;(nh, 1)&#96;&#96; if necessary.",
            "lineNumber": 4269
          },
          {
            "text": "    zs : list of tuples, length ns, optional",
            "lineNumber": 4270
          },
          {
            "text": "        Soft-data probabilistic information.  Each element &#96;&#96;zs[i]&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 4271
          },
          {
            "text": "        describes the PDF at location &#96;&#96;cs[i]&#96;&#96; using the stamps format:",
            "lineNumber": 4272
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4273
          },
          {
            "text": "        * &#96;&#96;(1,  nl, limi, probdens)&#96;&#96; — histogram PDF (type 1)",
            "lineNumber": 4274
          },
          {
            "text": "        * &#96;&#96;(2,  nl, limi, probdens)&#96;&#96; — linear PDF (type 2)",
            "lineNumber": 4275
          },
          {
            "text": "        * &#96;&#96;(10, mean, variance)&#96;&#96;     — Gaussian PDF (type 10)",
            "lineNumber": 4276
          },
          {
            "text": "        * &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96;                     — missing observation (skipped)",
            "lineNumber": 4277
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4278
          },
          {
            "text": "        where &#96;&#96;nl&#96;&#96; is the number of PDF classes (shape &#96;&#96;(1,)&#96;&#96; or",
            "lineNumber": 4279
          },
          {
            "text": "        scalar), &#96;&#96;limi&#96;&#96; are the class boundaries (shape &#96;&#96;(1, nl+1)&#96;&#96; for",
            "lineNumber": 4280
          },
          {
            "text": "        type 1/2), and &#96;&#96;probdens&#96;&#96; are the probability densities",
            "lineNumber": 4281
          },
          {
            "text": "        (shape &#96;&#96;(1, nl)&#96;&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 4282
          },
          {
            "text": "        Use :func:&#96;stamps.bme.softconverter.probaUniform&#96; or",
            "lineNumber": 4283
          },
          {
            "text": "        :func:&#96;stamps.bme.softconverter.probaGaussian&#96; to construct these",
            "lineNumber": 4284
          },
          {
            "text": "        tuples from raw interval or Gaussian parameters.",
            "lineNumber": 4285
          },
          {
            "text": "    covmodel : callable or str, optional",
            "lineNumber": 4286
          },
          {
            "text": "        Covariance model function (e.g. &#96;&#96;exponentialC&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;sphericalC&#96;&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 4287
          },
          {
            "text": "        Required unless *covmat* is provided.  Accepts the signature",
            "lineNumber": 4288
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;covmodel(dist, sill, range_param)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 4289
          },
          {
            "text": "    covparam : list or ndarray, optional",
            "lineNumber": 4290
          },
          {
            "text": "        Parameters for *covmodel* in stamps nested-model format.  Required",
            "lineNumber": 4291
          },
          {
            "text": "        unless *covmat* is provided.  See :func:&#96;stamps.models.covmodel&#96; for",
            "lineNumber": 4292
          },
          {
            "text": "        the expected structure.",
            "lineNumber": 4293
          },
          {
            "text": "    covmat : ndarray, shape (nk+nh+ns, nk+nh+ns), optional",
            "lineNumber": 4294
          },
          {
            "text": "        Pre-computed full covariance matrix covering all estimation and data",
            "lineNumber": 4295
          },
          {
            "text": "        locations in the stacked order &#96;&#96;[ck; ch; cs]&#96;&#96;.  When provided,",
            "lineNumber": 4296
          },
          {
            "text": "        *covmodel* and *covparam* are ignored and no distances need to be",
            "lineNumber": 4297
          },
          {
            "text": "        computed.  Useful when the same matrix is reused across multiple calls",
            "lineNumber": 4298
          },
          {
            "text": "        (e.g. in a GUI loop).",
            "lineNumber": 4299
          },
          {
            "text": "    order : {np.nan, 0, ndarray of shape (nk+nh+ns, 1)}, default &#96;&#96;np.nan&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 4300
          },
          {
            "text": "        Prior-mean specification controlling the large-scale trend:",
            "lineNumber": 4301
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4302
          },
          {
            "text": "        * &#96;&#96;np.nan&#96;&#96;  — **zero-mean prior**.  Equivalent to Simple Kriging.",
            "lineNumber": 4303
          },
          {
            "text": "          Estimates revert to 0 wherever data are absent.  Appropriate only",
            "lineNumber": 4304
          },
          {
            "text": "          when the field has been pre-de-meaned.",
            "lineNumber": 4305
          },
          {
            "text": "        * &#96;&#96;0&#96;&#96;       — **global-mean prior**.  A single constant equal to",
            "lineNumber": 4306
          },
          {
            "text": "          the weighted average of all data (equivalent to Ordinary Kriging).",
            "lineNumber": 4307
          },
          {
            "text": "          Estimates revert to the data mean in data-sparse areas.",
            "lineNumber": 4308
          },
          {
            "text": "        * &#96;&#96;ndarray&#96;&#96; — **spatially-varying prior mean**, one value per row",
            "lineNumber": 4309
          },
          {
            "text": "          of the stacked &#96;&#96;[ck; ch; cs]&#96;&#96; coordinate array.  Use the output",
            "lineNumber": 4310
          },
          {
            "text": "          of :func:&#96;BMEpriorMean&#96; (method &#96;&#96;'kernel'&#96;&#96; or &#96;&#96;'kriging'&#96;&#96;) to",
            "lineNumber": 4311
          },
          {
            "text": "          build this array for a data-adaptive locally-varying trend.",
            "lineNumber": 4312
          },
          {
            "text": "    options : BMEoptions or None, optional",
            "lineNumber": 4313
          },
          {
            "text": "        Dictionary-like object controlling numerical options.  When &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 4314
          },
          {
            "text": "        (default), :class:&#96;stamps.bme.BMEoptions&#96; defaults are used.",
            "lineNumber": 4315
          },
          {
            "text": "        Relevant keys:",
            "lineNumber": 4316
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4317
          },
          {
            "text": "        * &#96;&#96;'soft_approx_gaussian'&#96;&#96; *(bool, default False)* — force the",
            "lineNumber": 4318
          },
          {
            "text": "          analytical Gaussian approximation for all soft data, bypassing QMC.",
            "lineNumber": 4319
          },
          {
            "text": "          Speeds up computation at the cost of accuracy when intervals are wide",
            "lineNumber": 4320
          },
          {
            "text": "          or asymmetric.",
            "lineNumber": 4321
          },
          {
            "text": "        * &#96;&#96;'outlier_handling'&#96;&#96; *(str, default &#96;&#96;'inflate'&#96;&#96;)* — how to treat",
            "lineNumber": 4322
          },
          {
            "text": "          soft data whose interval is statistically incompatible with the",

          },

          },

            "lineNumber": 1891
          },

          },

          },

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py",

              "startPosition": {

        },
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def tune_regularization_loocv(cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, reg_grid, base_options=None):",
            "lineNumber": 1904,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1953
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1954
          },
          {
            "text": "    for reg in reg_grid:",
            "lineNumber": 1955
          },
          {
            "text": "        current_options = base_options.copy()",
            "lineNumber": 1956
          },
          {
            "text": "        current_options['reg'] = reg",
            "lineNumber": 1957
          },
          {
            "text": "        total_log_likelihood = 0.0",
            "lineNumber": 1958
          },
          {
            "text": "        ",
            "lineNumber": 1959
          },
          {
            "text": "        print(f\"  Testing reg = {reg} ...\")",
            "lineNumber": 1960
          },
          {
            "text": "        ",
            "lineNumber": 1961
          },
          {
            "text": "        for i in range(n_data):",
            "lineNumber": 1962
          },
          {
            "text": "            # 1. Hold out point i",
            "lineNumber": 1963
          },
          {
            "text": "            ck_i = cs[i:i+1, :]         # The point to predict",
            "lineNumber": 1964
          },
          {
            "text": "            ps_i_known = ps[i, :]       # The known PDF at that point",
            "lineNumber": 1965
          },
          {
            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 1966
          },
          {
            "text": "            cs_minus_i = np.delete(cs, i, axis=0) # All other data coords",
            "lineNumber": 1967
          },
          {
            "text": "            ps_minus_i = np.delete(ps, i, axis=0) # All other data PDFs",
            "lineNumber": 1968
          },
          {
            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 1969
          },
          {
            "text": "            # Check if there's any data left to predict from",
            "lineNumber": 1970
          },
          {
            "text": "            if cs_minus_i.shape[0] == 0:",
            "lineNumber": 1971
          },
          {
            "text": "                continue ",
            "lineNumber": 1972
          },
          {
            "text": "                ",
            "lineNumber": 1973
          },
          {
            "text": "            # 2. Predict point i using the rest of the data",
            "lineNumber": 1974
          },
          {
            "text": "            pk_i_pred = BMEcatPdf(ck_i, ",
            "lineNumber": 1975
          },
          {
            "text": "                                  cs_minus_i, ",
            "lineNumber": 1976
          },
          {
            "text": "                                  ps_minus_i, ",
            "lineNumber": 1977
          },
          {
            "text": "                                  dmodel, ",
            "lineNumber": 1978
          },
          {
            "text": "                                  Pmodel, ",
            "lineNumber": 1979
          },
          {
            "text": "                                  nsmax, ",
            "lineNumber": 1980
          },
          {
            "text": "                                  dmax, ",
            "lineNumber": 1981
          },
          {
            "text": "                                  options=current_options)",
            "lineNumber": 1982
          },
          {
            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 1983
          },
          {
            "text": "            pk_i_pred_vector = pk_i_pred[0, :]",
            "lineNumber": 1984
          },
          {
            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 1985
          },
          {
            "text": "            # 3. Score the prediction using log-likelihood",
            "lineNumber": 1986
          },
          {
            "text": "            # We clip the predicted probabilities to avoid log(0)",
            "lineNumber": 1987
          },
          {
            "text": "            pk_i_pred_vector = np.clip(pk_i_pred_vector, 1e-15, 1.0)",
            "lineNumber": 1988
          },
          {
            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 1989
          },
          {
            "text": "            # This is the \"log score\"",
            "lineNumber": 1990
          },
          {
            "text": "            score_i = np.sum(ps_i_known * np.log(pk_i_pred_vector))",
            "lineNumber": 1991
          },
          {
            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 1992
          },
          {
            "text": "            if not np.isnan(score_i):",
            "lineNumber": 1993
          },
          {
            "text": "                total_log_likelihood += score_i",
            "lineNumber": 1994
          },
          {
            "text": "                ",
            "lineNumber": 1995
          },
          {
            "text": "        scores[reg] = total_log_likelihood",
            "lineNumber": 1996
          },
          {
            "text": "        print(f\"    -&gt; Score (Log-Likelihood): {total_log_likelihood:.4f}\")",
            "lineNumber": 1997
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1998
          },
          {
            "text": "    # 4. Find the best reg",
            "lineNumber": 1999
          },
          {
            "text": "    best_reg = max(scores, key=scores.get)",
            "lineNumber": 2000
          },
          {
            "text": "    print(f\"--- LOOCV Tuning Complete ---\")",
            "lineNumber": 2001
          },
          {
            "text": "    print(f\"All scores: {scores}\")",
            "lineNumber": 2002
          },
          {
            "text": "    print(f\"Best reg: {best_reg} (Score: {scores[best_reg]:.4f})\")",
            "lineNumber": 2003
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 2004
          },
          {
            "text": "    return scores, best_reg",
            "lineNumber": 2005,
            "isSignature": true
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.30533671379089355
    },

      "codeBlock": {

          {
            "text": "def BMEpriorMean(",
            "lineNumber": 3820,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        ck, ch, zh, cs=None, zs=None,",
            "lineNumber": 3821,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        method='kernel',",
            "lineNumber": 3822,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        bandwidth=None,",
            "lineNumber": 3823,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        kernel='gaussian',",
            "lineNumber": 3824,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        truncate=False,",
            "lineNumber": 3825,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        use_soft_data=False,",
            "lineNumber": 3826,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        cv_bandwidth=False,",
            "lineNumber": 3827,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        n_cv_bandwidths=30,",
            "lineNumber": 3828,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        cv_bandwidth_range=None,",
            "lineNumber": 3829,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        cv_verbose=False,",
            "lineNumber": 3830,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        covmodel=None, covparam=None,",
            "lineNumber": 3831,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "        order_trend=0):",
            "lineNumber": 3832,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Compute a prior mean surface for BME at all estimation and data locations.",
            "lineNumber": 3833
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3834
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns a stacked &#96;&#96;(nk + nh + ns, 1)&#96;&#96; array ready to pass directly as",
            "lineNumber": 3835
          },
          {
            "text": "    the &#96;&#96;order&#96;&#96; argument to :func:&#96;BMEPosteriorMoments&#96;.  This replaces the",
            "lineNumber": 3836
          },
          {
            "text": "    scalar &#96;&#96;order=np.nan&#96;&#96; (zero prior) or &#96;&#96;order=0&#96;&#96; (global mean prior)",
            "lineNumber": 3837
          },
          {
            "text": "    with a spatially-varying, data-driven estimate — giving BME behaviour",
            "lineNumber": 3838
          },
          {
            "text": "    closer to Ordinary Kriging in regions without nearby data.",
            "lineNumber": 3839
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3840
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 3841
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 3842
          },
          {
            "text": "    ck : ndarray, shape (nk, nd)",
            "lineNumber": 3843
          },
          {
            "text": "        Estimation locations.",
            "lineNumber": 3844
          },
          {
            "text": "    ch : ndarray, shape (nh, nd)",
            "lineNumber": 3845
          },
          {
            "text": "        Hard-data locations.",
            "lineNumber": 3846
          },
          {
            "text": "    zh : ndarray, shape (nh,) or (nh, 1)",
            "lineNumber": 3847
          },
          {
            "text": "        Hard-data observed values.",
            "lineNumber": 3848
          },
          {
            "text": "    cs : ndarray, shape (ns, nd), optional",
            "lineNumber": 3849
          },
          {
            "text": "        Soft-data locations.",
            "lineNumber": 3850
          },
          {
            "text": "    zs : list of per-location soft-data tuples, optional",
            "lineNumber": 3851
          },
          {
            "text": "        Standard stamps format &#96;&#96;(softpdftype, nl, limi, probdens)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 3852
          },
          {
            "text": "        Required (with *cs*) for methods that need soft data expected values.",
            "lineNumber": 3853
          },
          {
            "text": "    method : str, default &#96;&#96;'kernel'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3854
          },
          {
            "text": "        Prior mean estimation method.  Choices:",
            "lineNumber": 3855
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3856
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'kernel'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3857
          },
          {
            "text": "            Gaussian (or Epanechnikov) kernel smoother.  Data beyond",
            "lineNumber": 3858
          },
          {
            "text": "            *bandwidth* still contribute with exponentially decaying weight,",
            "lineNumber": 3859
          },
          {
            "text": "            so the smoother never produces NaN even at map edges.  By default",
            "lineNumber": 3860
          },
          {
            "text": "            only hard data are used (&#96;&#96;use_soft_data=False&#96;&#96;), avoiding the",
            "lineNumber": 3861
          },
          {
            "text": "            upward bias that arises when interval soft data midpoints are",
            "lineNumber": 3862
          },
          {
            "text": "            higher than the true hard-data mean.",
            "lineNumber": 3863
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3864
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'kernel_truncate'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3865
          },
          {
            "text": "            Same as &#96;&#96;'kernel'&#96;&#96; but the kernel is **truncated to zero beyond",
            "lineNumber": 3866
          },
          {
            "text": "            bandwidth** (wraps the existing",
            "lineNumber": 3867
          },
          {
            "text": "            :mod:&#96;stamps.stest.kernelsmoothing_truncate&#96; module).  Estimates",
            "lineNumber": 3868
          },
          {
            "text": "            are NaN at locations with no data within *bandwidth*; fill those",
            "lineNumber": 3869
          },
          {
            "text": "            with the global hard-data mean.",
            "lineNumber": 3870
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3871
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'idw'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3872
          },
          {
            "text": "            Inverse-distance weighting (power = 2).  Fast; exhibits sharper",
            "lineNumber": 3873
          },
          {
            "text": "            transitions near data clusters than Gaussian kernel.",
            "lineNumber": 3874
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3875
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'global_hard'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3876
          },
          {
            "text": "            Constant equal to the arithmetic mean of the hard data *zh* only.",
            "lineNumber": 3877
          },
          {
            "text": "            This is the recommended replacement for &#96;&#96;order=0&#96;&#96; when the soft",
            "lineNumber": 3878
          },
          {
            "text": "            data midpoints are biased relative to the hard data.",
            "lineNumber": 3879
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3880
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'global'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3881
          },
          {
            "text": "            Constant equal to the arithmetic mean of hard *and* soft data",
            "lineNumber": 3882
          },
          {
            "text": "            expected values (original &#96;&#96;order=0&#96;&#96; behaviour).  Can be biased",
            "lineNumber": 3883
          },
          {
            "text": "            high when interval soft data span regions with higher true values.",
            "lineNumber": 3884
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3885
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'localmeanBME'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3886
          },
          {
            "text": "            GLS regression using the full spatial covariance matrix as the",
            "lineNumber": 3887
          },
          {
            "text": "            weight (wraps :func:&#96;stamps.stest.localmeanBME.localmeanBME&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 3888
          },
          {
            "text": "            Requires *covmodel* and *covparam*.  Returns the best linear",
            "lineNumber": 3889
          },
          {
            "text": "            unbiased estimate of the constant (&#96;&#96;order_trend=0&#96;&#96;) or linear",
            "lineNumber": 3890
          },
          {
            "text": "            (&#96;&#96;order_trend=1&#96;&#96;) trend at every location, accounting for",
            "lineNumber": 3891
          },
          {
            "text": "            spatial autocorrelation.  Effectively the same as computing the",
            "lineNumber": 3892
          },
          {
            "text": "            Ordinary-Kriging mean but without the neighbourhood truncation.",
            "lineNumber": 3893
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3894
          },
          {
            "text": "    bandwidth : float, optional",
            "lineNumber": 3895
          },
          {
            "text": "        Characteristic smoothing length in the same distance units as *ck/ch*.",
            "lineNumber": 3896
          },
          {
            "text": "        Rules of thumb:",
            "lineNumber": 3897
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3898
          },
          {
            "text": "        * Set to ≈1–2× the covariance **range** for smooth trends.",
            "lineNumber": 3899
          },
          {
            "text": "        * Set to ≈0.5× the range for tighter locality.",
            "lineNumber": 3900
          },
          {
            "text": "        * Leave as &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96; (auto) to use a robust default:",
            "lineNumber": 3901
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;max(1.5 × median-NN-distance, 0.1 × study-area-extent)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 3902
          },
          {
            "text": "          This prevents the bandwidth from being excessively narrow when",
            "lineNumber": 3903
          },
          {
            "text": "          data contain closely-spaced survey transects.",
            "lineNumber": 3904
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3905
          },
          {
            "text": "        Ignored by &#96;&#96;'global_hard'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'global'&#96;&#96;, and &#96;&#96;'localmeanBME'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 3906
          },
          {
            "text": "        Overridden when *cv_bandwidth=True*.",
            "lineNumber": 3907
          },
          {
            "text": "    kernel : {'gaussian', 'epanechnikov'}, default &#96;&#96;'gaussian'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3908
          },
          {
            "text": "        Kernel shape; only used when *method* is &#96;&#96;'kernel'&#96;&#96; or",
            "lineNumber": 3909
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'kernel_truncate'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 3910
          },
          {
            "text": "    truncate : bool, default &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3911
          },
          {
            "text": "        If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, forces the truncated kernel regardless of *method*",
            "lineNumber": 3912
          },
          {
            "text": "        (equivalent to &#96;&#96;method='kernel_truncate'&#96;&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 3913
          },
          {
            "text": "    use_soft_data : bool, default &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3914
          },
          {
            "text": "        If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, the **expected values** of soft data PDFs are blended into",
            "lineNumber": 3915
          },
          {
            "text": "        the kernel smoother alongside the hard data.  This can slightly improve",
            "lineNumber": 3916
          },
          {
            "text": "        coverage in data-sparse areas but risks biasing the prior upward if",
            "lineNumber": 3917
          },
          {
            "text": "        soft data intervals are systematically offset from the hard data.",
            "lineNumber": 3918
          },
          {
            "text": "        Has no effect on &#96;&#96;'global_hard'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'localmeanBME'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 3919
          },
          {
            "text": "    cv_bandwidth : bool, default &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3920
          },
          {
            "text": "        If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, the bandwidth is selected automatically by",
            "lineNumber": 3921
          },
          {
            "text": "        **leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV)** on the hard data.  The",
            "lineNumber": 3922
          },
          {
            "text": "        bandwidth minimising the mean squared LOO prediction error is used.",
            "lineNumber": 3923
          },
          {
            "text": "        This is slower than the analytic auto-bandwidth but produces a more",
            "lineNumber": 3924
          },
          {
            "text": "        statistically optimal smoothing length and is recommended when:",
            "lineNumber": 3925
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3926
          },
          {
            "text": "        * The data contain irregularly-spaced clusters (e.g. survey transects",
            "lineNumber": 3927
          },
          {
            "text": "          mixed with scattered points), which can fool the NN-distance heuristic.",
            "lineNumber": 3928
          },
          {
            "text": "        * A principled, objective bandwidth is needed.",
            "lineNumber": 3929
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3930
          },
          {
            "text": "        Overrides *bandwidth* when active.",
            "lineNumber": 3931
          },
          {
            "text": "    n_cv_bandwidths : int, default 30",
            "lineNumber": 3932
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of candidate bandwidths evaluated during LOOCV.",
            "lineNumber": 3933
          },
          {
            "text": "    cv_bandwidth_range : array-like of float, optional",
            "lineNumber": 3934
          },
          {
            "text": "        Explicit list/array of bandwidth candidates for LOOCV.  If &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96;,",
            "lineNumber": 3935
          },
          {
            "text": "        30 log-spaced values from &#96;&#96;0.5 × 10th-pct NN distance&#96;&#96; to",
            "lineNumber": 3936
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;0.5 × max pairwise distance&#96;&#96; are auto-generated.",
            "lineNumber": 3937
          },
          {
            "text": "    cv_verbose : bool, default &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3938
          },
          {
            "text": "        Print the LOOCV error table to stdout.",
            "lineNumber": 3939
          },
          {
            "text": "    covmodel : list of str, optional",
            "lineNumber": 3940
          },
          {
            "text": "        Covariance model names; required for &#96;&#96;method='localmeanBME'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 3941
          },
          {
            "text": "    covparam : list of tuples, optional",
            "lineNumber": 3942
          },
          {
            "text": "        Covariance parameters; required for &#96;&#96;method='localmeanBME'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 3943
          },
          {
            "text": "    order_trend : {0, 1, np.nan}, default &#96;&#96;0&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3944
          },
          {
            "text": "        Regression trend order for &#96;&#96;method='localmeanBME'&#96;&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 3945
          },
          {
            "text": "        0 = constant mean, 1 = linear trend, np.nan = zero mean.",
            "lineNumber": 3946
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3947
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 3948
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 3949
          },
          {
            "text": "    order : ndarray, shape (nk + nh + ns, 1)",
            "lineNumber": 3950
          },
          {
            "text": "        Prior mean at each location, stacked as &#96;&#96;[ck, ch, cs]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 3951
          },
          {
            "text": "        Pass directly as &#96;&#96;order=BMEpriorMean(...)&#96;&#96; to",
            "lineNumber": 3952
          },
          {
            "text": "        :func:&#96;BMEPosteriorMoments&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 3953
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3954
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 3955
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 3956
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Why not just use order=0?**",
            "lineNumber": 3957
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;order=0&#96;&#96; computes the prior mean as the *arithmetic mean of all hard",
            "lineNumber": 3958
          },
          {
            "text": "    and soft data*.  When interval soft data midpoints are higher than the",
            "lineNumber": 3959
          },
          {
            "text": "    true hard-data mean (e.g., intervals spanning 20–40% while precise",
            "lineNumber": 3960
          },
          {
            "text": "    measurements average 15%), the global prior is biased high.  In data-void",
            "lineNumber": 3961
          },
          {
            "text": "    areas the BME estimate then reverts to this elevated prior — producing",
            "lineNumber": 3962
          },
          {
            "text": "    maps that appear *higher at the edges* than in well-sampled interiors.",
            "lineNumber": 3963
          },
          {
            "text": "    Using &#96;&#96;method='global_hard'&#96;&#96; or a kernel smoother over hard data only",
            "lineNumber": 3964
          },
          {
            "text": "    eliminates this bias.",
            "lineNumber": 3965
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3966
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Auto-bandwidth robustness**",
            "lineNumber": 3967
          },
          {
            "text": "    The default auto-bandwidth uses &#96;&#96;max(1.5 × median-NN, 0.1 × extent)&#96;&#96;,",
            "lineNumber": 3968
          },
          {
            "text": "    where *extent* is the largest dimension of the hard-data bounding box.",
            "lineNumber": 3969
          },
          {
            "text": "    The &#96;&#96;0.1 × extent&#96;&#96; floor prevents the bandwidth from becoming",
            "lineNumber": 3970
          },
          {
            "text": "    excessively narrow (&lt; 5% of domain size) when data contain closely-spaced",
            "lineNumber": 3971
          },
          {
            "text": "    survey points that pull the median NN distance down.  The LOOCV option",
            "lineNumber": 3972
          },
          {
            "text": "    provides a fully data-driven, objective bandwidth.",
            "lineNumber": 3973
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3974
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Relationship to Ordinary Kriging**",
            "lineNumber": 3975
          },
          {
            "text": "    OK implicitly estimates a local mean via the unbiasedness constraint.",
            "lineNumber": 3976
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;method='kernel'&#96;&#96; approximates this by kernel-smoothing the hard data.",
            "lineNumber": 3977
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;method='localmeanBME'&#96;&#96; goes further: it uses GLS to account for",
            "lineNumber": 3978
          },
          {
            "text": "    spatial autocorrelation in the regression, giving the best linear",
            "lineNumber": 3979
          },
          {
            "text": "    unbiased estimate of the mean trend.",
            "lineNumber": 3980
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3981
          },
          {
            "text": "    Examples",
            "lineNumber": 3982
          },
          {
            "text": "    --------",
            "lineNumber": 3983
          },
          {
            "text": "    Basic usage — kernel-smoothed prior from hard data only:",
            "lineNumber": 3984
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3985
          },
          {
            "text": "    &gt;&gt;&gt; order_arr = BMEpriorMean(ck, ch, zh, cs=cs, zs=zs_list,",
            "lineNumber": 3986
          },
          {
            "text": "    ...                               method='kernel', bandwidth=5000.0)",
            "lineNumber": 3987
          },
          {
            "text": "    &gt;&gt;&gt; result = BMEPosteriorMoments(",
            "lineNumber": 3988
          },
          {
            "text": "    ...     ck, ch=ch, cs=cs, zh=zh, zs=zs_list,",
            "lineNumber": 3989
          },
          {
            "text": "    ...     covmodel=['exponentialC'], covparam=[(30.0, 8000.0)],",
            "lineNumber": 3990
          },

            "text": "    ...     order=order_arr, nhmax=12, nsmax=4,",
            "lineNumber": 3991
          },

            "text": "    ...     dmax=np.array([[15000.0]]))",
            "lineNumber": 3992
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3993
          },
          {
            "text": "    LOOCV bandwidth selection (data-driven optimal):",
            "lineNumber": 3994
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3995
          },
          {
            "text": "    &gt;&gt;&gt; order_cv = BMEpriorMean(ck, ch, zh, cs=cs, zs=zs_list,",
            "lineNumber": 3996
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 3998
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3999
          },
          {
            "text": "    GLS-based prior (most rigorous, needs covmodel/covparam):",

            "text": "def neighbours_separable(",

          },

            "lineNumber": 473
          },

            "text": "        # Kish effective sample size",

          },

          {

          },

          },

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "        # Shrinkage coefficient: decays toward 0 as N_eff grows",

          },

          },

          },

          {
            "text": "def MPLestimator(active_constraints, ndim, nc, tol):",
            "lineNumber": 963,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 964
          },
          {
            "text": "    Fits a MaxEnt PDF using non-regularized Maximum Pseudo-Likelihood (MPL).",
            "lineNumber": 965
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 966
          },
          {
            "text": "    This estimator is a composite likelihood method. It finds the parameters",
            "lineNumber": 967
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;mu&#96; for each bivariate marginal *independently* and then combines them.",
            "lineNumber": 968
          },
          {
            "text": "    It is fast but ignores higher-order interactions and can be unstable",
            "lineNumber": 969
          },
          {
            "text": "    if target probabilities are 0 or 1.",
            "lineNumber": 970
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 971
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 972
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 973
          },
          {
            "text": "    active_constraints : list",
            "lineNumber": 974
          },
          {
            "text": "        A list of tuples, &#96;&#96;[((i, j), Pbiv_table), ...]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 975
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;(i, j)&#96;&#96;: A tuple of the two dimension indices.",
            "lineNumber": 976
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;Pbiv_table&#96;&#96;: The &#96;&#96;(nc, nc)&#96;&#96; target probability table.",
            "lineNumber": 977
          },
          {
            "text": "    ndim : int",
            "lineNumber": 978
          },
          {
            "text": "        The total number of dimensions (e.g., estimation point + neighbors).",
            "lineNumber": 979
          },
          {
            "text": "    nc : int",
            "lineNumber": 980
          },
          {
            "text": "        The number of categories.",
            "lineNumber": 981
          },
          {
            "text": "    tol : float",
            "lineNumber": 982
          },
          {
            "text": "        The convergence tolerance for the L-BFGS-B optimizer.",
            "lineNumber": 983
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 984
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 985
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 986
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pfit : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 987
          },
          {
            "text": "        The fitted multivariate probability table, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, ..., nc)&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 988
          },
          {
            "text": "        with &#96;ndim&#96; dimensions.",
            "lineNumber": 989
          },
          {
            "text": "    niter : int",
            "lineNumber": 990
          },
          {
            "text": "        The number of function evaluations from the optimizer.",
            "lineNumber": 991
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 992
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 993
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- START LOGIC FIX --- (This part is OK)",
            "lineNumber": 994
          },
          {
            "text": "    nbiv = len(active_constraints) # O(n*k) or O(n^2)",
            "lineNumber": 995
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_0 = np.zeros(nbiv*nc*nc)",
            "lineNumber": 996
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pbiv_vec = np.zeros([nbiv,nc*nc])",
            "lineNumber": 997
          },
          {
            "text": "    idx = np.zeros([nbiv, 2], dtype=np.int16)",
            "lineNumber": 998
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 999
          },
          {
            "text": "    for k, (pair, Pbiv_table) in enumerate(active_constraints):",
            "lineNumber": 1000
          },
          {
            "text": "        i, j = pair",
            "lineNumber": 1001
          },
          {
            "text": "        if Pbiv_table is None or len(Pbiv_table) == 0:",
            "lineNumber": 1002
          },
          {
            "text": "            Pbiv_ravel = np.full((nc*nc), np.nan)",
            "lineNumber": 1003
          },
          {
            "text": "        else:",
            "lineNumber": 1004
          },
          {
            "text": "            Pbiv_ravel = Pbiv_table.ravel()",
            "lineNumber": 1005
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1006
          },
          {
            "text": "        # --- START CONVERGENCE FIX --- (This is OK)",
            "lineNumber": 1007
          },
          {
            "text": "        if not np.all(np.isnan(Pbiv_ravel)):",
            "lineNumber": 1008
          },
          {
            "text": "            eps = 1e-10",
            "lineNumber": 1009
          },
          {
            "text": "            Pbiv_ravel = np.clip(Pbiv_ravel, eps, 1.0 - (eps * nc * nc))",

          },
          {
            "text": "            if np.nansum(Pbiv_ravel) &gt; 0:",

          },
          {

          },

          },

          },

          {
            "text": "# --- START: New tune_regularization_loocv function ---",
            "lineNumber": 1903
          },
          {
            "text": "def tune_regularization_loocv(cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, reg_grid, base_options=None):",
            "lineNumber": 1904,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1905
          },
          {
            "text": "    Tunes the regularization hyperparameter 'reg' using Leave-One-Out (LOOCV).",
            "lineNumber": 1906
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1907
          },
          {
            "text": "    Predicts each data point &#96;i&#96; using all *other* data points and finds the",
            "lineNumber": 1908
          },
          {
            "text": "    'reg' value from &#96;reg_grid&#96; that maximizes the total log-likelihood",
            "lineNumber": 1909
          },
          {
            "text": "    of the \"held-out\" predictions.",
            "lineNumber": 1910
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1911
          },
          {
            "text": "    Note: This is intended for 'MLE_reg' or 'ME_dual' estimators.",
            "lineNumber": 1912
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1913
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 1914
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 1915
          },
          {
            "text": "    cs : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1916
          },
          {
            "text": "        Data point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(n, d)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1917
          },
          {
            "text": "    ps : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1918
          },
          {
            "text": "        Soft data (PDFs) at data points, shape &#96;&#96;(n, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1919
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1920
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of distances for &#96;Pmodel&#96;, shape &#96;&#96;(nd,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1921
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1922
          },
          {
            "text": "        3D array of bivariate probability tables, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, nc, nd)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1923
          },
          {
            "text": "    nsmax : int",
            "lineNumber": 1924
          },
          {
            "text": "        Maximum number of neighbors to use.",
            "lineNumber": 1925
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmax : float",
            "lineNumber": 1926
          },
          {
            "text": "        Maximum search distance.",
            "lineNumber": 1927
          },
          {
            "text": "    reg_grid : list or np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1928
          },
          {
            "text": "        A list of 'reg' values to test (e.g., [1e-8, 1e-7, 1e-6]).",
            "lineNumber": 1929
          },
          {
            "text": "    base_options : dict, optional",
            "lineNumber": 1930
          },
          {
            "text": "        Other options for BMEcatPdf (e.g., 'tol', 'model_structure',",
            "lineNumber": 1931
          },
          {
            "text": "        'estimator'). 'estimator' should be 'MLE_reg' or 'ME_dual'.",
            "lineNumber": 1932
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1933
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 1934
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 1935
          },
          {
            "text": "    scores : dict",
            "lineNumber": 1936
          },
          {
            "text": "        A dictionary of {reg: total_log_likelihood} scores.",
            "lineNumber": 1937
          },
          {
            "text": "    best_reg : float",
            "lineNumber": 1938
          },
          {
            "text": "        The 'reg' value from &#96;reg_grid&#96; with the highest score.",
            "lineNumber": 1939
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1940
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1941
          },
          {
            "text": "    if base_options is None:",
            "lineNumber": 1942
          },
          {
            "text": "        base_options = {}",
            "lineNumber": 1943
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1944
          },
          {
            "text": "    if 'estimator' not in base_options:",
            "lineNumber": 1945
          },
          {
            "text": "        print(\"Warning: 'estimator' not in base_options. Defaulting to 'MLE_reg' for tuning.\")",
            "lineNumber": 1946
          },
          {
            "text": "        base_options['estimator'] = 'MLE_reg'",
            "lineNumber": 1947
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1948
          },
          {
            "text": "    n_data = cs.shape[0]",
            "lineNumber": 1949
          },
          {
            "text": "    scores = {}",
            "lineNumber": 1950
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1951
          },
          {
            "text": "    print(f\"--- Starting LOOCV Hyperparameter Tuning ---\")",
            "lineNumber": 1952
          },
          {
            "text": "    print(f\"Testing {n_data} data points with {len(reg_grid)} reg values...\")",
            "lineNumber": 1953
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1954
          },
          {
            "text": "    for reg in reg_grid:",
            "lineNumber": 1955
          },
          {
            "text": "        current_options = base_options.copy()",
            "lineNumber": 1956
          }
        ]
      },

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def MLEestimator(active_constraints, ndim, nc, tol, reg=0.1):",

          },

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "        # --- START CONVERGENCE FIX --- (This is OK)",
            "lineNumber": 828
          },
          {
            "text": "        if not np.all(np.isnan(Pbiv_ravel)):",
            "lineNumber": 829
          },
          {
            "text": "            eps = 1e-10",
            "lineNumber": 830
          },
          {
            "text": "            Pbiv_ravel = np.clip(Pbiv_ravel, eps, 1.0 - (eps * nc * nc))",
            "lineNumber": 831
          },
          {
            "text": "            if np.nansum(Pbiv_ravel) &gt; 0:",
            "lineNumber": 832
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 833
          },
          {
            "text": "        # --- END CONVERGENCE FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 834
          },
          {
            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 835
          },
          {
            "text": "        Pbiv_vec[k] = Pbiv_ravel",
            "lineNumber": 836
          },
          {
            "text": "        idx[k,:]=[i,j]",
            "lineNumber": 837
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- END LOGIC FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 838
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 839
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pbiv_all=Pbiv_vec.reshape(nbiv*nc*nc)",
            "lineNumber": 840
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 841
          },
          {
            "text": "    res = minimize(likeli_MLE, mu_0, method='L-BFGS-B', jac=likeli_diff_MLE",
            "lineNumber": 842
          },
          {
            "text": "                   ,args=(Pbiv_all, reg, nbiv, nc) ",
            "lineNumber": 843
          },
          {
            "text": "                   ,options={'disp': False,'ftol':tol}) ",
            "lineNumber": 844
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 845
          },
          {
            "text": "    niter = res.nfev",

          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 847
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_mat = (res.x).reshape(nbiv, nc, nc) # Reshape to (nbiv, nc, nc)",
            "lineNumber": 848
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 849
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- START BROADCASTING FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 850
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Create a dictionary to map (i, j) pairs to their mu_k table",
            "lineNumber": 851
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_dict = {tuple(idx[k]): mu_mat[k] for k in range(nbiv)}",

          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 853
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pfit = np.zeros([nc]*ndim) # Calculate maximum entropy pdf",
            "lineNumber": 854
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 855
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Loop over all possible (i, j) pairs, just like GIS/IIS",
            "lineNumber": 856
          },
          {
            "text": "    for i in range(ndim):",
            "lineNumber": 857
          },
          {
            "text": "        for j in range(i + 1, ndim):",
            "lineNumber": 858
          },
          {
            "text": "            # Check if this pair (i, j) has an active constraint",
            "lineNumber": 859
          },
          {
            "text": "            if (i, j) in mu_dict:",
            "lineNumber": 860
          },
          {
            "text": "                mu_k = mu_dict[(i, j)]",
            "lineNumber": 861
          },
          {
            "text": "                ",
            "lineNumber": 862
          },
          {
            "text": "                # Create a (1, 1, ..., nc, ..., nc, ..., 1) shape",
            "lineNumber": 863
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 864
          },
          {

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "                # Reshape mu[k] and add to Pfit",

          },
          {
            "text": "                Pfit += mu_k.reshape(broadcast_shape)",
            "lineNumber": 869
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- END BROADCASTING FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 870
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 871
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- FIX: Use stable softmax for final Pfit --- (This is OK)",
            "lineNumber": 872
          },
          {

          },

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 875
          }

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py",

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def BMEcatPdf(ck, cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, options=None):",
            "lineNumber": 1613,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1738
          },
          {
            "text": "    for i in range(nk):",
            "lineNumber": 1739
          },
          {
            "text": "        ck0=ck[[i],:]",
            "lineNumber": 1740
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1741
          },
          {
            "text": "        ## V~d臨近的位置 ds為每個被找的點與ck0之距離 sumnslocal為總共找到的已知點數 ck0為未知點位, cs與ps分別為已知點位與機率",
            "lineNumber": 1742
          },
          {
            "text": "        ## cslocal,pslocal分別為鄰近已知點座標與機率",
            "lineNumber": 1743
          },
          {
            "text": "        if sep_bme is not None:",
            "lineNumber": 1744
          },
          {
            "text": "            cslocal, pslocal, ds, sumnslocal, _, _dcomp, _p_local_k = neighbours_separable(",
            "lineNumber": 1745
          },
          {
            "text": "                ck0,",
            "lineNumber": 1746
          },
          {
            "text": "                cs,",
            "lineNumber": 1747
          },
          {
            "text": "                ps,",
            "lineNumber": 1748
          },
          {
            "text": "                nsmax,",
            "lineNumber": 1749
          },
          {
            "text": "                sep_bme['components'],",
            "lineNumber": 1750
          },
          {
            "text": "                options=options,",
            "lineNumber": 1751
          },
          {
            "text": "                p_marginal=sep_bme.get('p_marginal'),",
            "lineNumber": 1752
          },
          {
            "text": "                mode=sep_bme.get('mode', 'product'),",
            "lineNumber": 1753
          },
          {
            "text": "            )",
            "lineNumber": 1754
          },
          {
            "text": "        else:",
            "lineNumber": 1755
          },
          {
            "text": "            cslocal, pslocal, ds, sumnslocal, _ = neighbours(",
            "lineNumber": 1756
          },
          {
            "text": "                ck0, cs, ps, nsmax, dmax, options=options)",
            "lineNumber": 1757
          },
          {
            "text": "            _p_local_k = None   # not available in 1-D path",
            "lineNumber": 1758
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1759
          },
          {
            "text": "        # --- Determine the desired no-data-limit target q_eff(c) ---",
            "lineNumber": 1760
          },
          {
            "text": "        #",
            "lineNumber": 1761
          },
          {
            "text": "        # The ME table has p_global baked into every axis marginal.  For the",
            "lineNumber": 1762
          },
          {
            "text": "        # BME posterior to converge to a target q_eff(c) when no neighbours",
            "lineNumber": 1763
          },
          {
            "text": "        # are found, we must pass prior_to_use = q_eff / p_global (normalised)",
            "lineNumber": 1764
          },
          {
            "text": "        # into producttablepdf — the p_global in S(c) then cancels.",
            "lineNumber": 1765
          },
          {
            "text": "        #",
            "lineNumber": 1766
          },
          {
            "text": "        # Three cases based on which information sources are active:",
            "lineNumber": 1767
          },
          {
            "text": "        #",
            "lineNumber": 1768
          },
          {
            "text": "        #   Case A — external prior AND local_marginal",
            "lineNumber": 1769
          },
          {
            "text": "        #     q_eff(c) = p_local(c) × q_XGB(c) / p_global(c)   (composite)",
            "lineNumber": 1770
          },
          {
            "text": "        #     → sparse-data limit: posterior ∝ p_local × XGB-odds",
            "lineNumber": 1771
          },
          {
            "text": "        #     → uninformative XGB (q_XGB≈p_global): reduces to p_local  ✓",
            "lineNumber": 1772
          },
          {
            "text": "        #     → no local variation (p_local≈p_global): reduces to q_XGB ✓",
            "lineNumber": 1773
          },
          {
            "text": "        #",
            "lineNumber": 1774
          },
          {
            "text": "        #   Case B — local_marginal only (no external prior)",
            "lineNumber": 1775
          },
          {
            "text": "        #     q_eff(c) = p_local(c)",
            "lineNumber": 1776
          },
          {
            "text": "        #     → sparse-data limit: posterior → p_local             ✓",
            "lineNumber": 1777
          },
          {
            "text": "        #",
            "lineNumber": 1778
          },
          {
            "text": "        #   Default — external prior only (original BF)",
            "lineNumber": 1779
          },
          {
            "text": "        #     q_eff(c) = q_XGB(c)",
            "lineNumber": 1780

## 1. Confusion Matrix — Code to Add

The `station_loocv` function already collects `post_all` and `true_all`. The cleanest way is to modify it to return the raw arrays, then compute the matrix outside. Here is the revised LOOCV block to add to `pingtung_estimation.py` (or a new notebook cell):

```python
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix, classification_report, balanced_accuracy_score

def station_loocv_full(method_fn, coords, ps, dmodel_list, Pmodel_list,
                       station_ids, categories, nsmax, options,
                       use_xgb_prior=False, cs_features=None):
    """Same as station_loocv but returns (acc, mll, bal_acc, true_arr, pred_arr)."""
    unique_st = np.unique(station_ids)
    all_post, all_true = [], []
    base_opts = {**options, 'category_codes': categories}
    for st in unique_st:
        tr = station_ids != st
        te = station_ids == st
        fold_opts = dict(base_opts)
        if use_xgb_prior and cs_features is not None:
            with warnings.catch_warnings():
                warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
                ext, _ = BMEcatPrior(
                    ck=coords[te], cs=coords[tr], ps=ps[tr],
                    ck_features=cs_features[te], cs_features=cs_features[tr],
                    method='xgboostlss', cv_config={'n_trials': 0},
                    categories=categories, verbose=False, return_details=True)
            fold_opts['prior_pdf_at_ck'] = ext
        post = method_fn(coords[te], coords[tr], ps[tr],
                         dmodel_list, Pmodel_list, nsmax, None,
                         options=fold_opts)
        all_post.append(post)
        all_true.append(ps[te])

    post_all = np.vstack(all_post)
    true_all = np.concatenate(all_true)
    cats     = np.asarray(categories)
    pred_all = cats[np.argmax(post_all, axis=1)]
    acc      = float(np.mean(pred_all == true_all))
    bal_acc  = balanced_accuracy_score(true_all, pred_all)
    ti       = np.searchsorted(categories, true_all)
    mll      = float(np.mean(np.log(np.clip(
        post_all[np.arange(len(true_all)), ti], 1e-15, None))))
    return acc, mll, bal_acc, true_all, pred_all


# --- Run LOOCV for all three methods ---
acc_mcp, mll_mcp, bal_mcp, y_true_mcp, y_pred_mcp = station_loocv_full(
    MCPcatPdf, cs_bme, ps_bme, [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel],
    station_ids, LITHO_CODES, nsmax_3d, bme_opts_3d)

acc_bme, mll_bme, bal_bme, y_true_bme, y_pred_bme = station_loocv_full(
    BMEcatPdf, cs_bme, ps_bme, [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel],
    station_ids, LITHO_CODES, nsmax_3d, bme_opts_3d)

acc_xgb, mll_xgb, bal_xgb, y_true_xgb, y_pred_xgb = station_loocv_full(
    BMEcatPdf, cs_bme, ps_bme, [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel],
    station_ids, LITHO_CODES, nsmax_3d, bme_opts_3d,
    use_xgb_prior=True, cs_features=X_well)


# --- Plot confusion matrices ---
method_info = [
    ('MCPcatPdf + local',      y_true_mcp,  y_pred_mcp,  acc_mcp,  bal_mcp),
    ('BMEcatPdf + local',      y_true_bme,  y_pred_bme,  acc_bme,  bal_bme),
    ('BMEcatPdf + composite',  y_true_xgb,  y_pred_xgb,  acc_xgb,  bal_xgb),
]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 5))
for ax, (title, y_true, y_pred, acc, bal) in zip(axes, method_info):
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=LITHO_CODES, normalize='true')
    im = ax.imshow(cm, vmin=0, vmax=1, cmap='Blues')
    ax.set_xticks(range(nc)); ax.set_xticklabels(LITHO_LABELS, rotation=30, ha='right')
    ax.set_yticks(range(nc)); ax.set_yticklabels(LITHO_LABELS)
    ax.set_xlabel('Predicted'); ax.set_ylabel('True')
    ax.set_title(f'{title}\nAcc={acc:.3f}  BalAcc={bal:.3f}')
    for i in range(nc):
        for j in range(nc):
            ax.text(j, i, f'{cm[i,j]:.2f}',
                    ha='center', va='center',
                    color='white' if cm[i,j] > 0.5 else 'black', fontsize=9)
    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.04)

plt.suptitle('LOOCV confusion matrices (row-normalised)', fontsize=12)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, 'fig11_loocv_confusion.png'), dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')

# Per-class report
for title, y_true, y_pred in [(t, yt, yp) for t, yt, yp, *_ in method_info]:
    print(f'\n=== {title} ===')
    print(classification_report(y_true, y_pred, target_names=LITHO_LABELS))
```

The **row-normalised** matrix shows the recall per class: diagonal = fraction of that class correctly identified. This immediately reveals whether the model is collapsing into Gravel.

---

## 2. Understanding the 54.2% Accuracy

Before declaring 54.2% "bad", compare to the **majority-class baseline**. Based on the long history of this problem, Gravel dominates at roughly **47–55%** of samples. If `naive_accuracy ≈ 0.50`, then 54.2% is only marginally better — confirming the model is close to the Gravel baseline. 

**Balanced accuracy** (average per-class recall) is the right metric here: a model that predicts Gravel everywhere would score ~25% balanced accuracy despite ~50% overall accuracy. If your BME balanced accuracy is similar to 25%, the model is not learning much spatial structure.

---

## 3. Improvement Ideas (Ranked by Expected Impact)

### A. Use `HBMEcatPdf` — Already in the Codebase

There is already a `HBMEcatPdf` function in `BMEcatPdf.py` (line 2548). It is a two-step **Hybrid BME**:

1. **MCP regional prior** (large radius, up to ~20 neighbours) — captures the regional lithological trend without ME table solving overhead.
2. **BME local update** (small radius, 4–6 closest neighbours) — rigorously accounts for local spatial structure.

This resolves the tension between "need many neighbours for the prior" and "ME table becomes ill-conditioned with many neighbours". You can try:

```python
from stamps.bme.BMEcatPdf import HBMEcatPdf

hbme_opts = {
    'auto_dmax':         True,
    'auto_dmax_mcp':     True,
    'category_codes':    LITHO_CODES,
    'neighbour_ranking': 'tv',
    'local_marginal':    True,
    'nsmax_total':       16,    # MCP uses up to 16 neighbours
    'use_annular_mcp':   True,  # strict data independence between steps
}
result_hbme = HBMEcatPdf(
    ck_bme, cs_bme, ps_bme, dmodel, Pmodel,  # NOTE: 1D Pmodel for HBME
    nsmax=6, dmax=None, options=hbme_opts)
```

---

### B. Increase `nsmax` and Test Sensitivity

With only **8 neighbours** in a 3D separable search, many estimation locations (especially in the horizontal plane where data is sparse) may find fewer than 4 actual neighbours. Try `nsmax=12` or `nsmax=16`. The ME solver can degrade with many neighbours, but MCP handles this more gracefully. The key diagnostic is to print `mean(nsub)` during estimation.

---

### C. Better XGBoostLSS Features — Spatial Trend Components

Currently features are: `Z, Height, Formation Factor, inResModel, Testing_Distance, Corner_Distance_1/2/3, Basin_*`.

Candidate additions that would help capture spatial non-stationarity:
- **Polynomial spatial trend**: `X`, `Y`, `X²`, `Y²`, `X·Y` — captures broad N–S or E–W lithological trends in the Pingtung plain
- **Distance to mountain front** (alluvial fan apex) — a dominant geological control on gravel/sand/clay lateral distribution
- **Z × Distance to mountain front** interaction — proximal deep = gravel; distal shallow = fine sediment
- **Geomorphic unit proxy** — the `Basin` variable is coarse; finer geomorphic zonation would help

---

### D. Separate Coarse Merging for Evaluation

Fine sand (code 2) and Sand (code 3) are both sandy classes with similar spatial behavior. If the confusion matrix shows these two are consistently swapped, consider **evaluating on a 3-class scheme** (Clay / Sandy / Gravel) to reveal whether the model is capturing the coarse structure correctly. This also helps interpret whether 54% is fundamentally limited by the data or by the model.

---

### E. Anisotropic Pmodel

The current Pmodel passes isotropic horizontal distances. But `estimate_anisotropy_from_ptables` already computes `theta_hat` (principal axis angle) and `r_hat` (anisotropy ratio). If `r_hat` deviates meaningfully from 1.0 (say < 0.6 or > 1.6), transforming horizontal coordinates before building the Pmodel (stretching along the minor axis) would improve the correlation structure.

The coordinate transform is:

```python
# cos/sin rotation + axis rescaling
theta = theta_hat   # principal axis angle
scale = r_hat       # minor/major ratio
R = np.array([[np.cos(theta), -np.sin(theta)],
              [np.sin(theta),  np.cos(theta)]])
T = np.diag([1.0, 1.0 / scale])   # stretch minor axis
transform = T @ R

station_xy_aniso = (transform @ station_xy.T).T
xy_all_aniso     = (transform @ wells[['X','Y']].values.T).T
ck_aniso         = np.column_stack([(transform @ ck_bme[:, :2].T).T, ck_bme[:, 2]])
cs_aniso         = np.column_stack([(transform @ cs_bme[:, :2].T).T, cs_bme[:, 2]])
```

Then run the full pipeline on `*_aniso` coordinates.

---

### F. LOOCV at Depth Level, Not Station Level

The current LOOCV holds out **entire boreholes**. This is a realistic scenario (predicting at a new borehole location) but produces high variance because nearby boreholes are still in the training set. An alternative is **leave-one-depth-level-out** per borehole — hold out a single Z-sample within each borehole — which better reflects the interpolation use case and will give higher (but more optimistic) accuracy.

The opposite — **spatial block validation** — is more conservative: hold out all boreholes within a spatial block (e.g., 5 km radius). This reveals how performance degrades at prediction locations far from any data, which is critical in a sparse dataset like Pingtung.

---

### G. Class-Weighted XGBoost Training

XGBoostLSS for Dirichlet regression doesn't support `scale_pos_weight` directly, but you can pass **sample weights** inversely proportional to class frequency to the training call. This forces the model to predict non-Gravel distributions in Gravel-dominated regions when other features suggest otherwise. You'd modify `BMEcatPrior`'s internal call to accept sample weights.

---

### H. Per-Layer (Z-Level) Marginal as p_local Override

Even with `local_marginal=True`, if the kernel bandwidth is large (= `dmax/3` ≈ few km), the kernel-smoothed `p_local` near data-sparse areas collapses toward `p_global`. A simpler per-layer marginal can help:

```python
# Compute exact class proportions at each Z-level
layer_marginals = {}
for zval in np.unique(wells['Z']):
    m = wells['Z'] == zval
    props = [(wells.loc[m, 'LithoCode'] == c).mean() for c in LITHO_CODES]
    layer_marginals[zval] = np.array(props)
```

Then pass `layer_marginals[z_at_ck]` as the prior at each estimation node. This avoids the kernel bandwidth problem entirely for the Z dimension.

---

| Confusion matrix / balanced acc. | Low | Diagnostic only | None |
| `HBMEcatPdf` | Low (already coded) | Medium–High | Needs 1D Pmodel |
| Increase `nsmax` to 12–16 | Very low | Low–Medium | Slower |
| Add X/Y spatial features to XGB | Medium | Medium | Overfitting |
| Anisotropic coordinate transform | Medium | Medium | Needs validation |
| Spatial block CV | Medium | Diagnostic | More pessimistic |
| Class-weighted XGB | High | Medium | API change |
| Per-layer marginal prior | Low | Low–Medium | Sharp transitions |

          },
          {
            "text": "def MCPcatPdf(ck, cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, options=None):",
            "lineNumber": 2241,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Estimate categorical PDF using Maximum Conditional Probability (MCP).",
            "lineNumber": 2242
          },

            "lineNumber": 2243
          },
          {
            "text": "    A fast log-space approximation of BME that assumes conditional independence",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2246
          },

            "text": "    Parameters",

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 2253
          },
          {
