            "lineNumber": 2254
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2255
          },
          {
            "text": "        * If values are in &#96;&#96;0 … nc-1&#96;&#96; they are used as column indices.",
            "lineNumber": 2256
          },
          {
            "text": "        * Otherwise the function auto-infers &#96;&#96;category_codes&#96;&#96; from",
            "lineNumber": 2257
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;np.sort(np.unique(ps))&#96;&#96; (assuming sorted codes match Pmodel",
            "lineNumber": 2258
          },
          {
            "text": "          row order).  Provide &#96;&#96;options['category_codes']&#96;&#96; explicitly",
            "lineNumber": 2259
          },
          {
            "text": "          for non-sorted or custom orderings.",
            "lineNumber": 2260
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2261
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmodel : (nd,) ndarray **or** list of (nd_k,) arrays",
            "lineNumber": 2262
          },
          {
            "text": "        Tabulated distances for the Pmodel.",
            "lineNumber": 2263
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2264
          },
          {
            "text": "        * **1-D mode** — a single 1-D array, shape &#96;&#96;(nd,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2265
          },
          {
            "text": "        * **Separable mode** — a Python list of per-axis arrays",

          },

          },

            "lineNumber": 2268
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2269
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pmodel : (nc, nc, nd) ndarray **or** list of such arrays",
            "lineNumber": 2270
          },
          {
            "text": "        Bivariate probability tables.",
            "lineNumber": 2271
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2272
          },
          {
            "text": "        * **1-D mode** — shape &#96;&#96;(nc, nc, nd)&#96;&#96;.",

          },
          {
            "text": "        * **Separable mode** — list &#96;&#96;[Pmodel_h, Pmodel_v, …]&#96;&#96; whose",

            "text": "          length matches &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96;.",

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2281
          },
          {
            "text": "        * **1-D mode** — scalar float.  Ignored when &#96;&#96;auto_dmax=True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2282
          },
          {
            "text": "        * **Separable mode** — &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96; (all axes use &#96;&#96;auto_dmax&#96;&#96;), a",

          },

          },

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'product'&#96;&#96; (Carle–Fogg chain) or &#96;&#96;'additive'&#96;&#96;.  Ignored for 1-D.",
            "lineNumber": 2290
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2291
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'p_marginal'&#96;&#96; *(array, optional)* — category marginal proportions",

          },

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "        effective correlation range from :func:&#96;_find_effective_range&#96;.",

          },

            "lineNumber": 2307
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96; *(float, default &#96;&#96;0.05&#96;&#96;)* — TV threshold",

          },
          {
            "text": "        for &#96;&#96;auto_dmax&#96;&#96;.",

          },

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 2486
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2487
          },
          {
            "text": "        # --- 5c. Calculate the log of the likelihood product term ---",
            "lineNumber": 2488
          },
          {
            "text": "        # This is SUM_k [ log( P(X_k | X_0) ) ]",

          },
          {
            "text": "        log_likelihood_sum = np.zeros(nc)",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2491
          },
          {
            "text": "        # Loop over each of the 'n' neighbors",

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 2495
          },
          {

          },

            "text": "            if sep_opt is not None:",

          },

          },

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "                Pmodels_s = [c['Pmodel'] for c in comps]",
            "lineNumber": 2501
          },
          {
            "text": "                p_m = np.asarray(sep_opt['p_marginal'], dtype=float).ravel()",
            "lineNumber": 2502
          },
          {
            "text": "                mode_s = sep_opt.get('mode', 'product')",

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "            else:",

          },
          {
            "text": "                d_k = dsub[k]",

          },
          {
            "text": "                biv_k0 = probamodel2bitable(d_k, dmodel, Pmodel)",

          },

            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 2509
          },
          {
            "text": "            # sum_term[j] = SUM_i [ P(X_k=i, X_0=j) * P_data(X_k=i) ]",

            "text": "            # This is the term from the original MCP paper for soft data",

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "            # Biv_k0.T.dot(ps_k) is the correct formulation.",
            "lineNumber": 2514
          },

            "text": "            sum_term = biv_k0.T.dot(ps_k)",
            "lineNumber": 2515
          },

            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 2516
          },
          {
            "text": "            # Accumulate the sum of logs",

          },
          {
            "text": "            log_likelihood_sum += np.log(sum_term + 1e-30)",
            "lineNumber": 2518
          },

            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 2519
          },
          {
            "text": "        # --- 6. Calculate the unnormalized posterior in log-space ---",
            "lineNumber": 2520
          },
          {
            "text": "        log_numerator = log_prior_term + log_likelihood_sum",
            "lineNumber": 2521
          },

            "text": "        ",

          },

            "text": "        # --- 7. Normalize using the Log-Sum-Exp trick ---",
            "lineNumber": 2523
          },
          {
            "text": "        # This converts from log-space back to probabilities",

          },

            "text": "        # without underflowing to zero.",

          },
          {
            "text": "        ",
            "lineNumber": 2526
          },
          {
            "text": "        # a. Subtract the max value for numerical stability",
            "lineNumber": 2527
          },
          {
            "text": "        max_log = np.max(log_numerator)",
            "lineNumber": 2528
          },

          },

            "text": "def maxentropytable(c, dmodel, Pmodel, options=None):",

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def _find_effective_range(dmodel, Pmodel, threshold=0.05):",
            "lineNumber": 2149,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2198
          },
          {
            "text": "    p_marginal /= p_marginal.sum()",
            "lineNumber": 2199
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2200
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Independence product  P_indep[c, c'] = p(c) * p(c')",
            "lineNumber": 2201
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_indep = np.outer(p_marginal, p_marginal)",
            "lineNumber": 2202
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2203
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Compute normalised TV at every tabulated distance",
            "lineNumber": 2204
          },
          {
            "text": "    tv = np.zeros(nd)",
            "lineNumber": 2205
          },
          {
            "text": "    for k in range(nd):",
            "lineNumber": 2206
          },
          {
            "text": "        P_k = Pmodel[:, :, k].copy()",
            "lineNumber": 2207
          },
          {
            "text": "        s = P_k.sum()",
            "lineNumber": 2208
          },
          {
            "text": "        if s &gt; 1e-30:",
            "lineNumber": 2209
          },
          {
            "text": "            P_k /= s           # ensure sums to 1",
            "lineNumber": 2210
          },
          {
            "text": "        tv[k] = 0.5 * np.abs(P_k - P_indep).sum()",
            "lineNumber": 2211
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2212
          },
          {
            "text": "    tv_max = tv[0]",
            "lineNumber": 2213
          },
          {
            "text": "    if tv_max &lt; 1e-15:",
            "lineNumber": 2214
          },
          {
            "text": "        # No dependence at all — any dmax is fine; return smallest distance",
            "lineNumber": 2215
          },
          {
            "text": "        return float(dmodel[0])",
            "lineNumber": 2216
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2217
          },
          {
            "text": "    tv_norm = tv / tv_max      # 1 at d=dmodel[0], approaching 0 at large d",
            "lineNumber": 2218
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2219
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Find the first index where tv_norm &lt;= threshold",
            "lineNumber": 2220
          },
          {
            "text": "    below = np.where(tv_norm &lt;= threshold)[0]",
            "lineNumber": 2221
          },
          {
            "text": "    if len(below) == 0:",
            "lineNumber": 2222
          },
          {
            "text": "        # TV never drops below threshold in the tabulated range",
            "lineNumber": 2223
          },
          {
            "text": "        return float(dmodel[-1])",
            "lineNumber": 2224
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2225
          },
          {
            "text": "    idx = below[0]",
            "lineNumber": 2226
          },
          {
            "text": "    if idx == 0:",
            "lineNumber": 2227
          },
          {
            "text": "        return float(dmodel[0])",
            "lineNumber": 2228
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2229
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Linear interpolation between dmodel[idx-1] and dmodel[idx]",
            "lineNumber": 2230
          },
          {
            "text": "    d_lo, d_hi   = float(dmodel[idx - 1]), float(dmodel[idx])",
            "lineNumber": 2231
          },
          {
            "text": "    tv_lo, tv_hi = tv_norm[idx - 1],       tv_norm[idx]",
            "lineNumber": 2232
          },
          {
            "text": "    if abs(tv_hi - tv_lo) &lt; 1e-15:",
            "lineNumber": 2233
          },
          {
            "text": "        return d_lo",
            "lineNumber": 2234
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2235
          },
          {
            "text": "    d_range = d_lo + (d_hi - d_lo) * (threshold - tv_lo) / (tv_hi - tv_lo)",
            "lineNumber": 2236
          },
          {
            "text": "    return float(d_range)",
            "lineNumber": 2237,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------",
            "lineNumber": 2238
          },

            "lineNumber": 2239
          },

          },
          {
            "text": "def MCPcatPdf(ck, cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, options=None):",

      "codeBlock": {

        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# --- START: NEW HYBRID BME/MCP FUNCTION ---",
            "lineNumber": 2546
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2547
          },
          {
            "text": "def HBMEcatPdf(ck,cs,ps,dmodel,Pmodel,nsmax,dmax,options = None):",
            "lineNumber": 2548,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2549
          },
          {
            "text": "    Performs Hybrid BME (HBME) categorical data prediction.",
            "lineNumber": 2550
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 2551
          },
          {
            "text": "    This function implements a two-step hybrid approach:",
            "lineNumber": 2552
          },
          {
            "text": "    1. **Regional prior (MCP step):** Run &#96;MCPcatPdf&#96; with up to &#96;nsmax_total&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2553
          },
          {
            "text": "       neighbours, restricted to &#96;dmax_mcp&#96;, to build a spatially varying",
            "lineNumber": 2554
          },
          {
            "text": "       prior that captures the regional trend.",
            "lineNumber": 2555
          },
          {
            "text": "    2. **Local update (BME step):** Run &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; with the &#96;nsmax&#96; *closest*",
            "lineNumber": 2556
          },
          {
            "text": "       neighbours and &#96;model_structure='full'&#96; to rigorously update the prior,",
            "lineNumber": 2557
          },
          {
            "text": "       correctly accounting for local spatial redundancy.",
            "lineNumber": 2558
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2559
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 2560
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 2561
          },
          {
            "text": "    ck : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2562
          },
          {
            "text": "        Estimation point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, d)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2563
          },
          {
            "text": "    cs : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2564
          },
          {
            "text": "        Data point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(n, d)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2565
          },
          {
            "text": "    ps : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2566
          },
          {
            "text": "        Soft data (PDFs) at data points, shape &#96;&#96;(n, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2567
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2568
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of distances for &#96;Pmodel&#96;, shape &#96;&#96;(nd,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2569
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2570
          },
          {
            "text": "        3D array of bivariate probability tables, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, nc, nd)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2571
          },
          {
            "text": "    nsmax : int",
            "lineNumber": 2572
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of *closest* neighbours for the final BME update step.",
            "lineNumber": 2573
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmax : float",
            "lineNumber": 2574
          },
          {
            "text": "        Maximum search distance for the BME update step (Step 2).",
            "lineNumber": 2575
          },
          {
            "text": "    options : dict, optional",
            "lineNumber": 2576
          },
          {
            "text": "        Dictionary of options:",
            "lineNumber": 2577
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2578
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'nsmax_total'&#96;&#96; (int): Maximum number of neighbours for the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2579
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior step (Step 1). Default &#96;&#96;20&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2580
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2581
          },
          {
            "text": "          .. warning::",
            "lineNumber": 2582
          },
          {
            "text": "             This must be kept **small** (typically 10–25).  At distances",
            "lineNumber": 2583
          },
          {
            "text": "             beyond the covariance correlation range the bivariate table",
            "lineNumber": 2584
          },
          {
            "text": "             factorises to the independence product P(c')·P(c), so each",
            "lineNumber": 2585
          },
          {
            "text": "             out-of-range neighbour contributes &#96;&#96;log P(c)&#96;&#96; to the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2586
          },
          {
            "text": "             log-posterior.  With n decorrelated neighbours the MCP result",
            "lineNumber": 2587
          },
          {
            "text": "             degenerates to the global marginal distribution **P(c), the",
            "lineNumber": 2588
          },
          {
            "text": "             same at every estimation point**, eliminating all spatial",
            "lineNumber": 2589
          },
          {
            "text": "             variation from the prior and making the final HBME map nearly",
            "lineNumber": 2590
          },
          {
            "text": "             flat.  A good starting value is &#96;&#96;nsmax_total ≈ 2–3 × nsmax&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2591
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2592
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (float): Maximum search radius for the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2593
          },
          {
            "text": "          step.  Defaults to &#96;&#96;dmax&#96;&#96;.  **Setting this to the covariance",
            "lineNumber": 2594
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlation range is strongly recommended** so that only spatially",
            "lineNumber": 2595
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlated neighbours contribute to the prior.  Ignored when",
            "lineNumber": 2596
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; is &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2597
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2598
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; is",
            "lineNumber": 2599
          },
          {
            "text": "          **determined automatically** from &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96; and &#96;&#96;Pmodel&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2600
          },
          {
            "text": "          using :func:&#96;_find_effective_range&#96; with the threshold given",
            "lineNumber": 2601
          },
          {
            "text": "          by &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96;.  This ensures the MCP ring radius",
            "lineNumber": 2602
          },
          {
            "text": "          equals the effective decorrelation distance in the bivariate",
            "lineNumber": 2603
          },
          {
            "text": "          model, preventing out-of-range data from contaminating the",
            "lineNumber": 2604
          },
          {
            "text": "          MCP prior.  Default &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2605
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2606
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96; (float): Decorrelation threshold",
            "lineNumber": 2607
          },
          {
            "text": "          for the automatic range detection.  The range is the distance",
            "lineNumber": 2608
          },
          {
            "text": "          at which the normalised total variation between &#96;&#96;Pmodel&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2609
          },
          {
            "text": "          the independence product &#96;&#96;p(c)*p(c')&#96;&#96; drops below this",
            "lineNumber": 2610
          },
          {
            "text": "          fraction.  Default &#96;&#96;0.05&#96;&#96; (5 %).",
            "lineNumber": 2611
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2612
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'use_annular_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96; (default), the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2613
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior is computed using only data in the **ring**",
            "lineNumber": 2614
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;dmax &lt; r &lt;= dmax_mcp&#96;&#96;, i.e. data that lie *outside* the local",
            "lineNumber": 2615
          },
          {
            "text": "          BME update zone.  This gives strict data independence between the",
            "lineNumber": 2616
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior step and the likelihood step (no data leakage).  If",
            "lineNumber": 2617
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96;, MCP uses all data within &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; (original",
            "lineNumber": 2618
          },
          {
            "text": "          behaviour, slightly faster but reuses data).",
            "lineNumber": 2619
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2620
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'global_marginal'&#96;&#96; (np.ndarray, shape &#96;&#96;(nc,)&#96;&#96;): Empirical",
            "lineNumber": 2621
          },
          {
            "text": "          category frequencies &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96;.  When provided, the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2622
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; is passed to BMEcatPdf together with &#96;&#96;global_marginal&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2623
          },
          {
            "text": "          so that the Bayes-factor correction &#96;&#96;q(c)/p(c)&#96;&#96; is applied",
            "lineNumber": 2624
          },
          {
            "text": "          automatically, preventing double-counting of the global",
            "lineNumber": 2625
          },
          {
            "text": "          marginal.  If not provided, &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; is estimated automatically",
            "lineNumber": 2626
          },
          {
            "text": "          from &#96;&#96;ps.mean(axis=0)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2627
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2628
          },
          {
            "text": "        - All other options (e.g., &#96;&#96;'tol'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'reg'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'estimator'&#96;&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 2629
          },
          {
            "text": "          are forwarded to the final &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; update step.",
            "lineNumber": 2630
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'model_structure'&#96;&#96; is *ignored* for the BME step and forced to",
            "lineNumber": 2631
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'full'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2632
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2633
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 2634
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 2635
          },
          {
            "text": "    pk : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2636
          },
          {
            "text": "        The estimated posterior marginal PDFs, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2637
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2638
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 2639
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 2640
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Choosing nsmax_total and dmax_mcp:**",
            "lineNumber": 2641
          },
          {
            "text": "    Let r be the covariance correlation range.  Set &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp ≈ r&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2642
          },
          {
            "text": "    choose &#96;&#96;nsmax_total&#96;&#96; as the expected number of data points within that",
            "lineNumber": 2643
          },
          {
            "text": "    radius (typically 10–25 for datasets of 50–200 points).  Using too many",
            "lineNumber": 2644
          },
          {
            "text": "    decorrelated neighbours (beyond r) causes the MCP prior to converge to",
            "lineNumber": 2645
          },
          {
            "text": "    the global marginal P(c) at every location, destroying spatial variation.",
            "lineNumber": 2646
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2647
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Bayes-factor correction:**",
            "lineNumber": 2648
          },
          {
            "text": "    The Maximum Entropy table solved by &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; carries an implicit",
            "lineNumber": 2649
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; weight (the global marginal).  Passing the MCP result &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2650
          },
          {
            "text": "    directly as a prior therefore weights the final posterior by",
            "lineNumber": 2651
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;q(c) · p(c)&#96;&#96; rather than &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; alone — a subtle double-counting",
            "lineNumber": 2652
          },
          {
            "text": "    of the baseline frequency.  The Bayes-factor correction divides the",
            "lineNumber": 2653
          },
          {
            "text": "    supplied prior by &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; before entering &#96;&#96;producttablepdf&#96;&#96;, so the",
            "lineNumber": 2654
          },
          {
            "text": "    net effect is exactly &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;.  When no prior is given this correction",
            "lineNumber": 2655
          },
          {
            "text": "    is never triggered and the original BME behaviour is preserved.",
            "lineNumber": 2656
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2657
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 2658
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- 1. Setup Options ---",
            "lineNumber": 2659
          },
          {
            "text": "    if options is None:",
            "lineNumber": 2660

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 2145,

        },
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def _find_effective_range(dmodel, Pmodel, threshold=0.05):",
            "lineNumber": 2149,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2150
          },
          {
            "text": "    Estimate the effective correlation range from bivariate probability tables.",
            "lineNumber": 2151
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2152
          },
          {
            "text": "    The function measures the total variation (TV) between the bivariate table",
            "lineNumber": 2153
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;Pmodel[:, :, k]&#96;&#96; and the corresponding **independence product**",
            "lineNumber": 2154
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;p(c) * p(c')&#96;&#96; at each tabulated distance &#96;&#96;dmodel[k]&#96;&#96;.  It then",
            "lineNumber": 2155
          },
          {
            "text": "    returns the interpolated distance at which the normalised TV drops to",
            "lineNumber": 2156
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;threshold&#96;&#96; × its value at the smallest distance.",
            "lineNumber": 2157
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2158
          },
          {
            "text": "    Mathematically:",
            "lineNumber": 2159
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2160
          },
          {
            "text": "    .. math::",
            "lineNumber": 2161
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2162
          },
          {
            "text": "        TV(d) = \\\\frac{1}{2}\\\\sum_{c,c'} \\\\left| P(c,c';d) - p(c)p(c') \\\\right|",
            "lineNumber": 2163
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2164
          },
          {
            "text": "        d^* = \\\\inf\\\\{ d : TV(d)/TV(d_0) \\\\le \\\\text{threshold} \\\\}",
            "lineNumber": 2165
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2166
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 2167
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 2168
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2169
          },
          {
            "text": "        1-D array of tabulated distances, shape &#96;&#96;(nd,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2170
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2171
          },
          {
            "text": "        3-D array of bivariate probability tables, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, nc, nd)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2172
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;Pmodel[:, :, k]&#96;&#96; is the joint table at distance &#96;&#96;dmodel[k]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2173
          },
          {
            "text": "    threshold : float, optional",
            "lineNumber": 2174
          },
          {
            "text": "        Fraction of the zero-distance TV below which the data are considered",
            "lineNumber": 2175
          },
          {
            "text": "        decorrelated.  Default &#96;&#96;0.05&#96;&#96; (5 %).",
            "lineNumber": 2176
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2177
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 2178
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 2179
          },
          {
            "text": "    d_range : float",
            "lineNumber": 2180
          },
          {
            "text": "        Estimated effective correlation range (in the same units as",
            "lineNumber": 2181
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96;).  If the TV never drops below &#96;&#96;threshold&#96;&#96; within the",
            "lineNumber": 2182
          },
          {
            "text": "        range of &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96;, the largest tabulated distance is returned as a",
            "lineNumber": 2183
          },
          {
            "text": "        conservative upper bound.",
            "lineNumber": 2184
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2185
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 2186
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 2187
          },
          {
            "text": "    The marginal &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; is estimated from the table at the **largest**",
            "lineNumber": 2188
          },
          {
            "text": "    tabulated distance (where the table is closest to independence).  If the",
            "lineNumber": 2189
          },
          {
            "text": "    largest-distance table is still far from independence the returned range",
            "lineNumber": 2190
          },
          {
            "text": "    will be a lower bound rather than the true range.",
            "lineNumber": 2191
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2192
          },
          {
            "text": "    nd = len(dmodel)",
            "lineNumber": 2193
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2194
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Estimate marginal p(c) from the table at the largest distance",
            "lineNumber": 2195
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_far = Pmodel[:, :, -1]",
            "lineNumber": 2196
          },
          {
            "text": "    p_marginal = P_far.sum(axis=1)          # sum over c' for each c",
            "lineNumber": 2197
          },
          {
            "text": "    p_marginal = np.clip(p_marginal, 1e-15, None)",
            "lineNumber": 2198
          },
          {
            "text": "    p_marginal /= p_marginal.sum()",
            "lineNumber": 2199
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2200

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },

            "text": "        phi2_angle -= np.pi",
            "lineNumber": 580
          },
          {
            "text": "    phi2_idx = np.argmin(np.abs(angLag - phi2_angle))",
            "lineNumber": 581
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 582
          },
          {
            "text": "    def _directional_contrast(gs, gv):",
            "lineNumber": 583
          },
          {
            "text": "        \"\"\"Compute T_n for a given coordinate set.\"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 584
          },
          {
            "text": "        gv2d = gv if gv.ndim == 2 else gv.reshape(-1, 1)",

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def estimate_anisotropy_params(CC, CCn, angLag, lagr, sill=None):",
            "lineNumber": 341,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Estimate the principal-axis angle and anisotropy ratio from directional covariances.",
            "lineNumber": 342
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 343
          },
          {
            "text": "    Extracts the effective spatial range at each direction from the output of",
            "lineNumber": 344
          },
          {
            "text": "    :func:&#96;polarstcovmap&#96; and fits an anisotropy ellipse to the directional",
            "lineNumber": 345
          },
          {
            "text": "    ranges by weighted least squares.",
            "lineNumber": 346
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 347
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 348
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 349
          },
          {
            "text": "    CC     : list of (nls, nlt) arrays  Directional covariances from",
            "lineNumber": 350
          },
          {
            "text": "             :func:&#96;polarstcovmap&#96;.  Only the purely spatial lag (column 0)",
            "lineNumber": 351
          },
          {
            "text": "             is used.",
            "lineNumber": 352
          },
          {
            "text": "    CCn    : list of (nls, nlt) arrays  Pair counts from :func:&#96;polarstcovmap&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 353
          },
          {
            "text": "    angLag : (na,) array  Directions in radians evaluated by",
            "lineNumber": 354
          },
          {
            "text": "             :func:&#96;polarstcovmap&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 355
          },
          {
            "text": "    lagr   : (nls, nlt) array  Spatial lag meshgrid from :func:&#96;polarstcovmap&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 356
          },
          {
            "text": "    sill   : float, optional  The sill value.  If &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96;, estimated as the",
            "lineNumber": 357
          },
          {
            "text": "             maximum observed covariance across all directions.",
            "lineNumber": 358
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 359
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 360
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 361
          },
          {
            "text": "    theta_hat : float  Estimated principal-axis angle in radians, in",
            "lineNumber": 362
          },
          {
            "text": "                &#96;&#96;(-pi/2, pi/2]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 363
          },
          {
            "text": "    r_hat     : float  Estimated anisotropy ratio (secondary / principal",
            "lineNumber": 364
          },
          {
            "text": "                range), in &#96;&#96;(0, 1]&#96;&#96;.  &#96;&#96;r_hat = 1&#96;&#96; means isotropy.",
            "lineNumber": 365
          },
          {
            "text": "    a_max_hat : float  Estimated principal (maximum) effective range.",
            "lineNumber": 366
          },
          {
            "text": "    a_dirs    : (na,) array  Effective ranges extracted at each direction.",
            "lineNumber": 367
          },
          {
            "text": "    valid     : (na,) bool array  &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96; if an effective range was found",
            "lineNumber": 368
          },
          {
            "text": "                for that direction.",
            "lineNumber": 369
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 370
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 371
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 372
          },
          {
            "text": "    The effective range at direction &#96;&#96;φ&#96;&#96; is defined as the lag &#96;&#96;h&#96;&#96; where",
            "lineNumber": 373
          },
          {
            "text": "    the covariance drops below &#96;&#96;exp(-1)&#96;&#96; times the sill.  The anisotropy",
            "lineNumber": 374
          },
          {
            "text": "    ellipse model is:",
            "lineNumber": 375
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 376
          },
          {
            "text": "    .. math::",
            "lineNumber": 377
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 378
          },
          {
            "text": "        a(\\\\phi) = \\\\frac{a_{max} \\\\cdot r}{\\\\sqrt{r^2 \\\\cos^2(\\\\phi-\\\\theta)",
            "lineNumber": 379
          },
          {
            "text": "                   + \\\\sin^2(\\\\phi-\\\\theta)}}",
            "lineNumber": 380
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 381
          },
          {
            "text": "    The fit minimises the weighted sum of squared residuals with weights",
            "lineNumber": 382
          },
          {
            "text": "    equal to the average pair count at each direction.",
            "lineNumber": 383
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 384
          },
          {
            "text": "    References",
            "lineNumber": 385
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 386
          },
          {
            "text": "    Zimmerman, D.L. (1993). Another look at anisotropy in geostatistics.",
            "lineNumber": 387
          },
          {
            "text": "        *Mathematical Geology*, 25(4), 453–470.",
            "lineNumber": 388
          },
          {
            "text": "        [Directional range ratio as isotropy test statistic.]",

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# ===========================================================================",
            "lineNumber": 797
          },
          {
            "text": "# Categorical / probability-table anisotropy functions",
            "lineNumber": 798
          },
          {
            "text": "# ===========================================================================",
            "lineNumber": 799
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 800
          },
          {
            "text": "def _ptable_range(D, P_diag, p_bg):",
            "lineNumber": 801,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Extract the effective range from one diagonal of a probability table.",
            "lineNumber": 802
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 803
          },
          {
            "text": "    The effective range is defined as the lag &#96;&#96;h&#96;&#96; at which the joint",
            "lineNumber": 804
          },
          {
            "text": "    self-transition departure from the **far-field independence level**",
            "lineNumber": 805
          },
          {
            "text": "    (&#96;&#96;p_c²&#96;&#96;) drops to &#96;&#96;exp(−1)&#96;&#96; of the lag-0 departure:",
            "lineNumber": 806
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 807
          },
          {
            "text": "    .. math::",
            "lineNumber": 808
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 809
          },
          {
            "text": "        a_c = \\\\min\\\\bigl\\\\{h : P_{cc}(h) - p_c^2 \\\\leq",
            "lineNumber": 810
          },
          {
            "text": "              e^{-1}\\\\,[P_{cc}(0) - p_c^2]\\\\bigr\\\\}",
            "lineNumber": 811
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 812
          },
          {
            "text": "    where &#96;&#96;P_{cc}(0) = \\\\mathbb{E}[p_i(c)^2]&#96;&#96; (from self-pairs) and the",
            "lineNumber": 813
          },
          {
            "text": "    far-field independence level is &#96;&#96;p_c^2 = (\\\\mathbb{E}[p_i(c)])^2&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 814
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 815
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Why** &#96;&#96;p_c^2&#96;&#96; **and not** &#96;&#96;p_c&#96;&#96;**?**",
            "lineNumber": 816
          },
          {
            "text": "    The joint probability &#96;&#96;P[c,c,h]&#96;&#96; decays from &#96;&#96;\\\\mathbb{E}[p_i(c)^2]&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 817
          },
          {
            "text": "    at &#96;&#96;h = 0&#96;&#96; down to &#96;&#96;p_c^2&#96;&#96; at large &#96;&#96;h&#96;&#96; (statistical independence).",
            "lineNumber": 818
          },
          {
            "text": "    Using &#96;&#96;p_c&#96;&#96; as the background would give a departure of",
            "lineNumber": 819
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;\\\\mathbb{E}[p_i(c)^2] - p_c ≤ 0&#96;&#96;, which is always non-positive and",
            "lineNumber": 820
          },
          {
            "text": "    makes the range undefined.  Using &#96;&#96;p_c^2&#96;&#96; gives a positive departure",
            "lineNumber": 821
          },
          {
            "text": "    equal to &#96;&#96;\\\\mathrm{Var}(p_i(c)) ≥ 0&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 822
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 823
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 824
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 825
          },
          {
            "text": "    D : (ncl,) array",
            "lineNumber": 826
          },
          {
            "text": "        Mean distances per lag bin (output of :func:&#96;probatablecalc_directional&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 827
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_diag : (ncl,) array",
            "lineNumber": 828
          },
          {
            "text": "        Self-transition values &#96;&#96;P[c, c, :]&#96;&#96; for one class &#96;&#96;c&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 829
          },
          {
            "text": "    p_bg : float",
            "lineNumber": 830
          },
          {
            "text": "        **Far-field independence level** for class &#96;&#96;c&#96;&#96;, equal to &#96;&#96;p_c²&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 831
          },
          {
            "text": "        where &#96;&#96;p_c = E[p_i(c)]&#96;&#96; is the overall marginal proportion.",
            "lineNumber": 832
          },
          {
            "text": "        Do **not** pass the marginal &#96;&#96;p_c&#96;&#96; itself — pass &#96;&#96;p_c ** 2&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 833
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 834
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 835
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 836
          },
          {
            "text": "    range_val : float or NaN",
            "lineNumber": 837
          },
          {
            "text": "        Effective range in the same units as &#96;&#96;D&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 838
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 839
          },
          {
            "text": "    D      = np.asarray(D,      dtype=float)",
            "lineNumber": 840
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_diag = np.asarray(P_diag, dtype=float)",
            "lineNumber": 841
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 842
          },
          {
            "text": "    valid  = ~np.isnan(D) &amp; ~np.isnan(P_diag)",
            "lineNumber": 843
          },
          {
            "text": "    if valid.sum() &lt; 2:",
            "lineNumber": 844
          },
          {
            "text": "        return np.nan",
            "lineNumber": 845
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 846
          },
          {
            "text": "    D_v = D[valid]",
            "lineNumber": 847
          }
        ]

          },

            "lineNumber": 402
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- extract effective range per direction ---",

          },

          },

          },

          {
            "text": "def isotropy_test(grid_s, grid_v, lagr, lagr_tol, angLag, angTol,",
            "lineNumber": 469,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                  method='bootstrap', n_boot=499, alpha=0.05,",
            "lineNumber": 470,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                  covmodel=None, covparam=None, seed=None):",
            "lineNumber": 471,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Formal statistical test of the isotropy hypothesis for 2-D spatial data.",
            "lineNumber": 472
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 473
          },
          {
            "text": "    Implements a tiered scientific workflow for deciding whether the observed",
            "lineNumber": 474
          },
          {
            "text": "    spatial covariance is consistent with isotropy:",
            "lineNumber": 475
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 476
          },
          {
            "text": "    * **'bootstrap'**  Spatial rotation bootstrap directional covariance",
            "lineNumber": 477
          },
          {
            "text": "      contrast test (model-free, recommended for irregular data).",
            "lineNumber": 478
          },
          {
            "text": "    * **'lrt'**        Gaussian likelihood ratio test (requires a fitted",
            "lineNumber": 479
          },
          {
            "text": "      covariance model; &#96;&#96;covmodel&#96;&#96; and &#96;&#96;covparam&#96;&#96; must be provided).",
            "lineNumber": 480
          },
          {
            "text": "    * **'symmetry'**   Axial symmetry screening test (fast, tests a necessary",
            "lineNumber": 481
          },
          {
            "text": "      but not sufficient condition for isotropy).",
            "lineNumber": 482
          },
          {
            "text": "    * **'all'**        Run all three and return combined results.",
            "lineNumber": 483
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 484
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 485
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 486
          },
          {
            "text": "    grid_s    : (n, 2) array  2-D spatial coordinates.",
            "lineNumber": 487
          },
          {
            "text": "    grid_v    : (n,) or (n, nt) array  Observation values.",
            "lineNumber": 488
          },
          {
            "text": "    lagr      : (L,) array  Reference spatial lags for the directional test.",
            "lineNumber": 489
          },
          {
            "text": "    lagr_tol  : (L,) array  Lag tolerances.",
            "lineNumber": 490
          },
          {
            "text": "    angLag    : (na,) array  Directions in radians, in &#96;&#96;(-pi/2, pi/2]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 491
          },
          {
            "text": "    angTol    : (na,) array  Angular tolerances.",
            "lineNumber": 492
          },
          {
            "text": "    method    : str  &#96;&#96;'bootstrap'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'lrt'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'symmetry'&#96;&#96;, or &#96;&#96;'all'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 493
          },
          {
            "text": "    n_boot    : int  Number of bootstrap rotations (default 499).",
            "lineNumber": 494
          },
          {
            "text": "    alpha     : float  Significance level (default 0.05).",
            "lineNumber": 495
          },
          {
            "text": "    covmodel  : list  Covariance model for &#96;&#96;'lrt'&#96;&#96; method.",
            "lineNumber": 496
          },
          {
            "text": "    covparam  : list  Initial covariance parameters for &#96;&#96;'lrt'&#96;&#96; method.",
            "lineNumber": 497
          },
          {
            "text": "    seed      : int or None  Random seed for reproducibility.",
            "lineNumber": 498
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 499
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 500
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 501
          },
          {
            "text": "    result : dict with keys",
            "lineNumber": 502
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'method'&#96;&#96;    — str, method(s) used.",
            "lineNumber": 503
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'test_stat'&#96;&#96; — float or dict, observed test statistic(s).",
            "lineNumber": 504
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'p_value'&#96;&#96;   — float or dict, p-value(s).",
            "lineNumber": 505
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'reject_H0'&#96;&#96; — bool or dict, whether H₀ is rejected.",
            "lineNumber": 506
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'r_hat'&#96;&#96;     — float, estimated anisotropy ratio (effect size).",
            "lineNumber": 507
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'theta_hat'&#96;&#96; — float, estimated principal-axis angle (radians).",
            "lineNumber": 508
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'message'&#96;&#96;   — str, plain-English interpretation.",
            "lineNumber": 509
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 510
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 511
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 512
          },
          {
            "text": "    The **bootstrap test** statistic is:",
            "lineNumber": 513
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 514
          },
          {
            "text": "    .. math::",
            "lineNumber": 515
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 516
          },
          {
            "text": "        T_n = \\\\max_{l=1,\\\\ldots,L} |\\\\hat{C}(h_l, \\\\phi_1) -",
            "lineNumber": 517
          },
          {
            "text": "              \\\\hat{C}(h_l, \\\\phi_2)|",
            "lineNumber": 518
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 519
          },
          {
            "text": "    where &#96;&#96;(φ₁, φ₂)&#96;&#96; are the estimated principal and secondary axes.  The",
            "lineNumber": 520
          },
          {
            "text": "    null distribution is obtained by randomly rotating all coordinates by",
            "lineNumber": 521
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;B&#96;&#96; uniformly drawn angles and recomputing &#96;&#96;T_n&#96;&#96; each time.",
            "lineNumber": 522
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 523
          },
          {
            "text": "    The **LRT** statistic is &#96;&#96;Λ = 2[ℓ(aniso) − ℓ(iso)] ~ χ²(2)&#96;&#96; under",
            "lineNumber": 524
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;H₀&#96;&#96;.  It requires that &#96;&#96;mlecovfitv&#96;&#96; has been run (or can be run",
            "lineNumber": 525
          },
          {
            "text": "    here) for both isotropic and anisotropic models.",
            "lineNumber": 526
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 527
          },
          {
            "text": "    The **symmetry test** checks whether",
            "lineNumber": 528
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;Ĉ(hx, hy) ≈ Ĉ(hy, hx)&#96;&#96; using the covariance map.",
            "lineNumber": 529
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 530
          },
          {
            "text": "    References",
            "lineNumber": 531
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 532
          },
          {
            "text": "    Guan, Y., Sherman, M., &amp; Calvin, J.A. (2004). A nonparametric test for",
            "lineNumber": 533
          },
          {
            "text": "        spatial isotropy using subsampling. *Journal of the American",
            "lineNumber": 534
          },

            "lineNumber": 535
          },

            "text": "        [Test statistic concept; rotation bootstrap replaces subsampling for",

          },

            "text": "        small n.]",

          },
          {
            "text": "    Maity, A. &amp; Sherman, M. (2012). Testing for spatial isotropy under",
            "lineNumber": 538
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 540

          {
            "text": "    Scaccia, L. &amp; Martin, R.J. (2005). Testing axial symmetry and",
            "lineNumber": 541

          },

          },

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 885
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",

          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },

          {
            "text": "def _ptable_range(D, P_diag, p_bg):",
            "lineNumber": 801,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 843
          },
          {
            "text": "    if valid.sum() &lt; 2:",
            "lineNumber": 844
          },
          {
            "text": "        return np.nan",
            "lineNumber": 845
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 846
          },
          {
            "text": "    D_v = D[valid]",
            "lineNumber": 847
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_v = P_diag[valid]",
            "lineNumber": 848
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 849
          },
          {
            "text": "    departure_0 = float(P_v[0]) - p_bg",
            "lineNumber": 850
          },
          {
            "text": "    if departure_0 &lt;= 0:",
            "lineNumber": 851
          },
          {
            "text": "        return np.nan",
            "lineNumber": 852
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 853
          },
          {
            "text": "    threshold = p_bg + np.exp(-1) * departure_0",
            "lineNumber": 854
          },
          {
            "text": "    below = np.where(P_v &lt;= threshold)[0]",
            "lineNumber": 855
          },
          {
            "text": "    if below.size == 0:",
            "lineNumber": 856
          },
          {
            "text": "        return np.nan",
            "lineNumber": 857
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 858
          },
          {
            "text": "    idx = below[0]",
            "lineNumber": 859
          },
          {
            "text": "    if idx == 0:",
            "lineNumber": 860
          },
          {
            "text": "        return float(D_v[0])",
            "lineNumber": 861
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 862
          },
          {
            "text": "    h0, h1 = float(D_v[idx - 1]), float(D_v[idx])",
            "lineNumber": 863
          },
          {
            "text": "    p0, p1 = float(P_v[idx - 1]), float(P_v[idx])",
            "lineNumber": 864
          },
          {
            "text": "    if p1 &gt;= p0:              # no decay → undefined",
            "lineNumber": 865
          },
          {
            "text": "        return np.nan",
            "lineNumber": 866
          },
          {
            "text": "    return h0 + (threshold - p0) / (p1 - p0) * (h1 - h0)",
            "lineNumber": 867,
            "isSignature": true
          },

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "isotropy_test_categorical       : Bootstrap isotropy test for categorical data.",

          },
          {
            "text": "\"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },

            "text": "import numpy",

          },

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def polar_ptable_map(coord, value, coord_limit, rLag, rLagTol,",
            "lineNumber": 870,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                     angLag=None, angTol=None,",
            "lineNumber": 871,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                     chunk_size=None, plot=True, figsize=None):",
            "lineNumber": 872,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 968
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 969
          },
          {
            "text": "    if plot:",
            "lineNumber": 970
          },
          {
            "text": "        n_cols  = nc",
            "lineNumber": 971
          },
          {
            "text": "        fs      = figsize or (4.5 * nc, 4.5)",
            "lineNumber": 972
          },
          {
            "text": "        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, n_cols, figsize=fs,",
            "lineNumber": 973
          },
          {
            "text": "                                 subplot_kw={'projection': 'polar'})",
            "lineNumber": 974
          },
          {
            "text": "        if nc == 1:",
            "lineNumber": 975
          },
          {
            "text": "            axes = [axes]",
            "lineNumber": 976
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 977
          },
          {
            "text": "        # Background = far-field independence level p_c^2.",
            "lineNumber": 978
          },
          {
            "text": "        # P[c,c,h] decays from E[p_i(c)^2] (at h=0) toward p_c^2 (at h→∞).",
            "lineNumber": 979
          },
          {
            "text": "        # Using p_c (marginal) would give a non-positive departure everywhere.",
            "lineNumber": 980
          },
          {
            "text": "        p_marginal = value.mean(axis=0)       # p_c = E[p_i(c)]",
            "lineNumber": 981
          },
          {
            "text": "        p_bg_sq    = p_marginal ** 2          # p_c^2  — far-field independence",
            "lineNumber": 982
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 983
          },
          {
            "text": "        for ci in range(nc):",
            "lineNumber": 984
          },
          {
            "text": "            ax = axes[ci]",
            "lineNumber": 985
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 986
          },
          {
            "text": "            # For each direction: mean departure from independence at lags rLag",
            "lineNumber": 987
          },
          {
            "text": "            c_dirs = np.zeros(na)",
            "lineNumber": 988
          },
          {
            "text": "            for k in range(na):",
            "lineNumber": 989
          },
          {
            "text": "                D_k = DD[k]",
            "lineNumber": 990
          },
          {
            "text": "                P_k = PP[k]",
            "lineNumber": 991
          },
          {
            "text": "                vals = []",
            "lineNumber": 992
          },
          {
            "text": "                for r, rt in zip(rLag, rLagTol):",
            "lineNumber": 993
          },
          {
            "text": "                    mask = ~np.isnan(D_k) &amp; (np.abs(D_k - r) &lt;= rt)",
            "lineNumber": 994
          },
          {
            "text": "                    if mask.any():",
            "lineNumber": 995
          },
          {
            "text": "                        # departure from p_c^2 (far-field independence level)",
            "lineNumber": 996
          },
          {
            "text": "                        dep = P_k[ci, ci, mask] - p_bg_sq[ci]",
            "lineNumber": 997
          },
          {
            "text": "                        vals.append(float(np.nanmean(dep)))",
            "lineNumber": 998
          },
          {
            "text": "                c_dirs[k] = float(np.nanmean(vals)) if vals else 0.0",
            "lineNumber": 999
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1000
          },
          {
            "text": "            c_dirs = np.clip(c_dirs, 0, None)",
            "lineNumber": 1001
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1002
          },
          {
            "text": "            # Full 360° symmetric rose.",
            "lineNumber": 1003
          },
          {
            "text": "            # Under second-order stationarity P[c,c;h,θ] = P[c,c;h,θ+π],",
            "lineNumber": 1004
          },
          {
            "text": "            # so the half-plane [-π/2, π/2) mirrors exactly onto [π/2, 3π/2).",
            "lineNumber": 1005
          },
          {
            "text": "            ang_full = np.concatenate([angLag, angLag + np.pi])",
            "lineNumber": 1006
          },
          {
            "text": "            c_full   = np.concatenate([c_dirs, c_dirs])",
            "lineNumber": 1007
          },
          {
            "text": "            # close the circle",
            "lineNumber": 1008
          },
          {
            "text": "            ang_full = np.append(ang_full, ang_full[0] + 2 * np.pi)",
            "lineNumber": 1009
          },
          {
            "text": "            c_full   = np.append(c_full,   c_full[0])",
            "lineNumber": 1010
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1011
          },
          {
            "text": "            # Densify to 720 angles so that ax.fill() draws smooth arcs",
            "lineNumber": 1012
          },
          {
            "text": "            # instead of straight Cartesian chords that cut across the plot",
            "lineNumber": 1013
          },
          {
            "text": "            # interior when a petal drops to near-zero next to a large petal.",
            "lineNumber": 1014
          },
          {
            "text": "            ang_dense = np.linspace(ang_full[0], ang_full[-1], 721)",
            "lineNumber": 1015
          },

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def isotropy_test(grid_s, grid_v, lagr, lagr_tol, angLag, angTol,",

          },
          {
            "text": "                  method='bootstrap', n_boot=499, alpha=0.05,",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 634
          },
          {
            "text": "    # ---- LRT -------------------------------------------------------------",

          },
          {
            "text": "    if method in ('lrt', 'all'):",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "                zh = np.nanmean(grid_v2d, axis=1) if grid_v2d.shape[1] &gt; 1 else grid_v2d.ravel()",
            "lineNumber": 647
          },
          {
            "text": "                zh = zh - np.nanmean(zh)",

            "lineNumber": 649
          },
          {
            "text": "                def _loglik(params, aniso_angle=None, aniso_ratio=None):",

          {

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./stamps/stamps/stats/dependence/anisotropy.py",

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def isotropy_test_categorical(coord, value, coord_limit, angLag, angTol,",
            "lineNumber": 1222,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                               class_weights=None,",
            "lineNumber": 1223,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                               n_boot=199, alpha=0.05, seed=None,",
            "lineNumber": 1224,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                               chunk_size=None):",
            "lineNumber": 1225,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Bootstrap isotropy test for **categorical** (probability-table) data.",
            "lineNumber": 1226
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1227
          },
          {
            "text": "    Tests whether the spatial dependence structure of a categorical variable",
            "lineNumber": 1228
          },
          {
            "text": "    is consistent with isotropy, using the effective ranges extracted from",
            "lineNumber": 1229
          },
          {
            "text": "    directional transition probability tables as the test statistic.",
            "lineNumber": 1230
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1231
          },
          {
            "text": "    The null hypothesis &#96;&#96;H₀&#96;&#96; is that the observed variation in effective",
            "lineNumber": 1232
          },
          {
            "text": "    range across directions is consistent with random spatial arrangement",
            "lineNumber": 1233
          },
          {
            "text": "    (isotropy).  The alternative is that the effective range is systematically",
            "lineNumber": 1234
          },
          {
            "text": "    larger in one direction (geometric anisotropy).",
            "lineNumber": 1235
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1236
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Test statistic**",
            "lineNumber": 1237
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1238
          },
          {
            "text": "    .. math::",
            "lineNumber": 1239
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1240
          },
          {
            "text": "        T_n = a_{\\\\text{principal}} - a_{\\\\text{secondary}}",
            "lineNumber": 1241
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1242
          },
          {
            "text": "    where the two directions are the estimated principal and secondary axes",
            "lineNumber": 1243
          },
          {
            "text": "    from :func:&#96;estimate_anisotropy_from_ptables&#96;.  A larger &#96;&#96;T_n&#96;&#96; means",
            "lineNumber": 1244
          },
          {
            "text": "    greater directional range contrast.",
            "lineNumber": 1245
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1246
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Null distribution**",
            "lineNumber": 1247
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1248
          },
          {
            "text": "    Generated by rotating all XY coordinates by &#96;&#96;n_boot&#96;&#96; uniformly drawn",
            "lineNumber": 1249
          },
          {
            "text": "    angles in &#96;&#96;[0, 2π)&#96;&#96; and recomputing &#96;&#96;T_n&#96;&#96; each time.  Under isotropy",
            "lineNumber": 1250
          },
          {
            "text": "    the rotation changes nothing about the dependence structure.",
            "lineNumber": 1251
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1252
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 1253
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 1254
          },
          {
            "text": "    coord : (n, 2) array",
            "lineNumber": 1255
          },
          {
            "text": "        2-D spatial coordinates (X, Y).",
            "lineNumber": 1256
          },
          {
            "text": "    value : (n, nc) array",
            "lineNumber": 1257
          },
          {
            "text": "        One-hot indicator matrix (or soft category probabilities).",
            "lineNumber": 1258
          },
          {
            "text": "    coord_limit : (ncl,) array",
            "lineNumber": 1259
          },
          {
            "text": "        Distance-class limits for the probability-table estimation.",
            "lineNumber": 1260
          },
          {
            "text": "    angLag : (na,) array",
            "lineNumber": 1261
          },
          {
            "text": "        Directions in radians to evaluate (e.g. 6 directions at 30° steps).",
            "lineNumber": 1262
          },
          {
            "text": "    angTol : (na,) array",
            "lineNumber": 1263
          },
          {
            "text": "        Angular tolerances (half-widths of acceptance windows).",
            "lineNumber": 1264
          },
          {
            "text": "    class_weights : (nc,) array or None",
            "lineNumber": 1265
          },
          {
            "text": "        Per-class weights for range averaging. &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96; → equal weights.",
            "lineNumber": 1266
          },
          {
            "text": "    n_boot : int",
            "lineNumber": 1267
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of bootstrap rotations.  Recommended ≥ 199.",
            "lineNumber": 1268
          },
          {
            "text": "    alpha : float",
            "lineNumber": 1269
          },
          {
            "text": "        Significance level for the reject/do-not-reject decision.",
            "lineNumber": 1270
          },
          {
            "text": "    seed : int or None",
            "lineNumber": 1271
          },
          {
            "text": "        Random seed for reproducibility.",
            "lineNumber": 1272
          },
          {
            "text": "    chunk_size : int or None",
            "lineNumber": 1273
          },
          {
            "text": "        Memory-control passed to :func:&#96;probatablecalc_directional&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1274
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1275
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 1276
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 1277
          },
          {
            "text": "    result : dict with keys",
            "lineNumber": 1278
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'theta_hat'&#96;&#96;      — float, estimated principal-axis angle (radians).",
            "lineNumber": 1279
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'r_hat'&#96;&#96;          — float, estimated anisotropy ratio.",
            "lineNumber": 1280
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'a_max_hat'&#96;&#96;      — float, estimated principal range.",
            "lineNumber": 1281
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'a_dirs'&#96;&#96;         — (na,) array, class-averaged directional ranges.",
            "lineNumber": 1282
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'a_dirs_per_class'&#96;&#96;— (nc, na) array, per-class directional ranges.",
            "lineNumber": 1283
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'test_stat'&#96;&#96;      — float, observed &#96;&#96;T_n&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1284
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'T_boot'&#96;&#96;         — (n_boot,) array, bootstrap &#96;&#96;T_n&#96;&#96; values.",
            "lineNumber": 1285
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'p_value'&#96;&#96;        — float, bootstrap p-value.",
            "lineNumber": 1286
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'reject_H0'&#96;&#96;      — bool, whether H₀ is rejected at level &#96;&#96;alpha&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1287
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'message'&#96;&#96;        — str, plain-English interpretation.",
            "lineNumber": 1288
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1289
          },
          {
            "text": "    References",
            "lineNumber": 1290
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 1291
          },
          {
            "text": "    Carle, S.F. &amp; Fogg, G.E. (1996). Transition probability-based indicator",
            "lineNumber": 1292
          },
          {
            "text": "        geostatistics. *Mathematical Geology*, 28(4), 453–476.",
            "lineNumber": 1293
          },
          {
            "text": "    Guan, Y., Sherman, M. &amp; Calvin, J.A. (2004). A nonparametric test for",
            "lineNumber": 1294
          },
          {
            "text": "        spatial isotropy using subsampling. *JASA*, 99(467), 810–821.",

          },
          {
            "text": "        [Rotation-bootstrap concept adapted here for categorical data.]",
            "lineNumber": 1296
          },

            "text": "    ",

          }
        ]

      "codeBlock": {
