```json
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def likeli_ME(mu, Pbiv_all, nbiv, nc, ndim, idx, reg):",
            "lineNumber": 1119,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1120
          },
          {
            "text": "    Objective function for the regularized *true* Maximum Entropy dual problem.",
            "lineNumber": 1121
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1122
          },
          {
            "text": "    L(mu) = log(Z) - mu * P_target + (1 / 2*reg) * ||mu||^2",
            "lineNumber": 1123
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1124
          },
          {
            "text": "    This is the function to be minimized. It is numerically stable due",
            "lineNumber": 1125
          },
          {
            "text": "    to the L2 regularization term.",
            "lineNumber": 1126
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1127
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 1128
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 1129
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1130
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of Lagrange multipliers, shape &#96;&#96;(nbiv * nc * nc,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1131
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pbiv_all : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1132
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of all target bivariate probabilities, flattened.",
            "lineNumber": 1133
          },
          {
            "text": "        Shape &#96;&#96;(nbiv * nc * nc,)&#96;&#96;. May contain NaNs.",
            "lineNumber": 1134
          },
          {
            "text": "    nbiv : int",
            "lineNumber": 1135
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of bivariate constraints.",
            "lineNumber": 1136
          },
          {
            "text": "    nc : int",
            "lineNumber": 1137
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of categories.",
            "lineNumber": 1138
          },
          {
            "text": "    ndim : int",
            "lineNumber": 1139
          },
          {
            "text": "        Total number of dimensions in the full PDF.",
            "lineNumber": 1140
          },
          {
            "text": "    idx : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 1141
          },
          {
            "text": "        Array mapping &#96;mu&#96; indices to dimension pairs, shape &#96;&#96;(nbiv, 2)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 1142
          },
          {
            "text": "    reg : float",
            "lineNumber": 1143
          },
          {
            "text": "        L2 regularization strength.",
            "lineNumber": 1144
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1145
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 1146
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 1147
          },
          {
            "text": "    obj : float",
            "lineNumber": 1148
          },
          {
            "text": "        The scalar value of the dual objective function.",
            "lineNumber": 1149
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1150
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_mat = mu.reshape(nbiv, nc, nc) # Reshape to (nbiv, nc, nc)",
            "lineNumber": 1151
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1152
          },
          {
            "text": "    # 1. Calculate P_logits (sum of mu's)",
            "lineNumber": 1153
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- START BROADCASTING FIX (This part is OK) ---",
            "lineNumber": 1154
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_dict = {tuple(idx[k]): mu_mat[k] for k in range(nbiv)}",
            "lineNumber": 1155
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_logits = np.zeros([nc] * ndim)",
            "lineNumber": 1156
          },
          {
            "text": "    for i in range(ndim):",
            "lineNumber": 1157
          },
          {
            "text": "        for j in range(i + 1, ndim):",
            "lineNumber": 1158
          },
          {
            "text": "            if (i, j) in mu_dict:",
            "lineNumber": 1159
          },
          {
            "text": "                mu_k = mu_dict[(i, j)]",
            "lineNumber": 1160
          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape = [1] * ndim",
            "lineNumber": 1161
          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape[i] = nc",
            "lineNumber": 1162
          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape[j] = nc",
            "lineNumber": 1163
          },
          {
            "text": "                mu_broadcast = mu_k.reshape(broadcast_shape)",
            "lineNumber": 1164
          },
          {
            "text": "                P_logits += mu_broadcast",
            "lineNumber": 1165
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- END BROADCASTING FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 1166
          },
          {
            "text": "        ",
            "lineNumber": 1167
          },
          {
            "text": "    # 2. Calculate log(Z)",
            "lineNumber": 1168
          },
          {
            "text": "    max_logit = np.max(P_logits)",
            "lineNumber": 1169
          },
          {
            "text": "    log_Z = max_logit + np.log(np.sum(np.exp(P_logits - max_logit)))",
            "lineNumber": 1170
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1171
          },
          {
            "text": "    # 3. Calculate mu * P_target",
            "lineNumber": 1172
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_dot_P = np.nansum(mu * Pbiv_all) # Pbiv_all is already flattened",
            "lineNumber": 1173
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1174
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- START CONVERGENCE FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 1175
          },
          {
            "text": "    # 4. Add L2 Regularization Penalty",
            "lineNumber": 1176
          },
          {
            "text": "    l2_penalty = np.sum(mu**2) / (2.0 * reg)",
            "lineNumber": 1177
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- END CONVERGENCE FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 1178
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1179
          },
          {
            "text": "    # 5. Objective L(mu)",
            "lineNumber": 1180
          },
          {
            "text": "    obj = log_Z - mu_dot_P + l2_penalty",
            "lineNumber": 1181
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.3322407007217407

            "text": "def MPLestimator(active_constraints, ndim, nc, tol):",

          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 964
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 965
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 966
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 967
          },

            "lineNumber": 968
          },
          {
            "text": "    It is fast but ignores higher-order interactions and can be unstable",
            "lineNumber": 969
          },

            "lineNumber": 970
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 971
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",

          },
          {

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 974
          },
          {
            "text": "        A list of tuples, &#96;&#96;[((i, j), Pbiv_table), ...]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 975
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;(i, j)&#96;&#96;: A tuple of the two dimension indices.",
            "lineNumber": 976
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;Pbiv_table&#96;&#96;: The &#96;&#96;(nc, nc)&#96;&#96; target probability table.",
            "lineNumber": 977
          },
          {
            "text": "    ndim : int",
            "lineNumber": 978
          },
          {
            "text": "        The total number of dimensions (e.g., estimation point + neighbors).",
            "lineNumber": 979
          },
          {
            "text": "    nc : int",
            "lineNumber": 980
          },
          {
            "text": "        The number of categories.",
            "lineNumber": 981
          },
          {
            "text": "    tol : float",
            "lineNumber": 982
          },
          {
            "text": "        The convergence tolerance for the L-BFGS-B optimizer.",
            "lineNumber": 983
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 984
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 985
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 986
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pfit : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 987
          },
          {
            "text": "        The fitted multivariate probability table, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, ..., nc)&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 988
          },
          {
            "text": "        with &#96;ndim&#96; dimensions.",
            "lineNumber": 989
          },
          {
            "text": "    niter : int",
            "lineNumber": 990
          },
          {
            "text": "        The number of function evaluations from the optimizer.",

          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 992
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 993
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- START LOGIC FIX --- (This part is OK)",
            "lineNumber": 994
          },
          {
            "text": "    nbiv = len(active_constraints) # O(n*k) or O(n^2)",
            "lineNumber": 995
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_0 = np.zeros(nbiv*nc*nc)",
            "lineNumber": 996
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pbiv_vec = np.zeros([nbiv,nc*nc])",
            "lineNumber": 997
          },
          {
            "text": "    idx = np.zeros([nbiv, 2], dtype=np.int16)",
            "lineNumber": 998
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 999
          },
          {
            "text": "    for k, (pair, Pbiv_table) in enumerate(active_constraints):",
            "lineNumber": 1000
          },
          {
            "text": "        i, j = pair",
            "lineNumber": 1001
          },
          {
            "text": "        if Pbiv_table is None or len(Pbiv_table) == 0:",
            "lineNumber": 1002
          },
          {
            "text": "            Pbiv_ravel = np.full((nc*nc), np.nan)",
            "lineNumber": 1003
          },
          {
            "text": "        else:",

          },
          {
            "text": "            Pbiv_ravel = Pbiv_table.ravel()",

          },

            "lineNumber": 1006
          },
          {

          {
            "text": "        if not np.all(np.isnan(Pbiv_ravel)):",

          },
          {

        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# --- START: NEW HYBRID BME/MCP FUNCTION ---",
            "lineNumber": 2546
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2547
          },
          {
            "text": "def HBMEcatPdf(ck,cs,ps,dmodel,Pmodel,nsmax,dmax,options = None):",
            "lineNumber": 2548,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2549
          },
          {
            "text": "    Performs Hybrid BME (HBME) categorical data prediction.",
            "lineNumber": 2550
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 2551
          },
          {
            "text": "    This function implements a two-step hybrid approach:",
            "lineNumber": 2552
          },
          {
            "text": "    1. **Regional prior (MCP step):** Run &#96;MCPcatPdf&#96; with up to &#96;nsmax_total&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2553
          },
          {
            "text": "       neighbours, restricted to &#96;dmax_mcp&#96;, to build a spatially varying",
            "lineNumber": 2554
          },
          {
            "text": "       prior that captures the regional trend.",
            "lineNumber": 2555
          },
          {
            "text": "    2. **Local update (BME step):** Run &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; with the &#96;nsmax&#96; *closest*",
            "lineNumber": 2556
          },
          {
            "text": "       neighbours and &#96;model_structure='full'&#96; to rigorously update the prior,",
            "lineNumber": 2557
          },
          {
            "text": "       correctly accounting for local spatial redundancy.",
            "lineNumber": 2558
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2559
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 2560
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 2561
          },
          {
            "text": "    ck : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2562
          },
          {
            "text": "        Estimation point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, d)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2563
          },
          {
            "text": "    cs : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2564
          },
          {
            "text": "        Data point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(n, d)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2565
          },
          {
            "text": "    ps : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2566
          },
          {
            "text": "        Soft data (PDFs) at data points, shape &#96;&#96;(n, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2567
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2568
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of distances for &#96;Pmodel&#96;, shape &#96;&#96;(nd,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2569
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2570
          },
          {
            "text": "        3D array of bivariate probability tables, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, nc, nd)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2571
          },
          {
            "text": "    nsmax : int",
            "lineNumber": 2572
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of *closest* neighbours for the final BME update step.",
            "lineNumber": 2573
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmax : float",
            "lineNumber": 2574
          },
          {
            "text": "        Maximum search distance for the BME update step (Step 2).",
            "lineNumber": 2575
          },
          {
            "text": "    options : dict, optional",
            "lineNumber": 2576
          },
          {
            "text": "        Dictionary of options:",
            "lineNumber": 2577
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2578
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'nsmax_total'&#96;&#96; (int): Maximum number of neighbours for the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2579
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior step (Step 1). Default &#96;&#96;20&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2580
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2581
          },
          {
            "text": "          .. warning::",
            "lineNumber": 2582
          },
          {
            "text": "             This must be kept **small** (typically 10–25).  At distances",
            "lineNumber": 2583
          },
          {
            "text": "             beyond the covariance correlation range the bivariate table",
            "lineNumber": 2584
          },
          {
            "text": "             factorises to the independence product P(c')·P(c), so each",
            "lineNumber": 2585
          },
          {
            "text": "             out-of-range neighbour contributes &#96;&#96;log P(c)&#96;&#96; to the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2586
          },
          {
            "text": "             log-posterior.  With n decorrelated neighbours the MCP result",
            "lineNumber": 2587
          },
          {
            "text": "             degenerates to the global marginal distribution **P(c), the",
            "lineNumber": 2588
          },
          {
            "text": "             same at every estimation point**, eliminating all spatial",
            "lineNumber": 2589
          },
          {
            "text": "             variation from the prior and making the final HBME map nearly",
            "lineNumber": 2590
          },
          {
            "text": "             flat.  A good starting value is &#96;&#96;nsmax_total ≈ 2–3 × nsmax&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2591
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2592
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (float): Maximum search radius for the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2593
          },
          {
            "text": "          step.  Defaults to &#96;&#96;dmax&#96;&#96;.  **Setting this to the covariance",
            "lineNumber": 2594
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlation range is strongly recommended** so that only spatially",
            "lineNumber": 2595
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlated neighbours contribute to the prior.  Ignored when",
            "lineNumber": 2596
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; is &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2597
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2598
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; is",
            "lineNumber": 2599
          },
          {
            "text": "          **determined automatically** from &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96; and &#96;&#96;Pmodel&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2600
          },
          {
            "text": "          using :func:&#96;_find_effective_range&#96; with the threshold given",
            "lineNumber": 2601
          },
          {
            "text": "          by &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96;.  This ensures the MCP ring radius",
            "lineNumber": 2602
          },
          {
            "text": "          equals the effective decorrelation distance in the bivariate",
            "lineNumber": 2603
          },
          {
            "text": "          model, preventing out-of-range data from contaminating the",
            "lineNumber": 2604
          },
          {
            "text": "          MCP prior.  Default &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2605
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2606
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96; (float): Decorrelation threshold",
            "lineNumber": 2607
          },
          {
            "text": "          for the automatic range detection.  The range is the distance",
            "lineNumber": 2608
          },
          {
            "text": "          at which the normalised total variation between &#96;&#96;Pmodel&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2609
          },
          {
            "text": "          the independence product &#96;&#96;p(c)*p(c')&#96;&#96; drops below this",
            "lineNumber": 2610
          },
          {
            "text": "          fraction.  Default &#96;&#96;0.05&#96;&#96; (5 %).",
            "lineNumber": 2611
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2612
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'use_annular_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96; (default), the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2613
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior is computed using only data in the **ring**",
            "lineNumber": 2614
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;dmax &lt; r &lt;= dmax_mcp&#96;&#96;, i.e. data that lie *outside* the local",
            "lineNumber": 2615
          },
          {
            "text": "          BME update zone.  This gives strict data independence between the",
            "lineNumber": 2616
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior step and the likelihood step (no data leakage).  If",
            "lineNumber": 2617
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96;, MCP uses all data within &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; (original",
            "lineNumber": 2618
          },
          {
            "text": "          behaviour, slightly faster but reuses data).",
            "lineNumber": 2619
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2620
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'global_marginal'&#96;&#96; (np.ndarray, shape &#96;&#96;(nc,)&#96;&#96;): Empirical",
            "lineNumber": 2621
          },
          {
            "text": "          category frequencies &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96;.  When provided, the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2622
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; is passed to BMEcatPdf together with &#96;&#96;global_marginal&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2623
          },
          {
            "text": "          so that the Bayes-factor correction &#96;&#96;q(c)/p(c)&#96;&#96; is applied",
            "lineNumber": 2624
          },
          {
            "text": "          automatically, preventing double-counting of the global",
            "lineNumber": 2625
          },
          {
            "text": "          marginal.  If not provided, &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; is estimated automatically",
            "lineNumber": 2626
          },
          {
            "text": "          from &#96;&#96;ps.mean(axis=0)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2627
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2628
          },
          {
            "text": "        - All other options (e.g., &#96;&#96;'tol'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'reg'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'estimator'&#96;&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 2629
          },
          {
            "text": "          are forwarded to the final &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; update step.",
            "lineNumber": 2630
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'model_structure'&#96;&#96; is *ignored* for the BME step and forced to",

          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'full'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2632
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2633
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 2634
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 2635
          },
          {
            "text": "    pk : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2636
          },
          {
            "text": "        The estimated posterior marginal PDFs, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2637
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2638
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 2639
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 2640
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Choosing nsmax_total and dmax_mcp:**",
            "lineNumber": 2641
          },
          {
            "text": "    Let r be the covariance correlation range.  Set &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp ≈ r&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2642
          },
          {
            "text": "    choose &#96;&#96;nsmax_total&#96;&#96; as the expected number of data points within that",
            "lineNumber": 2643
          },
          {
            "text": "    radius (typically 10–25 for datasets of 50–200 points).  Using too many",
            "lineNumber": 2644
          },
          {
            "text": "    decorrelated neighbours (beyond r) causes the MCP prior to converge to",
            "lineNumber": 2645
          },
          {
            "text": "    the global marginal P(c) at every location, destroying spatial variation.",
            "lineNumber": 2646
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2647
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Bayes-factor correction:**",
            "lineNumber": 2648
          },
          {
            "text": "    The Maximum Entropy table solved by &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; carries an implicit",
            "lineNumber": 2649
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; weight (the global marginal).  Passing the MCP result &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2650
          },
          {
            "text": "    directly as a prior therefore weights the final posterior by",
            "lineNumber": 2651
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;q(c) · p(c)&#96;&#96; rather than &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; alone — a subtle double-counting",
            "lineNumber": 2652
          },
          {
            "text": "    of the baseline frequency.  The Bayes-factor correction divides the",
            "lineNumber": 2653
          },
          {
            "text": "    supplied prior by &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; before entering &#96;&#96;producttablepdf&#96;&#96;, so the",
            "lineNumber": 2654
          },
          {
            "text": "    net effect is exactly &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;.  When no prior is given this correction",
            "lineNumber": 2655
          },
          {
            "text": "    is never triggered and the original BME behaviour is preserved.",
            "lineNumber": 2656
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2657
          },

          },

            "text": "def MCPcatPdf(ck, cs, ps, dmodel, Pmodel, nsmax, dmax, options=None):",

          {
            "lineNumber": 2487

          {
            "text": "        # --- 5c. Calculate the log of the likelihood product term ---",

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },
          {

          },

          },

            "text": "            else:",
```

```json
          },
          {
            "text": "                d_k = dsub[k]",

            "text": "            ",
            "lineNumber": 2509
          },
          {
            "text": "            # sum_term[j] = SUM_i [ P(X_k=i, X_0=j) * P_data(X_k=i) ]",

            "text": "            # This is the term from the original MCP paper for soft data",

          },
          {
            "text": "        # --- 6. Calculate the unnormalized posterior in log-space ---",

          },

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "        ",
            "lineNumber": 2526
          },
          {
            "text": "        # a. Subtract the max value for numerical stability",
            "lineNumber": 2527
          },
          {
            "text": "        max_log = np.max(log_numerator)",
            "lineNumber": 2528
          },
          {
            "text": "        log_numerator_shifted = log_numerator - max_log",

          },

            "text": "        ",
            "lineNumber": 2530
          },
          {
            "text": "        # b. Exponentiate",

          },
          {

          }

          },

          },

            "lineNumber": 2407
          },
          {

          },

            "text": "        # The MCP posterior is:",

          },

          {
            "text": "    # --- START BROADCASTING FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 1087
          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_mat = mu.reshape(nbiv, nc, nc) # mu is 1D, reshape to (nbiv, nc, nc)",

          },
          {
            "text": "    mu_dict = {tuple(idx[k]): mu_mat[k] for k in range(nbiv)}",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "            if (i, j) in mu_dict:",

          },

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "                # Create a (1, 1, ..., nc, ..., nc, ..., 1) shape",

          },
          {
            "text": "                broadcast_shape = [1] * ndim",

          {
            "text": "                ",

          },
          {

          },

            "text": "    # --- END BROADCASTING FIX ---",
            "lineNumber": 1109
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 1110
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Pfit is the normalized probability table",

          },
          {
            "text": "    # Use log-sum-exp trick to avoid overflow",

          },
          {

          {

          },
          {

          },
          {

          {
            "text": "# --- START: NEW HYBRID BME/MCP FUNCTION ---",
            "lineNumber": 2546
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2547
          },
          {
            "text": "def HBMEcatPdf(ck,cs,ps,dmodel,Pmodel,nsmax,dmax,options = None):",
            "lineNumber": 2548,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2549
          },
          {
            "text": "    Performs Hybrid BME (HBME) categorical data prediction.",
            "lineNumber": 2550
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 2551
          },
          {
            "text": "    This function implements a two-step hybrid approach:",
            "lineNumber": 2552
          },
          {
            "text": "    1. **Regional prior (MCP step):** Run &#96;MCPcatPdf&#96; with up to &#96;nsmax_total&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2553
          },
          {
            "text": "       neighbours, restricted to &#96;dmax_mcp&#96;, to build a spatially varying",
            "lineNumber": 2554
          },
          {
            "text": "       prior that captures the regional trend.",
            "lineNumber": 2555
          },
          {
            "text": "    2. **Local update (BME step):** Run &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; with the &#96;nsmax&#96; *closest*",
            "lineNumber": 2556
          },
          {
            "text": "       neighbours and &#96;model_structure='full'&#96; to rigorously update the prior,",
            "lineNumber": 2557
          },
          {
            "text": "       correctly accounting for local spatial redundancy.",
            "lineNumber": 2558
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2559
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 2560
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 2561
          },
          {
            "text": "    ck : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2562
          },
          {
            "text": "        Estimation point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, d)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2563
          },
          {
            "text": "    cs : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2564
          },
          {
            "text": "        Data point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(n, d)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2565
          },
          {
            "text": "    ps : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2566
          },
          {
            "text": "        Soft data (PDFs) at data points, shape &#96;&#96;(n, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2567
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2568
          },
          {
            "text": "        1D array of distances for &#96;Pmodel&#96;, shape &#96;&#96;(nd,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2569
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2570
          },
          {
            "text": "        3D array of bivariate probability tables, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, nc, nd)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2571
          },
          {
            "text": "    nsmax : int",
            "lineNumber": 2572
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of *closest* neighbours for the final BME update step.",
            "lineNumber": 2573
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmax : float",
            "lineNumber": 2574
          },
          {
            "text": "        Maximum search distance for the BME update step (Step 2).",
            "lineNumber": 2575
          },
          {
            "text": "    options : dict, optional",
            "lineNumber": 2576
          },
          {
            "text": "        Dictionary of options:",
            "lineNumber": 2577
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2578
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'nsmax_total'&#96;&#96; (int): Maximum number of neighbours for the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2579
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior step (Step 1). Default &#96;&#96;20&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2580
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2581
          },
          {
            "text": "          .. warning::",
            "lineNumber": 2582
          },
          {
            "text": "             This must be kept **small** (typically 10–25).  At distances",
            "lineNumber": 2583
          },
          {
            "text": "             beyond the covariance correlation range the bivariate table",
            "lineNumber": 2584
          },
          {
            "text": "             factorises to the independence product P(c')·P(c), so each",
            "lineNumber": 2585
          },
          {
            "text": "             out-of-range neighbour contributes &#96;&#96;log P(c)&#96;&#96; to the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2586
          },
          {
            "text": "             log-posterior.  With n decorrelated neighbours the MCP result",
            "lineNumber": 2587
          },
          {
            "text": "             degenerates to the global marginal distribution **P(c), the",
            "lineNumber": 2588
          },
          {
            "text": "             same at every estimation point**, eliminating all spatial",
            "lineNumber": 2589
          },
          {
            "text": "             variation from the prior and making the final HBME map nearly",
            "lineNumber": 2590
          },
          {
            "text": "             flat.  A good starting value is &#96;&#96;nsmax_total ≈ 2–3 × nsmax&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2591
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2592
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (float): Maximum search radius for the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2593
          },
          {
            "text": "          step.  Defaults to &#96;&#96;dmax&#96;&#96;.  **Setting this to the covariance",
            "lineNumber": 2594
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlation range is strongly recommended** so that only spatially",
            "lineNumber": 2595
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlated neighbours contribute to the prior.  Ignored when",
            "lineNumber": 2596
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; is &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2597
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2598
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; is",
            "lineNumber": 2599
          },
          {
            "text": "          **determined automatically** from &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96; and &#96;&#96;Pmodel&#96;&#96;",

          },
          {
            "text": "          using :func:&#96;_find_effective_range&#96; with the threshold given",

          },
          {
            "text": "          by &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96;.  This ensures the MCP ring radius",
            "lineNumber": 2602
          },
          {
            "text": "          equals the effective decorrelation distance in the bivariate",

          },
          {
            "text": "          model, preventing out-of-range data from contaminating the",

          },
          {
            "text": "          MCP prior.  Default &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2605
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2606
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96; (float): Decorrelation threshold",

          },
          {
            "text": "          for the automatic range detection.  The range is the distance",

          },
          {

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "          fraction.  Default &#96;&#96;0.05&#96;&#96; (5 %).",
            "lineNumber": 2611
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2612
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'use_annular_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96; (default), the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2613
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior is computed using only data in the **ring**",
            "lineNumber": 2614
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;dmax &lt; r &lt;= dmax_mcp&#96;&#96;, i.e. data that lie *outside* the local",
            "lineNumber": 2615
          },
          {
            "text": "          BME update zone.  This gives strict data independence between the",
            "lineNumber": 2616
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior step and the likelihood step (no data leakage).  If",
            "lineNumber": 2617
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96;, MCP uses all data within &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; (original",
            "lineNumber": 2618
          },
          {
            "text": "          behaviour, slightly faster but reuses data).",
            "lineNumber": 2619
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2620
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'global_marginal'&#96;&#96; (np.ndarray, shape &#96;&#96;(nc,)&#96;&#96;): Empirical",
            "lineNumber": 2621
          },
          {
            "text": "          category frequencies &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96;.  When provided, the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2622
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; is passed to BMEcatPdf together with &#96;&#96;global_marginal&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2623
          },
          {
            "text": "          so that the Bayes-factor correction &#96;&#96;q(c)/p(c)&#96;&#96; is applied",

          },
          {
            "text": "          automatically, preventing double-counting of the global",
            "lineNumber": 2625
          },
          {
            "text": "          marginal.  If not provided, &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; is estimated automatically",
            "lineNumber": 2626
          },
          {
            "text": "          from &#96;&#96;ps.mean(axis=0)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2627
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2628
          },
          {
            "text": "        - All other options (e.g., &#96;&#96;'tol'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'reg'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'estimator'&#96;&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 2629
          },
          {
            "text": "          are forwarded to the final &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; update step.",

          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'model_structure'&#96;&#96; is *ignored* for the BME step and forced to",

          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'full'&#96;&#96;.",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2633
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 2634
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 2635
          },
          {
            "text": "    pk : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2636
          },
          {
            "text": "        The estimated posterior marginal PDFs, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2637
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2638
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 2639
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 2640
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Choosing nsmax_total and dmax_mcp:**",
            "lineNumber": 2641
          },
          {
            "text": "    Let r be the covariance correlation range.  Set &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp ≈ r&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2642
          },
          {
            "text": "    choose &#96;&#96;nsmax_total&#96;&#96; as the expected number of data points within that",

          },
          {
            "text": "    radius (typically 10–25 for datasets of 50–200 points).  Using too many",
            "lineNumber": 2644
          },
          {
            "text": "    decorrelated neighbours (beyond r) causes the MCP prior to converge to",
            "lineNumber": 2645
          },
          {
            "text": "    the global marginal P(c) at every location, destroying spatial variation.",
            "lineNumber": 2646
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2647
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Bayes-factor correction:**",
            "lineNumber": 2648
          },
          {
            "text": "    The Maximum Entropy table solved by &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; carries an implicit",
            "lineNumber": 2649
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; weight (the global marginal).  Passing the MCP result &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2650
          },
          {
            "text": "    directly as a prior therefore weights the final posterior by",
            "lineNumber": 2651
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;q(c) · p(c)&#96;&#96; rather than &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; alone — a subtle double-counting",
            "lineNumber": 2652

            "text": "# --- END: New tune_regularization_loocv function ---",

            "text": "# Helper: auto-determine effective correlation range from Pmodel",

            "text": "# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------",

          },
          {
            "text": "def _p_marginal_from_pmodel(Pmodel):",
            "lineNumber": 2012,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Estimate the marginal category proportions from the far-field bivariate table.",
            "lineNumber": 2013
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2014
          },
          {
            "text": "    At the largest tabulated distance the joint table should be close to the",
            "lineNumber": 2015
          },
          {
            "text": "    independence product &#96;&#96;p(c) * p(c')&#96;&#96;.  Row-summing gives &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2016

          {
            "lineNumber": 2017
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",

            "text": "    Pmodel : (nc, nc, nd) ndarray",

          },

            "text": "        Bivariate probability tables along a single axis.",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2022
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 2023
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 2024
          },
          {
            "text": "    p : (nc,) ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2025
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2026
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_far = Pmodel[:, :, -1]",
            "lineNumber": 2027
          },
          {
            "text": "    p = P_far.sum(axis=1)",
            "lineNumber": 2028
          },
          {
            "text": "    p = np.clip(p, 1e-15, None)",
            "lineNumber": 2029
          },
          {
            "text": "    return p / p.sum()",
            "lineNumber": 2030,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2031
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2032
          },
          {
            "text": "def _auto_coord_cols(nd, K):",
            "lineNumber": 2033,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Default coordinate-column assignment for K separable components in nd dimensions.",
            "lineNumber": 2034
          },

            "lineNumber": 2035
          },
          {
            "text": "    Convention (mirrors the stamps space-time convention in &#96;&#96;coord2K&#96;&#96;):",
            "lineNumber": 2036
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2037
          },
          {
            "text": "    * K == 2, nd == 3 → &#96;&#96;[[0, 1], [2]]&#96;&#96;  (XY horizontal, Z vertical)",

          },
          {
            "text": "    * K == 2, nd == 2 → &#96;&#96;[[0], [1]]&#96;&#96;     (X, Y)",

          },

          {

            "lineNumber": 2260
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2261
          },

            "text": "    dmodel : (nd,) ndarray **or** list of (nd_k,) arrays",

          },
          {
            "text": "        Tabulated distances for the Pmodel.",

          },

          },

            "lineNumber": 2272

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "        * **1-D mode** — scalar float.  Ignored when &#96;&#96;auto_dmax=True&#96;&#96;.",

          },

          },
          {

          },

          },

          },

          {
            "text": "def MPLestimator(active_constraints, ndim, nc, tol):",
            "lineNumber": 963,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 964
          },
          {
            "text": "    Fits a MaxEnt PDF using non-regularized Maximum Pseudo-Likelihood (MPL).",
            "lineNumber": 965
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 966
          },
          {
            "text": "    This estimator is a composite likelihood method. It finds the parameters",
            "lineNumber": 967
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;mu&#96; for each bivariate marginal *independently* and then combines them.",
            "lineNumber": 968
          },
          {
            "text": "    It is fast but ignores higher-order interactions and can be unstable",
            "lineNumber": 969
          },
          {
            "text": "    if target probabilities are 0 or 1.",
            "lineNumber": 970
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 971
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 972
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 973
          },
          {
            "text": "    active_constraints : list",
            "lineNumber": 974
          },
          {
            "text": "        A list of tuples, &#96;&#96;[((i, j), Pbiv_table), ...]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 975
          },

          {
            "text": "def multiplysubtable(P,dim,index,ptheor,pest):",
            "lineNumber": 528,
            "isSignature": true

          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 529
          },
          {
            "text": "    (Legacy GIS function) Multiplies a subtable by a ratio of scalars.",
            "lineNumber": 530
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 531
          },
          {
            "text": "    This is a helper function for the &#96;iterativerescaling_GIS&#96; algorithm.",
            "lineNumber": 532
          },
          {
            "text": "    It multiplies elements in the full PDF &#96;P&#96; corresponding to a",

          },
          {
            "text": "    specific bivariate marginal by a correction ratio.",
            "lineNumber": 534
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 535
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 536
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 537
          },
          {
            "text": "    P : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 538
          },
          {
            "text": "        The full multidimensional PDF, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, ..., nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 539
          },
          {
            "text": "    dim : tuple or list",
            "lineNumber": 540
          },
          {
            "text": "        A 2-element list &#96;[dim1, dim2]&#96; specifying the axes of the marginal.",
            "lineNumber": 541
          },
          {
            "text": "    index : tuple or list",
            "lineNumber": 542
          },
          {
            "text": "        A 2-element list &#96;[idx1, idx2]&#96; specifying the indices within",
            "lineNumber": 543
          },
          {
            "text": "        the marginal (which category pair).",
            "lineNumber": 544
          },
          {
            "text": "    ptheor : float",
            "lineNumber": 545
          },
          {
            "text": "        The theoretical (target) probability for this category pair.",
            "lineNumber": 546
          },
          {
            "text": "    pest : float",
            "lineNumber": 547
          },
          {
            "text": "        The estimated (model) probability for this category pair.",
            "lineNumber": 548
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 549
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 550
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 551
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pfit : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 552
          },
          {
            "text": "        A *copy* of &#96;P&#96; with the relevant elements rescaled.",
            "lineNumber": 553
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 554
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 555
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Create a list of slices",
            "lineNumber": 556
          },
          {
            "text": "    slices = [slice(None)] * P.ndim  # Start with all slices",
            "lineNumber": 557
          },
          {
            "text": "    slices[dim[0]] = index[0]  # Set the first dimension index",

          },

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 560
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Convert to a tuple",

          },
          {
            "text": "    slices = tuple(slices)",
            "lineNumber": 562
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pfit = P.copy()",
            "lineNumber": 563
          },
          {
            "text": "    if ptheor == 0:",

          },
          {
            "text": "        Pfit[slices] = 0",

          },
          {
            "text": "    else:",

          },
          {
            "text": "        Pfit[slices] *= ptheor / pest",
            "lineNumber": 567
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 568
          },
          {
            "text": "    return Pfit",
            "lineNumber": 569,
            "isSignature": true

          {
            "lineNumber": 570
          },

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py",
        "range": {

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def _find_effective_range(dmodel, Pmodel, threshold=0.05):",
            "lineNumber": 2149,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2150
          },
          {
            "text": "    Estimate the effective correlation range from bivariate probability tables.",
            "lineNumber": 2151
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2152
          },
          {
            "text": "    The function measures the total variation (TV) between the bivariate table",
            "lineNumber": 2153
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;Pmodel[:, :, k]&#96;&#96; and the corresponding **independence product**",
            "lineNumber": 2154
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;p(c) * p(c')&#96;&#96; at each tabulated distance &#96;&#96;dmodel[k]&#96;&#96;.  It then",
            "lineNumber": 2155
          },
          {
            "text": "    returns the interpolated distance at which the normalised TV drops to",
            "lineNumber": 2156
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;threshold&#96;&#96; × its value at the smallest distance.",
            "lineNumber": 2157
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2158
          },
          {
            "text": "    Mathematically:",
            "lineNumber": 2159
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2160
          },
          {
            "text": "    .. math::",
            "lineNumber": 2161
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2162
          },
          {
            "text": "        TV(d) = \\\\frac{1}{2}\\\\sum_{c,c'} \\\\left| P(c,c';d) - p(c)p(c') \\\\right|",
            "lineNumber": 2163
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2164
          },
          {
            "text": "        d^* = \\\\inf\\\\{ d : TV(d)/TV(d_0) \\\\le \\\\text{threshold} \\\\}",
            "lineNumber": 2165
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2166
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 2167
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 2168
          },
          {
            "text": "    dmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2169
          },
          {
            "text": "        1-D array of tabulated distances, shape &#96;&#96;(nd,)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2170
          },
          {
            "text": "    Pmodel : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2171
          },
          {
            "text": "        3-D array of bivariate probability tables, shape &#96;&#96;(nc, nc, nd)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2172
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;Pmodel[:, :, k]&#96;&#96; is the joint table at distance &#96;&#96;dmodel[k]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2173
          },
          {
            "text": "    threshold : float, optional",
            "lineNumber": 2174
          },
          {
            "text": "        Fraction of the zero-distance TV below which the data are considered",
            "lineNumber": 2175
          },
          {
            "text": "        decorrelated.  Default &#96;&#96;0.05&#96;&#96; (5 %).",
            "lineNumber": 2176
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2177
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 2178
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 2179
          },
          {
            "text": "    d_range : float",
            "lineNumber": 2180
          },
          {
            "text": "        Estimated effective correlation range (in the same units as",
            "lineNumber": 2181
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96;).  If the TV never drops below &#96;&#96;threshold&#96;&#96; within the",
            "lineNumber": 2182
          },
          {
            "text": "        range of &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96;, the largest tabulated distance is returned as a",
            "lineNumber": 2183
          },
          {
            "text": "        conservative upper bound.",
            "lineNumber": 2184
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2185
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 2186
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 2187
          },
          {
            "text": "    The marginal &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; is estimated from the table at the **largest**",
            "lineNumber": 2188
          },
          {
            "text": "    tabulated distance (where the table is closest to independence).  If the",
            "lineNumber": 2189
          },
          {
            "text": "    largest-distance table is still far from independence the returned range",
            "lineNumber": 2190
          },
          {
            "text": "    will be a lower bound rather than the true range.",
            "lineNumber": 2191
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2192
          },
          {
            "text": "    nd = len(dmodel)",
            "lineNumber": 2193
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2194
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Estimate marginal p(c) from the table at the largest distance",
            "lineNumber": 2195
          },
          {
            "text": "    P_far = Pmodel[:, :, -1]",
            "lineNumber": 2196
          },
          {
            "text": "    p_marginal = P_far.sum(axis=1)          # sum over c' for each c",
            "lineNumber": 2197
          },
          {
            "text": "    p_marginal = np.clip(p_marginal, 1e-15, None)",
            "lineNumber": 2198
          },
          {
            "text": "    p_marginal /= p_marginal.sum()",
            "lineNumber": 2199
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2200
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Independence product  P_indep[c, c'] = p(c) * p(c')",
            "lineNumber": 2201
          }
        ]
      },

            "text": "def likeli_diff_ME(mu, Pbiv_all, nbiv, nc, ndim, idx, reg):",

          },

          },

          },

          },
          {
```

---

## Why BMEcatPdf Degrades Sand and Fine Sand Precision

### 1. The Core Mathematical Difference: Joint vs. Conditional

The key contrast between BME and MCP is **where the multivariate joint distribution is evaluated**.

**MCP formula** (lines 2480–2518):
```
log P_MCP(c₀) = log prior_to_use(c₀) − n·log p_dc(c₀) + Σₖ log [Σ_b P_biv(b, c₀|hₖ) · pₖ(b)]
```
Each neighbor contributes an **independent** log-likelihood term. The double-counting correction `−n·log p_dc(c₀)` then adjusts for how common class `c₀` is in the training data.

**BME formula** (lines 1848, 1868, 1873):
```python
Pkh_ = maxentropytable(...)         # ME joint table: P(c₀, c₁, ..., cₙ)
Pkh  = producttablepdf(Pkh_, ...)   # multiply in prior + soft data
pk[i,:] = Pkh.sum(axis=...)         # marginalize over c₁,...,cₙ
```
The ME joint table is built by fitting a log-linear Gibbs model:
\[
\log P_{ME}(c_0, c_1, \ldots, c_n) = \underbrace{\sum_{k} \mu_{0k}[c_0, c_k]}_{\text{c₀-neighbor pairs}} + \underbrace{\sum_{i < j,\; i,j \geq 1} \mu_{ij}[c_i, c_j]}_{\text{neighbor–neighbor pairs}}
\]
The crucial **second group** — the neighbor-neighbor coupling terms — is **absent in MCP** entirely.

---

### 2. Hard Data Case: BME ≈ MCP

When all neighbors are hard data (one-hot), `producttablepdf` zeroes out every configuration where `cₖ ≠ gravel`. The neighbor-neighbor terms become constants `μᵢⱼ[G, G]`, which cancel in normalization. So for hard data the results are essentially equivalent.

---

### 3. Soft Data Case: Where BME Diverges

In practice your data enters as soft PDFs (e.g., XGBoostLSS posteriors or uncertain borehole intervals), meaning `pₖ = [0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.70]` rather than a one-hot indicator. The marginalization in BME is:

\[
P_{post}(c_0) \propto \frac{q_{eff}(c_0)}{p_{global}(c_0)} \sum_{c_1,\ldots,c_n} P_{ME}(c_0, c_1,\ldots,c_n) \prod_k p_k(c_k)
\]

Now the neighbor-neighbor coupling terms **do not cancel**, because we're summing a product of soft weights over all configurations. The dominant term in that sum is the all-Gravel configuration `(G, G, ..., G)`:

\[
\exp\!\bigg[\sum_k \mu_{0k}[c_0, G] + \sum_{i<j} \mu_{ij}[G, G]\bigg] \cdot (0.70)^n
\]

The magnitude of `μᵢⱼ[G, G]` is large because Gravel-Gravel co-occurrence at short distances is high (Gravel is ~47% of the data). With `n = 8` neighbors there are \(\binom{8}{2} = 28\) such inter-neighbor coupling terms — **each one reinforcing Gravel independently of the estimation point**. This creates a super-linear amplification of the dominant class proportional to `n²` (number of neighbor pairs), whereas MCP grows only linearly with `n`.

---

### 4. Why These Two Classes Specifically?

The class distribution is approximately:
| Class | Proportion |
|-------|-----------|
| Clay (1) | ~14% |
| Fine Sand (2) | ~19% |
| Sand (3) | ~19% |
| Gravel (4) | ~47% |

**Sand and Fine Sand sit in the "intermediate transition zone":**

- They have **non-trivial cross-bivariate probability with Gravel** (`P_biv(G, S|h)` and `P_biv(G, FS|h)` are nonzero), because grain-size sequence in alluvial fans is Gravel → Sand → Fine Sand → Clay. This means neither Sand nor Fine Sand can "escape" the Gravel pressure through near-zero cross terms.
- Their **absolute self-bivariate probabilities are modest**: `P_biv(S,S|h=0) = p(S) ≈ 0.19` and `P_biv(FS,FS|h=0) ≈ 0.19`, compared to `P_biv(G,G|h=0) = p(G) ≈ 0.47`. The Lagrange multipliers `μ[S,S]` and `μ[FS,FS]` are therefore much smaller than `μ[G,G]` in the ME table.
- In the ME joint table, any configuration that contains Sand or Fine Sand has far less probability mass than the all-Gravel configuration. When `producttablepdf` multiplies in the soft data, there's insufficient self-correlation to resist the Gravel amplification.

**Clay (14%) is actually better protected**, despite being the rarest class:

Clay in the Pingtung basin occurs in coherent **stratigraphic layers** at depth. The **vertical component of the separable Pmodel** has a high Clay-Clay self-transition probability at small vertical distances. When the estimation point is at a Clay depth zone with Clay observations nearby in the vertical direction, the ME table's vertical bivariate constraint `P_biv(C, C|Δz)` provides a strong anchor for Clay. BME can leverage this precisely because it handles the joint distribution — the vertically adjacent Clay observations reinforce each other through the ME table, partially offsetting the Gravel pressure from horizontally separated neighbors.

Sand and Fine Sand do not benefit from this stratigraphic layering protection: they occur transitionally throughout the profile rather than in thick coherent layers.

---

### 5. MCP's Built-In Protection

The MCP correction term `−n·log p_dc(c₀)` (where `p_dc = p_global`) acts like a **class-frequency equalizer**. For decorrelated neighbors at large distances, `P_biv(G, c₀|h→∞) = p(G)·p(c₀)`, so the n-neighbor log-likelihood grows as `n·log[p(G)·p(c₀)]`. The correction `−n·log p(c₀)` removes the `p(c₀)^n` factor, leaving `p(G)^n` — **identical for all classes**. Decorrelated data thus contributes zero net discrimination.

BME achieves the same in the `(c₀, cₖ)` direction via the BF correction `prior_to_use = q_eff / p_global`. But it has **no analogous correction for the neighbor-neighbor terms** `μᵢⱼ[cᵢ, cⱼ]`, which is where the extra Gravel amplification slips in through soft data.

---

### Summary

| Factor | Effect on Sand/Fine Sand |
|--------|--------------------------|
| n² neighbor-pair coupling terms in ME table | Gravel amplified super-linearly; Sand/FS pushed out |
| Moderate self-bivariate probability | Lagrange multipliers `μ[S,S]`, `μ[FS,FS]` too small to resist |
| Non-trivial cross-terms with Gravel | Cannot "escape" via near-zero cross-bivariate |
| No stratigraphic layering | No strong vertical self-correlation to anchor the posterior |
| Clay has coherent vertical layers | Vertical ME constraint partially counteracts horizontal Gravel pressure |

The root cause is that **BME's strength — capturing neighbor-neighbor spatial correlations — becomes a liability in an imbalanced, Gravel-dominated neighborhood with soft data**. The correlated Gravel signals among neighbors reinforce each other through the joint ME table in a way that MCP's independence assumption prevents, at the cost of the most "squeezed" intermediate classes: Sand and Fine Sand.

```
print(f'BMEcatPdf + local:      {result_bme_local.shape}  ({t_bme_local:.1f} s)')

result_bme_xgb = BMEcatPdf(

=== CELL [21] id=diag_bme_vs_mcp ===
# ── Diagnostic: 3 Z=-15 locations where MCPcatPdf and BMEcatPdf disagree ──────
from stamps.bme.BMEcatPdf import (
    _coerce_ps_soft, _resolve_pmodel,
    _find_effective_range, neighbours_separable,
)
from stamps.stats.dependence.probatablefit import probamodel2bitable_separable

# --- Reconstruct the separable config used inside BMEcatPdf/MCPcatPdf ----------
cs_f = np.asarray(cs_bme, dtype=float)
sep_diag, _, _, _ = _resolve_pmodel(
    [dmodel_h, dmodel], [Pmodel_h, Pmodel], None, cs_f, bme_opts_3d)

_thresh = bme_opts_3d.get('auto_dmax_threshold', 0.05)
for _co in sep_diag['components']:
    _co['dmax'] = _find_effective_range(_co['dmodel'], _co['Pmodel'], threshold=_thresh)

ps_soft = _coerce_ps_soft(ps_bme, nc, bme_opts_3d)
_p_marg = np.asarray(sep_diag.get('p_marginal'), dtype=float)
_p_marg = _p_marg / _p_marg.sum()

print('Separable dmax applied inside neighbours_separable:')
for _co in sep_diag['components']:
    print(f"  cols={_co['coord_cols']}  dmax={_co['dmax']:.1f}")

# --- Find Z=-15 locations where MCP MAP != BME-local MAP ----------------------
z_diag   = -15.0
mask_z15 = np.abs(ck_bme[:, 2] - z_diag) &lt; 1.0
idx_z15  = np.where(mask_z15)[0]

disagree = idx_z15[map_mcp[idx_z15] != map_bme_loc[idx_z15]]
print(f'\nGrid nodes at Z={z_diag:.0f} m : {len(idx_z15)}')
print(f'Nodes where MCP != BME-local  : {len(disagree)}')

if len(disagree) == 0:
    print('No disagreeing nodes found at Z=-15 m.')
else:
    n_pick = min(3, len(disagree))
    chosen = disagree[np.round(np.linspace(0, len(disagree)-1, n_pick)).astype(int)]

    lbl_map  = dict(zip(LITHO_CODES, LITHO_LABELS))
    _dms = [_co['dmodel'] for _co in sep_diag['components']]
    _Pms = [_co['Pmodel'] for _co in sep_diag['components']]
    _P_indep = np.outer(_p_marg, _p_marg)

    for loc_idx in chosen:
        ck0 = ck_bme[[loc_idx], :]
        x0, y0, z0 = ck0[0, 0], ck0[0, 1], ck0[0, 2]

        csub, Zsub, dsub, nsub, sltidx, d_comp, p_local = neighbours_separable(
            ck0, cs_f, ps_soft, nsmax_3d,
            sep_diag['components'],
            options=bme_opts_3d,
            p_marginal=_p_marg,
            mode=sep_diag.get('mode', 'product'),
        )

        mcp_cls   = lbl_map[int(map_mcp[loc_idx])]
        bme_l_cls = lbl_map[int(map_bme_loc[loc_idx])]
        bme_x_cls = lbl_map[int(map_bme_xgb[loc_idx])]

        print(f'\n{"="*72}')
        print(f'Location idx={loc_idx}  X={x0:.0f}  Y={y0:.0f}  Z={z0:.1f} m')
        print(f'  MCP+local  : {mcp_cls}')
        print(f'  BME+local  : {bme_l_cls}')
        print(f'  BME+compos.: {bme_x_cls}')
        print(f'  Neighbours : {nsub}')

        if p_local is not None:
            _ps = '  '.join(f'{l}={v:.3f}' for l, v in zip(LITHO_LABELS, p_local))
            print(f'  p_local    : [{_ps}]')
        else:
            print('  p_local    : None (no candidates in kernel range)')

        if nsub == 0:
            print('  (no neighbours found)')
            print('=' * 72)
            continue

        # TV score per selected neighbour
        rows = []
        for k in range(nsub):
            _dvec = d_comp[k, :]
            _P3d  = probamodel2bitable_separable(
                _dvec, _dms, _Pms, _p_marg,
                mode=sep_diag.get('mode', 'product'))
            _tv  = 0.5 * np.abs(_P3d - _P_indep).sum()
            _cls = lbl_map.get(LITHO_CODES[int(np.argmax(Zsub[k]))], '?')
            rows.append((_cls, _dvec[0], _dvec[1], csub[k, 2], _tv))

        print(f'\n  {"#":&gt;2}  {"Class":&lt;10}  {"d_horiz(km)":&gt;11}  '
              f'{"d_vert(m)":&gt;9}  {"TV":&gt;6}  Z_data(m)')
        print(f'  {"-"*60}')
        for k, (_cls, dh, dv, zk, tv) in enumerate(rows):
            print(f'  {k:2d}  {_cls:&lt;10}  {dh/1e3:&gt;11.3f}  '
                  f'{abs(dv):&gt;9.1f}  {tv:&gt;6.3f}  {zk:.1f}')
        print('=' * 72)

# Summary table
```

```
## 7. Estimation — MCP, BME, and HBME

Five estimators using the separable 3-D Pmodel:

1. **MCPcatPdf + local** ($n=20$) — fast conditional-independence approximation with kernel-smoothed nonstationary baseline $p_\text{local}(c)$.
2. **BMEcatPdf + local** ($n=8$) — full ME with $p_\text{local}$ as the prior; sparse-data limit $\to p_\text{local}$.
3. **BMEcatPdf + composite** ($n=8$) — full ME with composite prior $q_\text{eff}(c) \propto p_\text{local}(c) \times q_\text{XGB}(c) / p_\text{global}(c)$.
4. **HBMEcatPdf + local** (inner $n=8$, outer $n=20$) — two-step hybrid: MCP regional prior (outer ring, $n=20$) then BME local update (inner $n=8$) with $p_\text{local}$.
5. **HBMEcatPdf + composite** (inner $n=8$, outer $n=20$) — same HBME structure but with XGBoostLSS composite prior injected.

The Bayes-factor denominator is **always** $p_\text{global}$ (the structural Pmodel marginal).
```

## Summary of changes

### `stamps/stamps/bme/BMEcatPdf.py` — Fix `HBMEcatPdf` for separable list inputs

`HBMEcatPdf` previously assumed `dmodel` and `Pmodel` were scalar NumPy arrays, which broke when called with separable list inputs (the format used by the notebook). Four targeted fixes were made:

1. **`ncat` detection** — calls `_resolve_pmodel` at the start to detect separable mode and extract the number of categories from the first component's `Pmodel.shape[0]`, instead of `Pmodel.shape[0]` directly.
2. **`auto_dmax_mcp` computation** — for separable inputs, runs `_find_effective_range` on each component and takes the max as the scalar ring radius, instead of failing on a list.
3. **`ncat` at main loop** — now uses the variable `_ncat_hbme` instead of `Pmodel.shape[0]`.
4. **Ring mask boundary** — when `use_annular_mcp=True` and `dmax=None` (separable), computes a scalar inner radius from the component effective ranges.

### `pingtung_lithology_workflow.ipynb` — 6 cells updated

| Cell | Change |
|------|--------|
| **[1] imports** | Added `HBMEcatPdf` to the import |
| **[15] Pmodel setup** | Added `nsmax_mcp=20`, `nsmax_hbme=20`, and `hbme_opts_3d` dict with `nsmax_total=20, use_annular_mcp=False` |
| **[19] markdown** | Updated to describe all 5 estimators |
| **[20] estimation** | MCP now uses `nsmax_mcp=20`; added `HBMEcatPdf + local` and `HBMEcatPdf + composite` runs |
| **[22] maps** | `plot_estimation_maps` now shows all 5 method maps |
| **[27] LOOCV** | Added HBME + local and HBME + composite LOOCV runs with `HBMEcatPdf` |
| **[28] results** | 5-method summary table, bar chart, 2×3 confusion matrix grid, classification report for best method |

**Design note on `use_annular_mcp=False`**: With only ~52 sparse boreholes, the annular ring (data *beyond* the horizontal effective range of ~14.5 km) would frequently be empty, causing HBME to fall back to the global marginal as its prior. Setting `use_annular_mcp=False` uses all data within `dmax_mcp` for the outer MCP prior step — a small data-leakage trade-off that is standard and mentioned in the `HBMEcatPdf` docstring.

```
for k, uid in enumerate(unique_keys):
    mask = station_ids == uid
    station_xy[k] = wells.loc[mask, ['X', 'Y']].values[0]
    for ci, c in enumerate(LITHO_CODES):
        station_ind[k, ci] = np.mean(wells.loc[mask, 'LithoCode'] == c)

_, suggested_dmax_h, _ = pair_distance_diagnostic(

d_max_h = suggested_dmax_h
n_bins_h = 12
print(f'Suggested horizontal d_max: {d_max_h/1e3:.1f} km')

# --- Horizontal Pmodel: per-Z-level pairs (Option B) -------------------------
# Pass all individual depth samples to probatablecalc with group_ids set to
# each row's Z value.  Only pairs sharing the same Z-level contribute to the
# empirical tables, so the Pmodel reflects within-layer horizontal transitions
# rather than the depth-averaged geology.

    xy_all, ind_all, coord_limit_h, group_ids=z_group_ids)

print(f'\nHorizontal Pmodel (per-Z pairs):')

print(f'  Total pairs    : {int(O_emp_h[1:].sum())}')

ang_step = np.pi / 6
angLag = np.arange(-np.pi/2, np.pi/2, ang_step)

## 5. Separable 3-D Pmodel (product mode)

The vertical and horizontal Pmodels are composed via a Markov-chain product:
$P_{3D}(a,b \mid \Delta h, \Delta z) = P_H \, D^{-1} \, P_V$
where $D = \mathrm{diag}(p)$.  Passing &#96;dmodel&#96; and &#96;Pmodel&#96; as **lists** to
&#96;MCPcatPdf&#96; / &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; activates separable mode automatically.
```

## Plan: Adding Anisotropic Estimation as an Instructional Comparison

### The Core Idea

Geometric anisotropy is handled by a **coordinate transformation**:
1. Rotate the horizontal XY plane so the principal correlation axis aligns with the X-axis (by `theta_hat` degrees)
2. Scale the secondary axis by `1/r_hat` — "stretching" the short direction to match the principal range

After transformation, the spatial structure is **isotropic in the new space**, so the same isotropic Pmodel machinery applies. Since `r_hat = 1.0` here, the results will be nearly identical to the isotropic case — and that itself is the instructional point: showing *why* the anisotropic model collapses to the isotropic one when the data supports isotropy.

`aniso2iso` already exists in your codebase at `stamps/stamps/stats/dependence/anisotropy.py` (line 192), taking `(c, angle_in_degrees, ratio)`.

---

### Where to Insert New Cells

The notebook currently has 30 cells (indices 0–29). The changes should be inserted as **four new cells** after cell 12 (anisotropy analysis):

#### **New Cell A** — after cell 12: Transform coordinates + refit anisotropic Pmodel

```python
from stamps.stats.dependence.anisotropy import aniso2iso

# Convert principal-axis angle from radians to degrees (aniso2iso expects degrees)
angle_deg = float(np.degrees(theta_hat))

# Transform all horizontal XY coordinates to the isotropic space.
# When r_hat=1.0 (isotropic data), this is a pure rotation – distances are
# invariant, so the anisotropic and isotropic Pmodels will be identical.
xy_all_iso     = aniso2iso(xy_all,                   angle_deg, r_hat)
station_xy_iso = aniso2iso(station_xy,               angle_deg, r_hat)
cs_xy_iso      = aniso2iso(wells[['X','Y']].values,  angle_deg, r_hat)
ck_xy_iso      = aniso2iso(grid_df[['X','Y']].values, angle_deg, r_hat)

# Build 3D anisotropic coordinates: (X_iso, Y_iso, Z)
cs_aniso = np.column_stack([cs_xy_iso,  wells['Z'].values])
ck_aniso = np.column_stack([ck_xy_iso,  grid_df['Z'].values])

# Refit the horizontal Pmodel in the isotropic (transformed) coordinate space
coord_limit_h_iso = adaptive_bins(station_xy_iso, n_bins=n_bins_h,
                                  d_max=d_max_h, method='equal_pairs')
D_emp_h_iso, P_emp_h_iso, O_emp_h_iso = probatablecalc(
    xy_all_iso, ind_all, coord_limit_h_iso, group_ids=z_group_ids)

dmodel_h_iso, Pmodel_h_iso, _ = build_pmodel(
    D_emp_h_iso, P_emp_h_iso, O_emp_h_iso,
    n_fit=80, n_bins=n_bins_h, d_max_emp=d_max_h,
    kstd=0.5 * d_max_h / n_bins_h, regularize=True, verbose=False)

print(f'Anisotropic transform: angle={angle_deg:.1f} deg, r_hat={r_hat:.3f}')
print(f'  (r_hat=1.0 → pure rotation; Pmodel range unchanged)')
print(f'Anisotropic Pmodel (isotropic space): '
      f'{dmodel_h_iso[0]/1e3:.2f} – {dmodel_h_iso[-1]/1e3:.2f} km')
```

#### **New Cell B** — after Cell A: Run anisotropic estimation

```python
# Anisotropic estimation uses cs_aniso / ck_aniso (transformed coordinates)
# and the Pmodel fitted in the isotropic (rotated/scaled) space.
# The estimation grid is still plotted in original XY space (ck_bme).

t0 = time.perf_counter()
result_mcp_aniso = MCPcatPdf(
    ck_aniso, cs_aniso, ps_bme,
    [dmodel_h_iso, dmodel], [Pmodel_h_iso, Pmodel],
    nsmax_mcp, None, options=bme_opts_3d)
t_mcp_a = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'MCPcatPdf anisotropic:  {result_mcp_aniso.shape}  ({t_mcp_a:.1f} s)')

t0 = time.perf_counter()
result_bme_local_aniso = BMEcatPdf(
    ck_aniso, cs_aniso, ps_bme,
    [dmodel_h_iso, dmodel], [Pmodel_h_iso, Pmodel],
    nsmax_3d, None, options=bme_opts_3d)
t_bme_a = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'BMEcatPdf aniso+local:  {result_bme_local_aniso.shape}  ({t_bme_a:.1f} s)')

map_mcp_aniso     = _codes[np.argmax(result_mcp_aniso,      axis=1)]
map_bme_loc_aniso = _codes[np.argmax(result_bme_local_aniso, axis=1)]
```

#### **New Cell C** — after Cell B: Isotropic vs anisotropic comparison maps

```python
# Compare isotropic vs anisotropic MAPs.
# Both are plotted using the ORIGINAL ck_bme coordinates for spatial reference.
# With r_hat ≈ 1.0 the maps should look nearly identical — confirming that
# the anisotropic correction is unnecessary for this dataset.
fig, axes = plot_estimation_maps(
    ck_bme,       # ← always original coords for plotting
    map_arrays=[map_mcp,        map_mcp_aniso,
                map_bme_loc,    map_bme_loc_aniso],
    method_names=['MCP + local (isotropic)',   'MCP + local (anisotropic)',
                  'BME + local (isotropic)',   'BME + local (anisotropic)'],
    categories=LITHO_CODES, labels=LITHO_LABELS, colors=LITHO_COLORS,
)
plt.suptitle(
```

```python
# LOOCV with anisotropic coordinates lets us quantify whether the coordinate

print(f'MCP anisotropic:  acc={cv_mcp_aniso["accuracy"]:.3f}  '

    BMEcatPdf, cs_aniso, ps_bme, _dml_iso, _Pml_iso,

# Tabulate iso vs aniso side-by-side

    'Accuracy':      [cv_mcp["accuracy"],  cv_mcp_aniso["accuracy"],
                      cv_bme["accuracy"],  cv_bme_aniso["accuracy"]],
    'Balanced acc.': [cv_mcp["balanced_accuracy"],  cv_mcp_aniso["balanced_accuracy"],
                      cv_bme["balanced_accuracy"],  cv_bme_aniso["balanced_accuracy"]],
    'Mean log-lik':  [cv_mcp["mean_log_likelihood"], cv_mcp_aniso["mean_log_likelihood"],
                      cv_bme["mean_log_likelihood"], cv_bme_aniso["mean_log_likelihood"]],
}, index=['MCP iso', 'MCP aniso', 'BME iso', 'BME aniso'])
print(iso_aniso_table.round(4))
```
