        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def probatablecalc(coord, value, coord_limit, group_ids=None,",
            "lineNumber": 488,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                   normalize_inputs=True,",
            "lineNumber": 489,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                   chunk_size=None, ShowCalDis=False):",
            "lineNumber": 490,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Estimate bivariate probability tables for categorical spatial data.",
            "lineNumber": 491
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 492
          },
          {
            "text": "    Computes empirical transition-probability tables &#96;&#96;P[a, b, h]&#96;&#96; for all",
            "lineNumber": 493
          },
          {
            "text": "    category pairs &#96;&#96;(a, b)&#96;&#96; at the distance classes defined by",
            "lineNumber": 494
          },
          {
            "text": "    *coord_limit*.",
            "lineNumber": 495
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 496
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Soft / probabilistic indicators are fully supported.**  You may pass",
            "lineNumber": 497
          },
          {
            "text": "    either hard (one-hot) or soft (fractional) class-probability vectors.",
            "lineNumber": 498
          },
          {
            "text": "    See *value* and *normalize_inputs* for details.",
            "lineNumber": 499
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 500
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 501
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 502
          },
          {
            "text": "    coord : (n, d) ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 503
          },
          {
            "text": "        Coordinates for the *n* data locations (any number of dimensions).",
            "lineNumber": 504
          },
          {
            "text": "    value : (n, nc) array-like",
            "lineNumber": 505
          },
          {
            "text": "        Class-indicator matrix at each location.  Two forms are accepted:",
            "lineNumber": 506
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 507
          },
          {
            "text": "        **Hard (one-hot) indicators** — standard categorical data where",
            "lineNumber": 508
          },
          {
            "text": "        each location belongs to exactly one class::",
            "lineNumber": 509
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 510
          },
          {
            "text": "            # 4-class example, location belongs to class 2:",
            "lineNumber": 511
          },
          {
            "text": "            [0, 1, 0, 0]",
            "lineNumber": 512
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 513
          },
          {
            "text": "        **Soft (probabilistic) indicators** — each row is a probability",
            "lineNumber": 514
          },
          {
            "text": "        vector representing uncertainty over class assignments::",
            "lineNumber": 515
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 516
          },
          {
            "text": "            # geophysical inversion / classifier output:",
            "lineNumber": 517
          },
          {
            "text": "            [0.2, 0.2, 0.8]   # most likely class 3, but uncertain",
            "lineNumber": 518
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 519
          },
          {
            "text": "        Soft indicators arise naturally from:",
            "lineNumber": 520
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 521
          },
          {
            "text": "        * Geophysical inversion results (e.g. ERT, seismic facies)",
            "lineNumber": 522
          },
          {
            "text": "        * Probabilistic classifier outputs (XGBoostLSS, random forest)",
            "lineNumber": 523
          },
          {
            "text": "        * Station-averaged lithology fractions (as in this example)",
            "lineNumber": 524
          },
          {
            "text": "        * Kriging or co-kriging of indicator variables",
            "lineNumber": 525
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 526
          },
          {
            "text": "        The table estimator computes the outer product",
            "lineNumber": 527
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;P(a, b | h) ∝ p_i[a] × p_j[b]&#96;&#96; for each pair &#96;&#96;(i, j)&#96;&#96; at lag",
            "lineNumber": 528
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;h&#96;&#96;, then averages over all such pairs in the bin.  This is",
            "lineNumber": 529
          },
          {
            "text": "        equivalent to treating soft probabilities as fractional class",
            "lineNumber": 530
          },
          {
            "text": "        memberships and pooling contributions across all classes",
            "lineNumber": 531
          },
          {
            "text": "        simultaneously — no NaN gaps from absent class combinations.",
            "lineNumber": 532
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 533
          },
          {
            "text": "        Rows are validated and row-normalized to sum to 1 (controlled by",
            "lineNumber": 534
          },
          {
            "text": "        *normalize_inputs*).",
            "lineNumber": 535
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 536
          },
          {
            "text": "    coord_limit : (ncl,) ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 537
          },
          {
            "text": "        Bin-edge limits for the distance classes (output of",
            "lineNumber": 538
          },
          {
            "text": "        :func:&#96;adaptive_bins&#96;).  Distance classes are **open on the left",
            "lineNumber": 539
          },
          {
            "text": "        and closed on the right**.  The first element must be 0 (sentinel",
            "lineNumber": 540
          },
          {
            "text": "        for self-pairs).",
            "lineNumber": 541
          },
          {
            "text": "    group_ids : (n,) array-like of int/str or None, optional",
            "lineNumber": 542
          },
          {
            "text": "        Group labels (e.g. borehole IDs).  When provided, **only pairs",
            "lineNumber": 543
          },
          {
            "text": "        within the same group** contribute to the empirical tables.  This",
            "lineNumber": 544
          },
          {
            "text": "        is essential for estimating vertical correlation from borehole",
            "lineNumber": 545
          },
          {
            "text": "        data, where cross-borehole pairs at the same depth separation do",
            "lineNumber": 546
          },
          {
            "text": "        not carry within-column transition information.",
            "lineNumber": 547
          },
          {
            "text": "    normalize_inputs : bool, optional",
            "lineNumber": 548
          },
          {
            "text": "        If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96; (default), call :func:&#96;normalize_indicators&#96; to",
            "lineNumber": 549
          },
          {
            "text": "        validate and row-normalize *value* before computing the tables.",
            "lineNumber": 550
          },
          {
            "text": "        This handles un-normalized soft indicators (e.g. raw scores that",
            "lineNumber": 551
          },
          {
            "text": "        sum to values other than 1) and emits informative warnings.",
            "lineNumber": 552
          },
          {
            "text": "        Set to &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96; only when you have already validated *value*",
            "lineNumber": 553
          },
          {
            "text": "        externally and want to skip the overhead.",
            "lineNumber": 554
          },
          {
            "text": "    chunk_size : int or None, optional",
            "lineNumber": 555
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of points per chunk for memory management.  The result is",
            "lineNumber": 556
          },
          {
            "text": "        independent of *chunk_size* (default: process all at once).",
            "lineNumber": 557
          },
          {
            "text": "    ShowCalDis : bool, optional",
            "lineNumber": 558
          },
          {
            "text": "        Print progress information (default False).",
            "lineNumber": 559
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 560
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 561
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 562
          },
          {
            "text": "    D : (ncl,) ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 563
          },
          {
            "text": "        Mean pair distance per bin.  &#96;&#96;D[0] = 0&#96;&#96; for the self-pair bin.",
            "lineNumber": 564
          },
          {
            "text": "        NaN for empty bins.",
            "lineNumber": 565
          },
          {
            "text": "    P : (nc, nc, ncl) ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 566
          },
          {
            "text": "        Bivariate probability table.  &#96;&#96;P[a, b, k]&#96;&#96; is the estimated",
            "lineNumber": 567
          },
          {
            "text": "        probability that class &#96;&#96;b&#96;&#96; occurs at distance &#96;&#96;D[k]&#96;&#96; from a",
            "lineNumber": 568
          },
          {
            "text": "        class-&#96;&#96;a&#96;&#96; location.  With soft indicators every bin is fully",
            "lineNumber": 569
          },
          {
            "text": "        populated (no NaN) as long as the bin is non-empty.",
            "lineNumber": 570
          },
          {
            "text": "    O : (ncl,) ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 571
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of unique undirected pairs per bin.",
            "lineNumber": 572
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 573
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 574
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 575
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Why soft indicators eliminate NaN gaps:**",
            "lineNumber": 576
          },
          {
            "text": "    With hard one-hot vectors, &#96;&#96;P[a, b, k]&#96;&#96; is NaN whenever no pair",
            "lineNumber": 577
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;(class a, class b)&#96;&#96; exists in bin &#96;&#96;k&#96;&#96;.  At short horizontal",
            "lineNumber": 578
          },
          {
            "text": "    ranges where only a handful of borehole pairs contribute, rare class",
            "lineNumber": 579
          },
          {
            "text": "    combinations are easily absent.  Soft indicators avoid this because",
            "lineNumber": 580
          },
          {
            "text": "    every pair contributes a non-zero weight &#96;&#96;p_i[a] × p_j[b]&#96;&#96; to",
            "lineNumber": 581
          },
          {
            "text": "    *all* &#96;&#96;(a, b)&#96;&#96; cells simultaneously.",
            "lineNumber": 582
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 583
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Joint-probability interpretation:**",
            "lineNumber": 584
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;P[a, b, h]&#96;&#96; is the *bivariate* (joint) probability of observing",
            "lineNumber": 585
          },
          {
            "text": "    class &#96;&#96;a&#96;&#96; at one location and class &#96;&#96;b&#96;&#96; at a location distance",
            "lineNumber": 586
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;h&#96;&#96; away, averaged over all such pairs::",
            "lineNumber": 587
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 588
          },
          {
            "text": "        P[a, b, h] = E[p_i(a) × p_j(b)]  / ΣΣ_ab E[p_i(a) × p_j(b)]",
            "lineNumber": 589
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 590
          },
          {
            "text": "    For one-hot data this reduces to the classical transition-probability",
            "lineNumber": 591
          },
          {
            "text": "    matrix (Carle &amp; Fogg 1996).",
            "lineNumber": 592
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 593
          },
          {
            "text": "    See Also",
            "lineNumber": 594
          },
          {
            "text": "    --------",
            "lineNumber": 595
          },
          {
            "text": "    normalize_indicators : Validate and row-normalize an indicator matrix.",
            "lineNumber": 596
          },
          {
            "text": "    adaptive_bins : Generate bin edges for this function.",
            "lineNumber": 597
          },
          {
            "text": "    pair_distance_diagnostic : Diagnose the pair-distance distribution.",
            "lineNumber": 598
          },
          {
            "text": "    probatablecalc_directional : Directional (anisotropy) variant.",
            "lineNumber": 599
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 600
          },
          {
            "text": "    if chunk_size is None:",
            "lineNumber": 601
          },
          {
            "text": "        chunk_size = len(coord)",
            "lineNumber": 602
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.3308630883693695

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./stamps/stamps/stats/dependence/probatablecalc_spatial.py",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {

          },

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def identify_homogeneous_regions(",
            "lineNumber": 426,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    center_coords,",
            "lineNumber": 427,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    P,",
            "lineNumber": 428,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    n_regions=None,",
            "lineNumber": 429,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    distance_threshold=None,",
            "lineNumber": 430,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    linkage_method='ward',",
            "lineNumber": 431,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    metric='kl_divergence',",
            "lineNumber": 432,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    min_samples_per_region=10,",
            "lineNumber": 433,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    ShowCalDis=False",
            "lineNumber": 434,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "):",
            "lineNumber": 435,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 436
          },
          {
            "text": "    Identify relatively homogeneous regions based on similarity of probability tables.",
            "lineNumber": 437
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 438
          },
          {
            "text": "    This function clusters center locations into regions where the probability tables",
            "lineNumber": 439
          },
          {
            "text": "    are relatively similar (homogeneous). It uses hierarchical clustering based on",
            "lineNumber": 440
          },
          {
            "text": "    a distance metric between probability tables.",
            "lineNumber": 441
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 442
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Clustering Method:**",
            "lineNumber": 443
          },
          {
            "text": "    The function uses scipy's hierarchical clustering algorithm:",
            "lineNumber": 444
          },
          {
            "text": "    1. Calculates a pairwise distance matrix between probability tables using the",
            "lineNumber": 445
          },
          {
            "text": "       specified metric (KL divergence, Euclidean, or Hellinger distance).",
            "lineNumber": 446
          },
          {
            "text": "    2. Performs hierarchical clustering using scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage with",
            "lineNumber": 447
          },
          {
            "text": "       the specified linkage method ('ward', 'complete', 'average', or 'single').",
            "lineNumber": 448
          },
          {
            "text": "       Note: 'ward' linkage requires Euclidean distances, so it automatically switches",
            "lineNumber": 449
          },
          {
            "text": "       to 'average' linkage when using KL divergence metric.",
            "lineNumber": 450
          },
          {
            "text": "    3. Forms flat clusters using scipy.cluster.hierarchy.fcluster based on either",
            "lineNumber": 451
          },
          {
            "text": "       the number of regions (n_regions) or a distance threshold (distance_threshold).",
            "lineNumber": 452
          },
          {
            "text": "    4. Merges regions with fewer than min_samples_per_region samples into the nearest",
            "lineNumber": 453
          },
          {
            "text": "       larger region based on spatial distance between centroids.",
            "lineNumber": 454
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 455
          },
          {
            "text": "    Args:",
            "lineNumber": 456
          },
          {
            "text": "        center_coords (ndarray): 2-D ndarray of floats with shape (n_centers, d).",
            "lineNumber": 457
          },
          {
            "text": "            Coordinates of center locations.",
            "lineNumber": 458
          },
          {
            "text": "        P (ndarray): 4-D ndarray of floats with shape (nc, nc, ncl, n_centers).",
            "lineNumber": 459
          },
          {
            "text": "            Spatial-varying probability tables from probatablecalc_spatial.",
            "lineNumber": 460
          },
          {

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "import numpy as np",
            "lineNumber": 1
          },
          {
            "text": "from scipy.spatial.distance import cdist, pdist",

          },
          {
            "text": "import warnings",

          },

            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "text": "# Import optimized version if available",
            "lineNumber": 5
          },
          {
            "text": "try:",
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "text": "    from .probatablecalc_optimized import probatablecalc_optimized",
            "lineNumber": 7
          },
          {
            "text": "except ImportError:",
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "    probatablecalc_optimized = None",

          },

            "lineNumber": 11
          },

            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "# ======================================================================",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "# Soft-indicator validation and normalization",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "# ======================================================================",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "def normalize_indicators(value, tol=1e-6, uniform_on_zero=True):",
            "lineNumber": 17,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Validate and row-normalize a soft-indicator (or one-hot) matrix.",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "    Ensures every row of *value* is non-negative and sums to 1 — the",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "    probability-simplex constraint required by :func:&#96;probatablecalc&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "text": "    Call this before :func:&#96;probatablecalc&#96; whenever your indicator data",
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "    may not be pre-normalized, for example:",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "    * Geophysical inversion outputs  &#96;&#96;[p_clay, p_sand, p_gravel]&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "    * XGBoostLSS / classifier probability vectors",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "    * Station-averaged lithology fractions (soft indicators)",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "    * Raw score vectors that need normalizing before use",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "    value : (n, nc) array-like",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "        Raw indicator matrix.  Accepts:",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "        - **Hard / one-hot** — rows are &#96;&#96;0/1&#96;&#96; vectors with one &#96;&#96;1&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": "          Example: class 2 of 4 → &#96;&#96;[0, 1, 0, 0]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "        - **Soft / probabilistic** — non-negative rows approximately",
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "text": "          summing to 1.  Example: &#96;&#96;[0.2, 0.5, 0.3]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "text": "        - **Raw (un-normalized) scores** — any non-negative matrix whose",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "text": "          rows do not yet sum to 1.  Example: &#96;&#96;[0.2, 0.2, 0.8]&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "text": "          (sum = 1.2).  Rows are automatically rescaled.",
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "    tol : float, optional",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "text": "        Rows whose sum deviates from 1.0 by more than *tol* trigger a",
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "        :class:&#96;UserWarning&#96; before normalization (default 1e-6).",
            "lineNumber": 46

          },

            "text": "        ",
            "lineNumber": 516
          },
          {
            "text": "        # Calculate pairwise KL divergence",
            "lineNumber": 517
          },
          {
            "text": "        def kl_divergence(p, q):",

          },
          {

          },

          {
            "text": "def outlier_detection(",
            "lineNumber": 99,

          },

            "text": "        'max_count': 100",

            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    },",
            "lineNumber": 112,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    inverse_distance_weighted_parameters=None):",
            "lineNumber": 113,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Detect space-time outliers in a multi-station sensor DataFrame.",
            "lineNumber": 114
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 115
          },
          {
            "text": "    For each value column, the function first z-scores each observation",
            "lineNumber": 116
          },
          {
            "text": "    relative to its source station (location), then groups records into",
            "lineNumber": 117
          },
          {
            "text": "    time slices of width *time_group_frequency*.  For every slice it looks",
            "lineNumber": 118
          },
          {
            "text": "    **backward** through an expanding time window (up to *bandwith_end* hours)",
            "lineNumber": 119
          },
          {
            "text": "    to collect at least *max_count* previously-accepted (non-outlier) data",
            "lineNumber": 120
          },
          {
            "text": "    points.  A space-time IDW estimate of the expected z-score is computed at",
            "lineNumber": 121
          },
          {
            "text": "    each station in the slice; any record deviating more than 3 standard",
            "lineNumber": 122
          },
          {
            "text": "    deviations from that IDW prediction is flagged as an outlier.  The",
            "lineNumber": 123
          },
          {
            "text": "    causal (past-only) look-back makes the detector suitable for real-time or",
            "lineNumber": 124
          },
          {
            "text": "    streaming use cases.",
            "lineNumber": 125
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 126
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 127
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 128
          },
          {
            "text": "    data_frame : pandas.DataFrame",
            "lineNumber": 129
          },
          {
            "text": "        Input observations.  Must contain at least the columns named by",
            "lineNumber": 130
          },
          {
            "text": "        *id_column*, *spatial_column*, *temporal_column*, and *value_column*.",
            "lineNumber": 131
          },
          {
            "text": "        Rows with NaN in any *value_column* are silently dropped before",
            "lineNumber": 132
          },
          {
            "text": "        processing.",
            "lineNumber": 133
          },
          {
            "text": "    id_column : str",
            "lineNumber": 134
          },
          {
            "text": "        Name of the column that uniquely identifies each monitoring station",
            "lineNumber": 135
          },
          {
            "text": "        or sensor (e.g. &#96;&#96;'station_id'&#96;&#96;).  Used to build the per-station",
            "lineNumber": 136
          },
          {
            "text": "        z-score statistics when *normalized=True*.",
            "lineNumber": 137
          },
          {
            "text": "    spatial_column : list of str",
            "lineNumber": 138
          },
          {
            "text": "        Names of the columns carrying spatial coordinates, e.g.",
            "lineNumber": 139
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;['longitude', 'latitude']&#96;&#96;.  Must be numeric and in consistent",
            "lineNumber": 140
          },
          {
            "text": "        units (metres or degrees) that match *s_range* inside the IDW call.",
            "lineNumber": 141
          },
          {
            "text": "    temporal_column : str",
            "lineNumber": 142
          },
          {
            "text": "        Name of the datetime column (must be &#96;&#96;datetime64&#96;&#96; dtype).  Used",
            "lineNumber": 143
          },
          {
            "text": "        both for time-grouping and for converting time to seconds for the",
            "lineNumber": 144
          },
          {
            "text": "        space-time distance metric inside &#96;&#96;idw_st&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 145
          },
          {
            "text": "    value_column : list of str",
            "lineNumber": 146
          },
          {
            "text": "        Names of the numeric columns to check for outliers.  Each column is",
            "lineNumber": 147
          },
          {
            "text": "        processed independently; one outlier flag column is added per entry.",
            "lineNumber": 148
          },
          {
            "text": "    normalized : bool, default &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 149
          },
          {
            "text": "        If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, observations are z-scored **per station** before the IDW",
            "lineNumber": 150
          },
          {
            "text": "        comparison, removing location-specific mean and variance so that",
            "lineNumber": 151
          },
          {
            "text": "        stations with systematically high or low baselines do not produce",
            "lineNumber": 152
          },
          {
            "text": "        spurious flags.  Set to &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96; only when all stations share a",
            "lineNumber": 153
          },
          {
            "text": "        common expected value (e.g. after a prior calibration step).",
            "lineNumber": 154
          },
          {
            "text": "    time_group_frequency : str or pandas offset alias",
            "lineNumber": 155
          },
          {
            "text": "        Width of each temporal processing slice, e.g. &#96;&#96;'1h'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'30min'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 156
          },
          {
            "text": "        Smaller values give finer temporal resolution at the cost of more",
            "lineNumber": 157
          },
          {
            "text": "        loop iterations.  Choose the smallest meaningful reporting period of",
            "lineNumber": 158
          },
          {
            "text": "        the sensor network.",
            "lineNumber": 159
          },
          {
            "text": "    search_parameters : dict",
            "lineNumber": 160
          },
          {
            "text": "        Controls the adaptive time-window search used to collect past data:",
            "lineNumber": 161
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 162
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'bandwith_start'&#96;&#96; : float",
            "lineNumber": 163
          },
          {
            "text": "            Initial look-back window, **in hours** (note: parameter name has",
            "lineNumber": 164
          },
          {
            "text": "            a known typo — \"bandwith\" instead of \"bandwidth\").  Default 1.5.",
            "lineNumber": 165
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'bandwith_step'&#96;&#96; : float",
            "lineNumber": 166
          },
          {
            "text": "            Increment added each iteration when too few points are found.",
            "lineNumber": 167
          },
          {
            "text": "            Default 0.1.",
            "lineNumber": 168
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'bandwith_end'&#96;&#96; : float",
            "lineNumber": 169
          },
          {
            "text": "            Maximum look-back window in hours before giving up.  Default 2.",
            "lineNumber": 170
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'max_count'&#96;&#96; : int",
            "lineNumber": 171
          },
          {
            "text": "            Minimum number of past non-outlier data points required before",
            "lineNumber": 172
          },
          {
            "text": "            running the IDW estimate.  Default 100.",
            "lineNumber": 173
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 174
          },
          {
            "text": "        Example::",
            "lineNumber": 175
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 176
          },
          {
            "text": "            search_parameters = {",
            "lineNumber": 177
          },
          {
            "text": "                'bandwith_start': 1.0,",
            "lineNumber": 178
          },
          {
            "text": "                'bandwith_step': 0.5,",
            "lineNumber": 179
          },
          {
            "text": "                'bandwith_end': 6.0,",
            "lineNumber": 180
          },
          {
            "text": "                'max_count': 50,",
            "lineNumber": 181
          },
          {
            "text": "            }",
            "lineNumber": 182
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 183
          },
          {
            "text": "    inverse_distance_weighted_parameters : dict or None",
            "lineNumber": 184
          },
          {
            "text": "        Reserved for future use.  The current implementation passes",
            "lineNumber": 185
          },
          {
            "text": "        hard-coded spatial/temporal ranges (10 km / 2 h) and IDW power = 2",
            "lineNumber": 186
          },
          {
            "text": "        directly to &#96;&#96;idw_st&#96;&#96;; this argument is accepted but **not yet",
            "lineNumber": 187
          },
          {
            "text": "        forwarded** to the inner IDW call.  Pass &#96;&#96;None&#96;&#96; (default).",
            "lineNumber": 188
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 189
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 190
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 191
          },
          {
            "text": "    data_frame : pandas.DataFrame",
            "lineNumber": 192
          },
          {
            "text": "        The input DataFrame enriched with the following columns for each",
            "lineNumber": 193
          },
          {
            "text": "        entry *vc* in *value_column*:",
            "lineNumber": 194
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 195
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'{vc}_zs'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 196
          },
          {
            "text": "            Per-station z-score of the raw observation.",
            "lineNumber": 197
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'{vc}_zs_idw'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 198
          },
          {
            "text": "            IDW-predicted z-score from causal (past-only) neighbours.",
            "lineNumber": 199
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;'outlier_{vc}_idw'&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 200
          },
          {
            "text": "            Boolean flag — &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96; if",
            "lineNumber": 201
          },
          {
            "text": "            &#96;&#96;|{vc}_zs − {vc}_zs_idw| &gt; 3&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 202
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 203
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Algorithm overview**",
            "lineNumber": 206
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 207
          },
          {
            "text": "    For each time slice *t* and each value column *vc*:",
            "lineNumber": 208
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 209
          },
          {
            "text": "    1. Collect all previously-accepted observations in the look-back window",
            "lineNumber": 210
          },
          {
            "text": "       &#96;&#96;[t − bandwith_start,  t)&#96;&#96;.  If fewer than *max_count* points are",
            "lineNumber": 211
          },
          {
            "text": "       found, expand the window by *bandwith_step* hours and repeat until",
            "lineNumber": 212
          },
          {
            "text": "       *bandwith_end* is reached.",
            "lineNumber": 213
          },
          {
            "text": "    2. Call &#96;&#96;idw_st&#96;&#96; with a fixed space-time metric",
            "lineNumber": 214
          },
          {
            "text": "       (&#96;&#96;s_range=10 000 m&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;t_range=2 h&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;st_ratio=10 000/3 600&#96;&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 215
          },
          {
            "text": "    3. Flag any record in slice *t* as an outlier if::",
            "lineNumber": 216
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 217
          },
          {
            "text": "           |z_actual − z_idw| &gt; 3",
            "lineNumber": 218
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 219
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Known limitations**",
            "lineNumber": 220
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 221
          },
          {
            "text": "    * The outlier threshold is hard-coded to **3 σ** and cannot currently be",
            "lineNumber": 222
          },
          {
            "text": "      changed via the function signature.",
            "lineNumber": 223
          },
          {
            "text": "    * The IDW space-time ranges (10 km spatial, 2 h temporal) are",
            "lineNumber": 224
          },
          {
            "text": "      hard-coded in the loop body; *inverse_distance_weighted_parameters* is",
            "lineNumber": 225
          },
          {
            "text": "      silently ignored.",
            "lineNumber": 226
          },
          {
            "text": "    * The function is marked &#96;&#96;# need fix this function #&#96;&#96; in the source —",
            "lineNumber": 227
          },
          {
            "text": "      use :func:&#96;space_time_outlier_detection&#96; for a more complete",
            "lineNumber": 228
          },
          {
            "text": "      space-time pipeline that applies both spatial and temporal screening.",
            "lineNumber": 229
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 230
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Causal detection**",
            "lineNumber": 231
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 232
          },
          {
            "text": "    Only observations strictly **before** the current time slice are used as",
            "lineNumber": 233
          },
          {
            "text": "    the IDW reference set.  This prevents data leakage into the future and",
            "lineNumber": 234
          },
          {
            "text": "    makes the detector applicable to operational, near-real-time monitoring.",
            "lineNumber": 235
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 236
          },
          {
            "text": "    Examples",
            "lineNumber": 237
          },
          {
            "text": "    --------",
            "lineNumber": 238
          },
          {
            "text": "    Detect outliers in a multi-station meteorological dataset:",
            "lineNumber": 239
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 240
          },
          {
            "text": "    &gt;&gt;&gt; import pandas as pd",
            "lineNumber": 241
          },
          {
            "text": "    &gt;&gt;&gt; import numpy as np",
            "lineNumber": 242
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 243
          },
          {
            "text": "    &gt;&gt;&gt;",
            "lineNumber": 244
          },
          {
            "text": "    &gt;&gt;&gt; df = pd.read_csv('weather_stations.csv', parse_dates=['timestamp'])",
            "lineNumber": 245

            "text": "    &gt;&gt;&gt; result = outlier_detection(",

            "text": "    ...     temporal_column='timestamp',",

            "text": "def HBMEcatPdf(ck,cs,ps,dmodel,Pmodel,nsmax,dmax,options = None):",

            "text": "    \"\"\"",

            "text": "    Performs Hybrid BME (HBME) categorical data prediction.",

            "text": "    ",

          },

            "text": "    This function implements a two-step hybrid approach:",

            "lineNumber": 2678
          },
          {
            "text": "    2. **Local update (BME step):** Run &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; with the &#96;nsmax&#96; *closest*",

          {
            "text": "       neighbours and &#96;model_structure='full'&#96; to rigorously update the prior,",

          {
            "text": "        Data point coordinates, shape &#96;&#96;(n, d)&#96;&#96;.",

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "             beyond the covariance correlation range the bivariate table",
            "lineNumber": 2707
          },
          {
            "text": "             factorises to the independence product P(c')·P(c), so each",
            "lineNumber": 2708
          },
          {
            "text": "             out-of-range neighbour contributes &#96;&#96;log P(c)&#96;&#96; to the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2709
          },
          {
            "text": "             log-posterior.  With n decorrelated neighbours the MCP result",
            "lineNumber": 2710
          },
          {
            "text": "             degenerates to the global marginal distribution **P(c), the",
            "lineNumber": 2711
          },
          {
            "text": "             same at every estimation point**, eliminating all spatial",
            "lineNumber": 2712
          },
          {
            "text": "             variation from the prior and making the final HBME map nearly",
            "lineNumber": 2713
          },
          {
            "text": "             flat.  A good starting value is &#96;&#96;nsmax_total ≈ 2–3 × nsmax&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2714
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2715
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (float): Maximum search radius for the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2716
          },
          {
            "text": "          step.  Defaults to &#96;&#96;dmax&#96;&#96;.  **Setting this to the covariance",
            "lineNumber": 2717
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlation range is strongly recommended** so that only spatially",
            "lineNumber": 2718
          },
          {
            "text": "          correlated neighbours contribute to the prior.  Ignored when",
            "lineNumber": 2719
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; is &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2720
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2721
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; is",
            "lineNumber": 2722
          },
          {
            "text": "          **determined automatically** from &#96;&#96;dmodel&#96;&#96; and &#96;&#96;Pmodel&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2723
          },
          {
            "text": "          using :func:&#96;_find_effective_range&#96; with the threshold given",
            "lineNumber": 2724
          },
          {
            "text": "          by &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96;.  This ensures the MCP ring radius",
            "lineNumber": 2725
          },
          {
            "text": "          equals the effective decorrelation distance in the bivariate",
            "lineNumber": 2726
          },
          {
            "text": "          model, preventing out-of-range data from contaminating the",
            "lineNumber": 2727
          },
          {
            "text": "          MCP prior.  Default &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2728
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2729
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'auto_dmax_threshold'&#96;&#96; (float): Decorrelation threshold",
            "lineNumber": 2730
          },
          {
            "text": "          for the automatic range detection.  The range is the distance",
            "lineNumber": 2731
          },
          {
            "text": "          at which the normalised total variation between &#96;&#96;Pmodel&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2732
          },
          {
            "text": "          the independence product &#96;&#96;p(c)*p(c')&#96;&#96; drops below this",
            "lineNumber": 2733
          },
          {
            "text": "          fraction.  Default &#96;&#96;0.05&#96;&#96; (5 %).",
            "lineNumber": 2734
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2735
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'use_annular_mcp'&#96;&#96; (bool): If &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96; (default), the MCP",
            "lineNumber": 2736
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior is computed using only data in the **ring**",
            "lineNumber": 2737
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;dmax &lt; r &lt;= dmax_mcp&#96;&#96;, i.e. data that lie *outside* the local",
            "lineNumber": 2738
          },
          {
            "text": "          BME update zone.  This gives strict data independence between the",
            "lineNumber": 2739
          },
          {
            "text": "          prior step and the likelihood step (no data leakage).  If",
            "lineNumber": 2740
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96;, MCP uses all data within &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp&#96;&#96; (original",
            "lineNumber": 2741
          },
          {
            "text": "          behaviour, slightly faster but reuses data).",
            "lineNumber": 2742
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2743
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'global_marginal'&#96;&#96; (np.ndarray, shape &#96;&#96;(nc,)&#96;&#96;): Empirical",
            "lineNumber": 2744
          },
          {
            "text": "          category frequencies &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96;.  When provided, the MCP prior",
            "lineNumber": 2745
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; is passed to BMEcatPdf together with &#96;&#96;global_marginal&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2746
          },
          {
            "text": "          so that the Bayes-factor correction &#96;&#96;q(c)/p(c)&#96;&#96; is applied",
            "lineNumber": 2747
          },
          {
            "text": "          automatically, preventing double-counting of the global",
            "lineNumber": 2748
          },
          {
            "text": "          marginal.  If not provided, &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; is estimated automatically",
            "lineNumber": 2749
          },
          {
            "text": "          from &#96;&#96;ps.mean(axis=0)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2750
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2751
          },
          {
            "text": "        - All other options (e.g., &#96;&#96;'tol'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'reg'&#96;&#96;, &#96;&#96;'estimator'&#96;&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 2752
          },
          {
            "text": "          are forwarded to the final &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; update step.",
            "lineNumber": 2753
          },
          {
            "text": "        - &#96;&#96;'model_structure'&#96;&#96; is *ignored* for the BME step and forced to",
            "lineNumber": 2754
          },
          {
            "text": "          &#96;&#96;'full'&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2755
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2756
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 2757
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 2758
          },
          {
            "text": "    pk : np.ndarray",
            "lineNumber": 2759
          },
          {
            "text": "        The estimated posterior marginal PDFs, shape &#96;&#96;(nk, nc)&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 2760
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2761
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 2762
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 2763
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Choosing nsmax_total and dmax_mcp:**",
            "lineNumber": 2764
          },
          {
            "text": "    Let r be the covariance correlation range.  Set &#96;&#96;dmax_mcp ≈ r&#96;&#96; and",
            "lineNumber": 2765
          },
          {
            "text": "    choose &#96;&#96;nsmax_total&#96;&#96; as the expected number of data points within that",
            "lineNumber": 2766
          },
          {
            "text": "    radius (typically 10–25 for datasets of 50–200 points).  Using too many",
            "lineNumber": 2767
          },
          {
            "text": "    decorrelated neighbours (beyond r) causes the MCP prior to converge to",
            "lineNumber": 2768
          },
          {
            "text": "    the global marginal P(c) at every location, destroying spatial variation.",
            "lineNumber": 2769
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2770
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Bayes-factor correction:**",
            "lineNumber": 2771
          },
          {
            "text": "    The Maximum Entropy table solved by &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96; carries an implicit",
            "lineNumber": 2772
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; weight (the global marginal).  Passing the MCP result &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2773
          },
          {
            "text": "    directly as a prior therefore weights the final posterior by",
            "lineNumber": 2774
          },
          {
            "text": "    &#96;&#96;q(c) · p(c)&#96;&#96; rather than &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96; alone — a subtle double-counting",
            "lineNumber": 2775
          },
          {
            "text": "    of the baseline frequency.  The Bayes-factor correction divides the",
            "lineNumber": 2776
          },
          {
            "text": "    supplied prior by &#96;&#96;p(c)&#96;&#96; before entering &#96;&#96;producttablepdf&#96;&#96;, so the",
            "lineNumber": 2777
          },
          {
            "text": "    net effect is exactly &#96;&#96;q(c)&#96;&#96;.  When no prior is given this correction",
            "lineNumber": 2778
          },
          {
            "text": "    is never triggered and the original BME behaviour is preserved.",
            "lineNumber": 2779
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 2780
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 2781
          },
          {
            "text": "    # --- 1. Setup Options ---",
            "lineNumber": 2782
          },
          {
            "text": "    if options is None:",
            "lineNumber": 2783
          },
          {
            "text": "        options = {}",
            "lineNumber": 2784
          }
        ]
      },

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def isotropy_test_categorical(coord, value, coord_limit, angLag, angTol,",
            "lineNumber": 1231,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                               class_weights=None,",
            "lineNumber": 1232,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                               n_boot=199, alpha=0.05, seed=None,",
            "lineNumber": 1233,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                               chunk_size=None):",
            "lineNumber": 1234,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "\"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1306
          },
          {
            "text": "    coord  = np.asarray(coord,  dtype=float)",
            "lineNumber": 1307
          },
          {
            "text": "    value  = np.asarray(value,  dtype=float)",
            "lineNumber": 1308
          },
          {
            "text": "    angLag = np.asarray(angLag, dtype=float)",
            "lineNumber": 1309
          },
          {
            "text": "    angTol = np.asarray(angTol, dtype=float)",
            "lineNumber": 1310
          },
          {
            "text": "    rng    = np.random.default_rng(seed)",
            "lineNumber": 1311
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1312
          },
          {
            "text": "    _p_marginal_iso = value.mean(axis=0)   # fixed across bootstrap rotations",
            "lineNumber": 1313
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1314
          },
          {
            "text": "    def _compute_T(gs):",
            "lineNumber": 1315
          },
          {
            "text": "        \"\"\"Compute test statistic from coordinates &#96;&#96;gs&#96;&#96;.\"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 1316
          },
          {
            "text": "        PP, OO, DD, _ = polar_ptable_map(",
            "lineNumber": 1317
          },
          {
            "text": "            gs, value, coord_limit,",
            "lineNumber": 1318
          },
          {
            "text": "            rLag    = np.array([]),   # rLag unused when plot=False",
            "lineNumber": 1319
          },
          {
            "text": "            rLagTol = np.array([]),",
            "lineNumber": 1320
          },
          {
            "text": "            angLag=angLag, angTol=angTol,",
            "lineNumber": 1321
          },
          {
            "text": "            chunk_size=chunk_size, plot=False,",
            "lineNumber": 1322
          },
          {
            "text": "        )",
            "lineNumber": 1323
          },
          {
            "text": "        theta, r, a_max, a_dirs, _, valid = estimate_anisotropy_from_ptables(",
            "lineNumber": 1324
          },
          {
            "text": "            DD, PP, OO, angLag,",
            "lineNumber": 1325
          },
          {
            "text": "            class_weights=class_weights,",
            "lineNumber": 1326
          },
          {
            "text": "            p_marginal=_p_marginal_iso,",
            "lineNumber": 1327
          },
          {
            "text": "        )",
            "lineNumber": 1328
          },
          {
            "text": "        if valid.sum() &lt; 2:",
            "lineNumber": 1329
          },
          {
            "text": "            return np.nan, theta, r, a_max, a_dirs",
            "lineNumber": 1330
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1331
          },
          {
            "text": "        # T_n = range(principal) - range(secondary)",
            "lineNumber": 1332
          },
          {
            "text": "        phi2 = theta + np.pi / 2",
            "lineNumber": 1333
          },
          {
            "text": "        if phi2 &gt; np.pi / 2:",
            "lineNumber": 1334
          },
          {
            "text": "            phi2 -= np.pi",
            "lineNumber": 1335
          },
          {
            "text": "        idx1 = int(np.argmin(np.abs(angLag - theta)))",
            "lineNumber": 1336
          },
          {
            "text": "        idx2 = int(np.argmin(np.abs(angLag - phi2)))",
            "lineNumber": 1337
          },
          {
            "text": "        a1 = float(a_dirs[idx1]) if not np.isnan(a_dirs[idx1]) else 0.0",
            "lineNumber": 1338
          },
          {
            "text": "        a2 = float(a_dirs[idx2]) if not np.isnan(a_dirs[idx2]) else 0.0",
            "lineNumber": 1339
          },
          {
            "text": "        return float(a1 - a2), theta, r, a_max, a_dirs",
            "lineNumber": 1340
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1341
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Observed statistic",
            "lineNumber": 1342
          },
          {
            "text": "    T_obs, theta_hat, r_hat, a_max_hat, a_dirs_obs = _compute_T(coord)",
            "lineNumber": 1343
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1344
          },
          {
            "text": "    # Bootstrap null distribution",
            "lineNumber": 1345
          },
          {
            "text": "    T_boot  = np.zeros(n_boot)",
            "lineNumber": 1346
          },
          {
            "text": "    center  = coord.mean(axis=0)",
            "lineNumber": 1347
          },
          {
            "text": "    for b in range(n_boot):",
            "lineNumber": 1348
          },
          {
            "text": "        angle_b      = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)",
            "lineNumber": 1349
          },
          {
            "text": "        cos_a, sin_a = np.cos(angle_b), np.sin(angle_b)",
            "lineNumber": 1350
          },
          {
            "text": "        R_b          = np.array([[cos_a, -sin_a], [sin_a, cos_a]])",
            "lineNumber": 1351
          },
          {
            "text": "        gs_rot       = (coord - center).dot(R_b.T) + center",
            "lineNumber": 1352
          },
          {
            "text": "        T_b, *_      = _compute_T(gs_rot)",
            "lineNumber": 1353
          },
          {
            "text": "        T_boot[b]    = T_b if not np.isnan(T_b) else 0.0",
            "lineNumber": 1354
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1355
          },
          {
            "text": "    p_value   = float(np.mean(T_boot &gt;= T_obs)) if not np.isnan(T_obs) else np.nan",
            "lineNumber": 1356
          }
        ]

            "text": "   ",

            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "text": "def stmean( grid_s, grid_t, grid_z, pars=None,kernel='tricube', smooth=True, DataObj = None ):",
            "lineNumber": 39,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Estimates space/time mean values from measurements.",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "text": "    Assuming a separable additive space/time mean trend model, this ",
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "text": "    function calculates the spatial mean component ms and temporal mean ",
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "    component mt of space/time random field grid_z, using measurements at ",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "text": "    fixed measuring  sites n and fixed measuring events m. ",
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "    The spatial mean component ms is obtained by averaging the measurements",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "text": "    at each measuring sites. Then a smoothed spatial mean component mss",
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "    is obtained by applying a specified spatial filter to ms.",
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "text": "    Similarly mt is obtained by averaging the measurement for each",
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "text": "    measuring event, and a smoothed temporal mean component mts is obtained",
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "text": "    by applying the same function of temporal filter to mt.",
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {
            "text": "    Args:",
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "        grid_s (ndarray): shape of (n, 2).",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "text": "            Data point coordinates.",
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "        grid_t (ndarray): shape of (m, 1).",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "text": "            Data point timestamps.",
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "        grid_z (ndarray): shape of (n, m).",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "text": "            Matrix of measurements at the n monitoring sites and m measuring events. ",
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {
            "text": "            grid_z may have NaN values.",
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "text": "        pars (array_like): Length is 4. Parameters to smooth the spatial and temporal average.",
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "text": "            p[0]=dNeib, distance (radius) of spatial neighborhood",
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "text": "            p[1]=tNeib, time (radius) ofs temporal neighborhood",
            "lineNumber": 65
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "            p[2]=ar, spatial range of kernel smoothing function ",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "            p[3]=at, temporal range of kernel smoothing function",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "        kernel (str): {'exp', 'tricube', 'bicube'}. Specified kernel function for smoothing.",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "text": "        smooth (bool): Whether to smooth the spa-temporal mean by given kernel function.",
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "        DataObj (bool): GUI for STAR-BME.",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns:",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "text": "        mean_s (ndarray): shape of (n, 1). vector of spatial average",
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "        mss (ndarray): shape of  (n, 1). The vector of smoothed spatial average",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "        mean_t (ndarray): shape of (1, m). vector of temporal average",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "        mts (ndarray): shape of (1, m). vector of smoothed temporal average ",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "        STmean (ndarray):shape of (n, m). Estimated spa-temporal mean.",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "    Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "        Randomly sampling 30 points in 20000x20000 fields and suppose there are 24 measurement events.",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "        &gt;&gt;&gt; grid_s = np.random.random_sample((30,2))*20000",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "        &gt;&gt;&gt; grid_t = np.arange(1,25)",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "        Randomly sampling 36 measuring events of each point.",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "text": "        &gt;&gt;&gt; grid_z = np.random.random_sample((30,24))+np.random.random_sample((30,1))*10",
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "        ",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "        Define the smoothing parameters of kernel.",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "        &gt;&gt;&gt; dNeib,tNeib,ar,at = 5000,5,5000,5",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "text": "        &gt;&gt;&gt; pars = [dNeib,tNeib,ar,at]",
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "        ",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "text": "        Calculate the spa-temporal mean.",
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "        &gt;&gt;&gt; mean_s,mss,mean_t,mts,STmean = stmean(grid_s = grid_s, grid_t = grid_t,grid_z = grid_z, pars = pars,kernel='tricube',smooth = True)",
            "lineNumber": 94

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "def probatablecalc_directional(coord, value, coord_limit, ang, angtol,",
            "lineNumber": 701,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                                group_ids=None,",
            "lineNumber": 702,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                                normalize_inputs=True,",
            "lineNumber": 703,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "                                chunk_size=None, ShowCalDis=False):",
            "lineNumber": 704,
            "isSignature": true
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"Estimate directional bivariate probability tables for categorical data.",
            "lineNumber": 705
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 706
          },
          {
            "text": "    Extends :func:&#96;probatablecalc&#96; with an azimuthal filter so that only pairs",
            "lineNumber": 707
          },
          {
            "text": "    whose separation vector falls within &#96;&#96;ang ± angtol&#96;&#96; contribute to the",
            "lineNumber": 708
          },
          {
            "text": "    table.  Repeating over a set of directions lets you characterise the",
            "lineNumber": 709
          },
          {
            "text": "    **anisotropy of categorical spatial dependence** purely from the",
            "lineNumber": 710
          },
          {
            "text": "    probability-table structure — no covariance proxy is needed.",
            "lineNumber": 711
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 712
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Soft / probabilistic indicators are fully supported** — see",
            "lineNumber": 713
          },
          {
            "text": "    :func:&#96;probatablecalc&#96; for details on how fractional class-probability",
            "lineNumber": 714
          },
          {
            "text": "    vectors are handled.",
            "lineNumber": 715
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 716
          },
          {
            "text": "    The counting convention is identical to :func:&#96;probatablecalc&#96;: every",
            "lineNumber": 717
          },
          {
            "text": "    ordered pair &#96;&#96;(i → j)&#96;&#96; and its reverse &#96;&#96;(j → i)&#96;&#96; both contribute once,",
            "lineNumber": 718
          },
          {
            "text": "    and pair counts / distances are divided by 2 so the result represents",
            "lineNumber": 719
          },
          {
            "text": "    unique undirected pairs.  Because the azimuth is wrapped to &#96;&#96;(-π/2, π/2]&#96;&#96;,",
            "lineNumber": 720
          },
          {
            "text": "    both orderings of a pair always share the same wrapped angle and are",
            "lineNumber": 721
          },
          {
            "text": "    therefore both accepted or both rejected by the angular filter.",
            "lineNumber": 722
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 723
          },
          {
            "text": "    Parameters",
            "lineNumber": 724
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 725
          },
          {
            "text": "    coord : (n, 2) array",
            "lineNumber": 726
          },
          {
            "text": "        2-D spatial coordinates (X, Y).  Only 2-D coordinates are accepted;",
            "lineNumber": 727
          },
          {
            "text": "        vertical (Z) data should be analysed separately.",
            "lineNumber": 728
          },
          {
            "text": "    value : (n, nc) array-like",
            "lineNumber": 729
          },
          {
            "text": "        Class-indicator matrix — hard (one-hot) *or* soft (probabilistic).",
            "lineNumber": 730
          },
          {
            "text": "        See :func:&#96;probatablecalc&#96; for full description and",
            "lineNumber": 731
          },
          {
            "text": "        :func:&#96;normalize_indicators&#96; for preprocessing utilities.",
            "lineNumber": 732
          },
          {
            "text": "    coord_limit : (ncl,) array",
            "lineNumber": 733
          },
          {
            "text": "        Distance-class limits (same meaning as in :func:&#96;probatablecalc&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 734
          },
          {
            "text": "    ang : float",
            "lineNumber": 735
          },
          {
            "text": "        Target direction in **radians**, in &#96;&#96;(-π/2, π/2]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 736
          },
          {
            "text": "        &#96;&#96;0&#96;&#96; = E–W,  &#96;&#96;π/4&#96;&#96; = NE–SW,  &#96;&#96;π/2&#96;&#96; = N–S.",
            "lineNumber": 737
          },
          {
            "text": "    angtol : float",
            "lineNumber": 738
          },
          {
            "text": "        Half-width of the angular acceptance window in **radians**.",
            "lineNumber": 739
          },
          {
            "text": "    group_ids : (n,) array-like or None, optional",
            "lineNumber": 740
          },
          {
            "text": "        Group labels (e.g. depth level as a string &#96;&#96;wells['Z'].astype(str)&#96;&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 741
          },
          {
            "text": "        When provided, **only pairs within the same group** contribute to the",
            "lineNumber": 742
          },
          {
            "text": "        empirical tables.  This mirrors the &#96;&#96;group_ids&#96;&#96; parameter of",
            "lineNumber": 743
          },
          {
            "text": "        :func:&#96;probatablecalc&#96; and is essential when the horizontal data",
            "lineNumber": 744
          },
          {
            "text": "        contains multiple depth samples per borehole location: passing the",
            "lineNumber": 745
          },
          {
            "text": "        Z-level as the group label ensures that only same-depth pairs",
            "lineNumber": 746
          },
          {
            "text": "        contribute, correctly reflecting within-layer horizontal transitions.",
            "lineNumber": 747
          },
          {
            "text": "    normalize_inputs : bool, optional",
            "lineNumber": 748
          },
          {
            "text": "        Validate and row-normalize *value* via :func:&#96;normalize_indicators&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 749
          },
          {
            "text": "        before computation (default &#96;&#96;True&#96;&#96;).  Set to &#96;&#96;False&#96;&#96; if the",
            "lineNumber": 750
          },
          {
            "text": "        matrix is already validated for performance.",
            "lineNumber": 751
          },
          {
            "text": "    chunk_size : int or None",
            "lineNumber": 752
          },
          {
            "text": "        Memory-control parameter (same as :func:&#96;probatablecalc&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 753
          },
          {
            "text": "    ShowCalDis : bool",
            "lineNumber": 754
          },
          {
            "text": "        Verbose progress output.",
            "lineNumber": 755
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 756
          },
          {
            "text": "    Returns",
            "lineNumber": 757
          },
          {
            "text": "    -------",
            "lineNumber": 758
          },
          {
            "text": "    D : (ncl,) array",
            "lineNumber": 759
          },
          {
            "text": "        Mean separation distance per bin (NaN for empty bins).",
            "lineNumber": 760
          },
          {
            "text": "    P : (nc, nc, ncl) array",
            "lineNumber": 761
          },
          {
            "text": "        Directional transition-probability table.  &#96;&#96;P[a, b, k]&#96;&#96; is the",
            "lineNumber": 762
          },
          {
            "text": "        estimated probability that class &#96;&#96;b&#96;&#96; occurs at separation &#96;&#96;D[k]&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 763
          },
          {
            "text": "        from a location of class &#96;&#96;a&#96;&#96;, averaged over pairs in direction &#96;&#96;ang&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 764
          },
          {
            "text": "    O : (ncl,) array",
            "lineNumber": 765
          },
          {
            "text": "        Number of unique undirected pairs per bin.",
            "lineNumber": 766
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 767
          },
          {
            "text": "    Notes",
            "lineNumber": 768
          },
          {
            "text": "    -----",
            "lineNumber": 769
          },
          {
            "text": "    **Azimuth convention** (matches :func:&#96;stamps.general.diffarray.diffarray&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 770
          },
          {
            "text": "    and :func:&#96;stamps.stats.dependence.stcov.stcov&#96;):",
            "lineNumber": 771
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 772
          },
          {
            "text": "    * Azimuth = &#96;&#96;arctan2(Δy, Δx)&#96;&#96; wrapped to &#96;&#96;(-π/2, π/2]&#96;&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 773
          },
          {
            "text": "    * Opposite directions share the same wrapped angle, so the filter is",
            "lineNumber": 774
          },
          {
            "text": "      automatically symmetric/undirected.",
            "lineNumber": 775
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 776
          },
          {
            "text": "    References",
            "lineNumber": 777
          },
          {
            "text": "    ----------",
            "lineNumber": 778
          },
          {
            "text": "    Carle, S.F. &amp; Fogg, G.E. (1996). Transition probability-based indicator",
            "lineNumber": 779
          },
          {
            "text": "        geostatistics. *Mathematical Geology*, 28(4), 453–476.",
            "lineNumber": 780
          },
          {
            "text": "    \"\"\"",
            "lineNumber": 781
          },
          {
            "text": "    coord       = np.asarray(coord,        dtype=float)",
            "lineNumber": 782
          },
          {
            "text": "    value       = np.asarray(value,        dtype=float)",
            "lineNumber": 783
          }
        ]
      },

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./stamps/stamps/stats/dependence/anisotropy.py",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {

          },

        "signatures": {
          "ranges": [
